_what: Trail, highlight and route links per stop, with the evidence tier for each one.
_why: The trail boxes were built when direct listing URLs could not be found, so half the named trails render as a search magnifier (135 of 265 main-loop items, 129 of 233 extension items). They can be found now. This file is the source; build_links.py injects it into STOPS/EXT_DATA. Editing the consts by hand is silently overwritten by the next build.

_tiers.official: Fetched from the managing authority (state park, NPS, USFS) and confirmed 200 with the expected content type, from this machine.
_tiers.indexed: Returned by web search with a matching title and a review count. The page itself could NOT be loaded — alltrails.com answers 403 to every request from here, so a 403 proves nothing either way. Real, but one tier below official.
_tiers.unlisted: Confirmed to exist by the managing authority, but no AllTrails listing found. Deliberately carries no trail link rather than a search that goes nowhere.

_match.exact: The official trail and the AllTrails listing are the same object.
_match.contains: The AllTrails listing is a longer user-assembled route that includes this official trail. Both are shown; the official name and length stay primary.

_uses: From the managing authority, not inferred. hike | bike | horse.
_cruise: true only where reviews support riding it at cruising pace on gravel tyres: rail-grade or packed surface, no walk sections, no puncture-hazard reports. Bike-legal is not sufficient. Technical singletrack is bike-legal nearly everywhere and is not what this flags.
_dogs: Dog rules per stop, each fetched from the managing authority and quoted. NOT generalised across authorities: the same agency gives opposite answers at neighbouring stops — Mesa Verde allows dogs on Wetherill Mesa and bans them on Chapin Mesa; Point Lobos will not let a dog stay in a parked car while Fort Ord, the other half of the same stop, has marked off-leash segments. 17 main-loop stops are deliberately still empty: the authority publishes no rule and inferring one would be the same error as a constructed URL.

caprock-canyons.note: TPWD: 'All trails are multiuse unless otherwise indicated.' Every named trail here permits hiking, biking and equestrian, so use is an attribute, not a section. The canyon trails are rocky singletrack — bike-legal but not cruising.

biking.name: Caprock Canyons Trailway
biking.official_length: 64 mi, former Fort Worth & Denver rail bed, through the 742-ft Clarity Tunnel
biking.cruise_reason: Ruled out on rider reports, not on paper. Surface is a sand-and-clay mix needing 700x35c minimum; rocky for the ~13 mi from South Plains to Clarity Tunnel; repeated goathead puncture reports; the tunnel itself is sandy and guano-covered and has to be walked. Described as remote and for prepared riders.
biking.reviews_note: No star rating surfaced for this listing in any search result — count only, not an omission in the data entry.

blurb_fix.problem: The activity card says the Trailway is 'a flat, packed-gravel former rail bed'. Riders describe sand and clay, rock, and goatheads. That description reads as an invitation to a casual ride.
blurb_fix.with: former rail bed — sand and clay, rocky in sections, gravel tyres and puncture kit

offroad.distance: not published on the free listing
offroad.difficulty: not published — Trails Offroad paywalls its difficulty scale

Santa Fe NF has repeatedly issued prescribed-burn advisories asking people to stay off FR 604 and FR 607 during burn windows — spring is burn season, so check before driving out.

scenicDrives_patch.name: US-50 through Bighorn Sheep Canyon
scenicDrives_patch.note: The Arkansas River canyon on US-50 between Salida and Parkdale (12 mi west of Canon City). Over 400 bighorn sheep use the cliffs; the pullouts along the river are the viewing. No designated-byway page exists for this stretch, so the Royal Gorge Region tourism board page is the best available source. Truck day-trip, as with every drive.
scenicDrives_patch.season: US-50 is a year-round primary route; no seasonal gate. Arrive 3 Apr 2027 — open, but early-April ice and rockfall are normal in the canyon.

salida-buenavista.dogs: Only one of these has a published rule: Hecla Junction sits in the Arkansas Headwaters Recreation Area, where Colorado Parks and Wildlife lists leashed dogs as permitted — the Forest Service publishes nothing for Waterdog Lakes or Old Monarch Pass, and Salida's code is contradictory (7-5-250 allows a leashed dog in any public space, 7-5-220 calls a dog in an undesignated part of a park a nuisance), so the town and Tenderfoot trails stay unknown.

offroad.name: Big Sandy Road (CR 118) to Big Sandy Trailhead
offroad.distance: roughly 60 miles from Pinedale — US-191 south ~12 mi, WY-353 ~15.5 mi, then Big Sandy–Elkhorn Road / CR 118 gravel to the trailhead
offroad.difficulty: graded gravel, not technical — the obstacle is snow and mud, not terrain
offroad.season: CONFLICTS WITH THE STOP DATES. Bridger-Teton opens Big Sandy Campground and trailhead access only once the snowpack lets the gravel road through — usually somewhere between June and July, closing early September. The stop arrives 24 Apr 2027, six to ten weeks before the road is normally driveable. Plan on the gate or the drifts stopping the truck well short of the trailhead.
offroad.note: Renamed from a verb phrase to the road it actually is. The Big Sandy Opening is the standard gateway to the Bridger Wilderness, which is why it is on the card, but late April is the wrong end of the year for it. Exact opening date varies every year with snow load — the Pinedale Ranger District is the only source that will know.

wind-river.dogs: Bridger-Teton's only dog order is somewhere else entirely — named Jackson Ranger District trails, 1 Dec to 1 May — and neither the Greater Yellowstone wilderness order (GYCC-7) nor any Pinedale Ranger District page says anything about dogs, so all four Wind River routes are unstated rather than confirmed.

offroad.name: Petersville Road
offroad.distance: first 9.4 miles paved; maintained gravel a further ~8.9 miles to the old Forks Roadhouse site at the Collinsville Road junction; primitive road for roughly 14.9 miles beyond that
offroad.difficulty: not published as a grade. 4WD recommended but not mandatory on the primitive section; the maintained portion is ordinary gravel
offroad.season: No formal closure, but conditions are only reliably good July through August — June and September are described as iffy, and snow lingers on the road beyond about mile 14 because of the Alaska Range. The stop arrives 3 Jul 2027, right at the front edge of the usable window. The paved and maintained gravel will be fine; the primitive section past the Forks may still be soft or snow-blocked.
offroad.note: Alaska DNR fact sheet used as the source because onX, which is the fullest listing, is paywalled. Collinsville Road, which branches at the Forks, is only maintained as far as the Peters Creek bridge and becomes a four-wheeler trail shortly after — that is an ATV route, not a truck route. This is Denali-view country on a clear day and mining-claim country the rest of the time; claims are active, so stay on the road.

offroad.name: Dempster Highway to Tombstone Territorial Park
offroad.distance: the Dempster leaves the Klondike Highway 40 km east of Dawson City. Park southern boundary at km 50.5; Tombstone Interpretive Centre and the road-accessible campground at km 71.5 — about a 110 km drive from Dawson, gravel from km 0
offroad.difficulty: not graded. Gravel throughout, surface swinging between dusty-firm and slick mud with the weather
offroad.season: NO CONFLICT, and the timing is deliberate. The Tombstone Interpretive Centre runs daily 9am–5pm from mid-May to about 20 September (2026 season was 16 May – 20 Sep). The stop arrives 30 Aug 2027, inside that window and inside the 25 Aug – 5 Sep tundra colour peak this stop is anchored to. The centre closes roughly three weeks after arrival, so the whole stay is covered.
offroad.note: Only Canadian road that crosses the Arctic Circle, though the Circle is at km 406, far past Tombstone. For the Tombstone day trip you need no ferries and no Eagle Plains fuel stop — those matter only if the drive continues north. Still: carry at least one full-size spare, extra fuel and emergency kit, and expect no cell service, no food and no services past the highway junction. Yukon 511 carries current Dempster road conditions.

dawson-city.dogs: On leash (max 1 m) anywhere in the City of Dawson outside the north-end dog park, so the 9th Ave Trail and the dike are fine; the City names Crocus Bluff Park as a dog-free area but does not say whether the Crocus Bluff trails are inside it, so treat those two as unresolved until the trailhead signs say otherwise; Tombstone's trails on the Dempster are Yukon Parks and allow dogs under physical control.

offroad.name: Salmon Glacier Road (Granduc Road)
offroad.distance: about 25 miles from Hyder at sea level to the Salmon Glacier summit viewpoint, climbing roughly 4,300 ft
offroad.difficulty: not published as a grade. Active mining road — sharp switchbacks, steep drop-offs, no guardrails, loose gravel; high clearance and durable tyres recommended
offroad.season: TIGHT AGAINST THE STOP DATES. The road is not open year-round; the usable window is roughly mid-June to September, and snowbanks can persist even mid-summer. The stop arrives 19 Sep 2027, at the very tail of that window — an early storm can shut the upper road with no notice. Verify locally in Stewart before driving up rather than assuming.
offroad.note: The route crosses back into British Columbia above Hyder, so carry passports for the return through the Canadian border post at Stewart. Fish Creek Wildlife Observation Site is six miles up the same road, with brown and black bears on the salmon from late July into September — that part of the drive is short, paved-adjacent and worth doing even if the upper road is closed. Land-manager coverage is thin: this is a private mining road, so state tourism is the best source found and there is no BLM/USFS/BC Parks page for it.

offroad.name: Titus Canyon Road
offroad.distance: 27 miles, one way westbound, entered from Nevada Highway 374 about two miles east of the park boundary; the last 3 miles at the west end are two-way
offroad.difficulty: not graded by NPS. High-clearance two-wheel drive recommended; 4WD may be needed after storms. Rough, steep and narrow, with the canyon narrows the tightest section. Allow 2–3 hours
offroad.season: RE-VERIFY BEFORE COUNTING ON IT. NPS scheduled a full closure of Titus Canyon Road from 1 October 2026 through at least 30 April 2027 for repairs, after an earlier repair-and-reopen cycle. The stop arrives 28 Dec 2027, eight months past the earliest stated reopening — so on the face of it there is no conflict, but 'at least' is doing real work in that sentence and this road has a recent history of extended closures. Beyond that, NPS says it is often closed for snow, mud or washouts, and December storms are exactly the cause.
offroad.note: Winter is the right season for it — summer travel is not advised and the canyon floods flash. One-way means committing: once past the entrance there is no turning back for 24 miles, the road is infrequently patrolled and there is no cell service. If the through route is closed, the two-way western three miles into the narrows is still driveable in a standard-clearance vehicle and is the best part of the canyon anyway.

not_a_route.problem: A status check, not a route. Nothing to link. Death Valley's road-status page is worth carrying on the stop, but as a note, not as a list item pretending to be a drive.

not_a_trail.problem: Not a trail — a 27-mile ONE-WAY backcountry driving route, east to west, starting from NV-374 two miles east of the park boundary; only the last 3 miles at the west end are two-way. NPS calls it the most popular back-country road in the park and requires two-wheel-drive high clearance as a minimum, with 4WD needed after weather. It belongs in offroad (or scenic drives), not the trails box. 2–3 hours to drive.
not_a_trail.season: SEASONAL — VERIFY BEFORE THE STOP. NPS scheduled a FULL CLOSURE of Titus Canyon Road from 1 October 2026 through at least 30 April 2027 for repairs. Arrive 28 Dec 2027 is after that published window, but the road is also routinely closed by snow, mud and washouts and is prone to flash flooding — never enter with rain threatening. Check park road status on the day.
not_a_trail.note_source: NPS Death Valley Titus Canyon page; Pahrump Valley Times and 8NewsNow reopening/closure reporting

scenicDrives_patch.name: Moro Rock/Crescent Meadow Road spur off Generals Highway
scenicDrives_patch.note: The spur from Giant Forest Museum past Tunnel Log to Moro Rock and Crescent Meadow. Even in summer NPS prohibits single vehicles over 22 ft and ANY vehicle towing — so this was never a coach road, and it is a truck day with the pickup unhitched. In summer it is shuttle-only at weekends and holidays.
scenicDrives_patch.season: SEASONAL CONFLICT ON A HARD-ANCHORED STOP. The Moro Rock/Crescent Meadow Road CLOSES TO VEHICLES as soon as snow accumulates and is not plowed, typically staying shut until around Memorial Day weekend. Arrive 23 Dec 2027 — the Christmas anchor cannot move, so plan on the road being closed to driving. It becomes a marked winter trail for walking, snowshoeing and cross-country skiing from Giant Forest Museum, which is the realistic version of this outing. The Moro Rock stairway is also closed when snow and ice make the exposed granite steps unsafe. Generals Highway between Ash Mountain and Giant Forest is the winter access road and is usually open but closes in storms.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: NPS SEKI vehicle length limits page; NPS 'Crescent Meadow Road winter trail'; SEKI winter trip planners

offroad.name: Nabesna Road
offroad.distance: 42 miles one way, gravel the whole length, from mile 60 of the Tok Cutoff at Slana
offroad.difficulty: not graded by NPS. Most 2WD vehicles manage the first 29 miles; beyond mile 29 the unbridged stream crossings need high clearance and sometimes 4WD
offroad.season: No gate and no published closure, but the crossings are the season. NPS warns that spring run-off and heavy rain can make the streams beyond mile 29 impassable. The stop arrives 25 Jun 2027, which is still late run-off in that valley — the first 29 miles should be fine, the last stretch is a day-of decision.
offroad.note: One of only two roads into Wrangell-St. Elias. Flat tires and washouts are common along the whole length; carry a full-size spare and the means to fit it. The maintained road ends at a private hunting lodge at mile 42, and NPS does not recommend driving the last four miles — deeply rutted and wet. Stop at the Slana Ranger Station at mile 0.5 for current crossing conditions and the free Nabesna Road Guide before committing.

tok-1.dogs: Leashed dogs are fine — the overlook trail is in Eagle Trail State Recreation Site, and Alaska State Parks allow pets throughout on a leash of nine feet or less in developed areas, voice control in the backcountry.

tok-1.dogs_note: Eagle Trail State Recreation Site, Mile 109.5 Tok Cut-Off, is an Alaska State Parks unit; its own page describes 'the 2.5-mile hiking trail with an overview of the Tok River Valley' (https://dnr.alaska.gov/parks/aspunits/northern/eagletrailsrs.htm) but publishes no pet rule of its own, so the statewide rule is what applies.

offroad.distance: about 7 miles from the Glenn Highway to the Alpenglow ski area; the pavement ends as the road starts climbing and the rest is wide gravel
offroad.difficulty: not published. Wide graded gravel with switchbacks — no low range needed, but it is exposed
offroad.season: Open in summer; the ski area itself runs mid-November to late March. The stop arrives 7 Jul 2027, which is the good season — alpine tundra, and late-summer berry picking a little later.

The other half, Eklutna Lake Road, is fully paved for all ten miles from the Glenn Highway to the lake — narrow and winding for the last seven, with no shoulders, but tarmac throughout. It is a scenic drive, not an offroad route, and should move to the scenic-drives box rather than stay here. Arctic Valley Road is the one that actually leaves the pavement.

offroad.name: Dalton Highway — Arctic Circle and Coldfoot
offroad.was_name: Dalton Highway detour to the Arctic Circle / Coldfoot
offroad.distance: the Dalton runs 414 miles from Livengood (84 miles north of Fairbanks) to Deadhorse. Arctic Circle BLM Wayside is at Dalton mile 115.5; Coldfoot at mile 174.8 — call it a 500-mile round trip from Fairbanks to Coldfoot and back
offroad.difficulty: not graded. Mostly gravel, open to ordinary vehicles, but with heavy truck traffic, no shoulders, and long stretches with no fuel or cell coverage
offroad.season: Open year-round — this is a working pipeline haul road, not a seasonal one. The stop arrives 23 Aug 2027, which is fine: the tundra is turning and the worst of the dust season is past, though early snow on Atigun is possible by then (Atigun is well north of Coldfoot and not on this detour).
offroad.note: BLM publishes a free 24-page Dalton Highway Visitor Guide and runs the Arctic Interagency Visitor Center at Coldfoot — pick both up. Carry two full-size spares; windshield damage from passing trucks is routine. This is a two-day out-and-back at minimum if Coldfoot is the turnaround, and a long single day if the Arctic Circle sign is enough.

Tok is a logistics stop; do not consume.entity: Tok, Alaska — the town itself, which the headline names. Matches the two sibling entries on this stop that already use the Tok article.

offroad.name: Nabesna Road
offroad.distance: 42 miles one way, gravel the whole length, from mile 60 of the Tok Cutoff at Slana
offroad.difficulty: not graded by NPS. Most 2WD vehicles manage the first 29 miles; beyond mile 29 the unbridged stream crossings need high clearance and sometimes 4WD
offroad.season: No gate and no published closure. The stop arrives 27 Aug 2027 — the best time of the three Alaska windows for this road: run-off is long past, so the stream crossings beyond mile 29 are at their lowest and the far end is most likely to go. No conflict.
offroad.note: Second bite at Nabesna, and the better one — if the crossings were up in late June on the tok-1 stop, this is the visit to push past mile 29. Flat tires and washouts are still common the whole length. The maintained road ends at a private lodge at mile 42; NPS does not recommend the last four miles, which are deeply rutted and wet. Slana Ranger Station at mile 0.5 has current conditions.

tok-2.dogs: Leashed dogs are fine — the overlook trail is in Eagle Trail State Recreation Site, and Alaska State Parks allow pets throughout on a leash of nine feet or less in developed areas, voice control in the backcountry.
tok-2.dogs_source_quote: Yes, Pets are welcome at state parks and campgrounds if leashed and accompanied by the owner at all times; unleashed dogs are allowed in the backcountry but must be within voice command.
tok-2.dogs_note: Same trail as tok-1. Eagle Trail State Recreation Site, Mile 109.5 Tok Cut-Off, is an Alaska State Parks unit.

Favor a rest day, river walk, museum, or.entity: Generic pacing advice with no single referent — 'a museum' and 'a river walk' are unnamed (the Whitehorse article has no 'museum' mention at all). The city article is already linked from 'Revisit only the Whitehorse attractions missed in June.' on this same stop, so nothing is lost.

whitehorse-2.dogs: On leash everywhere inside Whitehorse city boundaries (Animal Control Bylaw s.53), which covers the Miles Canyon and Yukon River riverfront trails; Fish Lake is outside city limits on Kwanlin Dun settlement and Yukon Crown land, and no authority publishes a dog rule for that trail.
whitehorse-2.dogs_source_quote: Under Section 53 of the Animal Control Bylaw, except in a designated off-leash area, no owner of a dog shall permit such dog to run at large, and where such animal is found running at large, it shall be deemed to be doing so with the consent of the owner.

whitehorse-3.dogs: On leash everywhere inside Whitehorse city boundaries (Animal Control Bylaw s.53), which covers the Miles Canyon and Yukon River riverfront trails; Fish Lake is outside city limits on Kwanlin Dun settlement and Yukon Crown land, and no authority publishes a dog rule for that trail.
whitehorse-3.dogs_source_quote: Under Section 53 of the Animal Control Bylaw, except in a designated off-leash area, no owner of a dog shall permit such dog to run at large, and where such animal is found running at large, it shall be deemed to be doing so with the consent of the owner.

smithers.dogs: Town of Smithers Animal Control and Licencing Bylaw No. 1780 requires leashing in public, which covers the Perimeter Trail and Riverside Park; BC Parks allows leashed pets at Call Lake and in Babine Mountains Park, where dogs are also discouraged from the alpine because of mountain goats; nobody publishes a rule for Crater Lake or Seymour Ridge.
smithers.dogs_source_quote: Leashing when in public and maintaining control of the dog at all times;

Mount Baldy hiking / scenic drive.entity: Mount Baldy / Baldy Mountain Resort, BC

trails.name: Frosty Mountain Trail
trails.was: Frosty Mountain Trail (Manning Park) — no url
trails.note_source: No direct listing url surfaced in search. Name and stop kept; no constructed slug — the fabricated-URL episode is why.

not_a_route.problem: Two things, neither of them an offroad route. Mount Baldy Road (Baldy Ski Hill Road) is the all-weather public access road to Baldy Mountain Resort — partly paved, partly hard-packed dirt, ordinary two-wheel-drive in summer, reached via McKinney Road from Oliver or Canyon Road off Hwy 3 from Osoyoos. That is a scenic drive. The hiking at the resort is trails. Nothing here needs 4x4 and nothing here is a named 4x4 route.

osoyoos.dogs: E.C. Manning Park: "Dogs and other domestic animals must be leashed and are not allowed in most beach areas or park buildings." There is a designated pet area east of the restaurant at Manning Park Resort.
osoyoos.dogs_exception: Frosty Mountain is a long subalpine day out in bear country — legal with the dog on a leash, but BC Parks' general advice against taking pets into the backcountry applies to the upper half of it.

Blue Lake Trail.entity: The Blue Lake trail off SR 20 below Liberty Bell. No article, and no parent documents it: the Washington Pass, Liberty Bell Mountain and Lexington Tower articles contain no 'Blue Lake' text (Lexington Tower's only hit is a compass-neighbour nav box, not documentation).

Goat Peak Lookout.entity: Goat Peak, 7,001 ft, in the North Cascades — the article documents the working USFS fire lookout on the summit, the Methow River valley views and the Forest Road 52 trailhead 1 mile southeast of Mazama, matching this entry exactly. (One of three Washington summits named Goat Peak; this is the Mazama one.)

Grasshopper Pass from Harts Pass.entity: The PCT segment south from Harts Pass. Neither pass has an article — 'Harts Pass', 'Hart's Pass' and 'Harts Pass (Washington)' are all redlinks. The only article containing 'Grasshopper Pass' is Mount Ballard, and only in a photo caption ('seen from PCT at Grasshopper Pass'); Slate Peak mentions Harts Pass Road only as a closure note. Neither documents the pass.

trails.name: Maple Pass Trail
trails.was: Maple Pass Loop — no url
trails.note_source: The larch stop exists for this. Most popular and hardest trail in Winthrop, and the fall colour is why 3 Oct is a frozen date.

trails.was: Cutthroat Lake and Cutthroat Pass via PCT — two entries for one route

trails.was: Grasshopper Pass from Harts Pass — no url
trails.note_source: Harts Pass road is the highest drivable road in Washington and is not coach ground — truck only, and it closes early with snow. No direct listing url surfaced.

not_a_trail.problem: Superseded — folded into the Cutthroat Lake and Cutthroat Pass entry, the single listed route.
The same route as the entry above, under a second name.

offroad.name: Harts Pass Road (FR 5400)
offroad.distance: climbs from Mazama in the Methow Valley to Harts Pass at 6,198 ft — the highest maintained road in Washington
offroad.difficulty: not published as an offroad grade. The Forest Service describes it as narrow and steep with only intermittent turnouts; the exposure, not the surface, is the difficulty
offroad.season: NO CONFLICT, BUT NARROW. The standing Forest Order closes FR 5400 to all motorized wheeled vehicles 1 December to 31 March every year, and snow in practice takes it from late October through to June or early July most years. The stop arrives 3 Oct 2027 — inside the open window, but within weeks of the usual first closing snow. A second, current problem: as of March 2026 Harts Pass Road is closed indefinitely from the Monument Creek Trailhead to the pass after December 2025 flood damage, with the Forest Service aiming to reopen after contractor repairs 'in early summer'. That is 2026 news, not a 2027 forecast, but it needs re-verifying before the trip.
offroad.note: Trailers of any type are prohibited on FR 5400 year-round under a Forest Order in effect since April 2014, with a narrow exemption for snowmobile trailers of 20 ft or less in two spring/autumn windows. Irrelevant here — the truck goes up alone — but it tells you what the road is like. The 3 Oct arrival is set by the larch anchor, and larch and Harts Pass are the same week, so this is the right stop for it if the road is open.

offroad.name: Slate Peak spur
offroad.distance: about 3 miles beyond Harts Pass, ending at the Slate Peak lookout — the highest point a vehicle reaches in Washington
offroad.difficulty: not published
offroad.season: Governed entirely by FR 5400 below it — closed 1 Dec to 31 Mar by the same Forest Order, and snow-blocked well outside those dates most years. The stop arrives 3 Oct 2027; if Harts Pass is open the spur normally is too, but it goes higher and holds snow longer.
offroad.note: No listing found. No separate land-manager page exists for the spur — the Forest Service documents it only as part of the FR 5400 order, and the detailed write-ups are on hiking blogs. Recorded with no URL rather than pointing at something that is not about this road. Ask the Methow Valley Ranger District at 509-996-4003 for the gate position; the final stretch to the lookout is walk-only in some years.

winthrop.authority: USDA Forest Service — Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest
winthrop.dogs: Okanogan-Wenatchee NF: dogs are allowed on most wilderness trails provided they are under control at all times, and the forest recommends leashing. The Blue Lake trailhead page states: "Please keep pets on leash to protect wildlife and pets."
winthrop.dogs_exception: One hard closure on this forest, well away from Winthrop: "Dogs and all pets are prohibited within the Enchantments Permit Area", service animals excepted.

scenicDrives_patch.name: North Cascades Highway (SR-20) over Washington Pass
scenicDrives_patch.note: The through-drive west from Winthrop over Washington Pass and Rainy Pass, with the paved fully-accessible Washington Pass Observation Site looking at Liberty Bell and the Early Winters Spires. WSDOT's own pass page is the live status.
scenicDrives_patch.season: OPEN ON THE DATE, closes soon after. WSDOT shuts SR-20 for the winter between Ross Dam and Early Winters every year — 4 Dec in 2025, typically Nov–Dec, reopening April/May. Arrive 3 Oct 2027: open, and this is the larch-gold week at Washington Pass. Note SR-20 opened LATER than usual in 2026 while repairs continued, so the spring date is not a fixed thing.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: WSDOT pass page; WSDOT 2025 closure release; WSDOT blog Apr 2026

scenicDrives_patch.name: Goat Creek Road (FR 52) to the Goat Peak trailhead
scenicDrives_patch.note: From Winthrop, 9 mi west on SR-20, right before Weeman Bridge onto Goat Creek Road (CR 1163), 3.3 mi, right onto FR 52 for 2.7 mi, then left onto FR 5225. Goat Peak carries a 1923 fire lookout at 7,000 ft, the most visible landmark in the Methow. The walk from the trailhead is 3.6 mi / 1,446 ft, rated hard.
scenicDrives_patch.season: Okanogan-Wenatchee forest roads are seasonally gated and snow-closed in winter. Arrive 3 Oct 2027 — normally still open, but this is the tail of the season at that elevation. Check the forest's current conditions page before driving up.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: USFS Goat Peak Trailhead and Trail #457 pages; WTA

scenicDrives_patch.name: Harts Pass and Slate Peak
scenicDrives_patch.was_name: Harts Pass and Slate Peak (truck only)
scenicDrives_patch.note: Highest road you can drive in Washington. Narrow shelf road with no guardrail; trailers prohibited and it is a truck-only day in any year. Removed '(truck only)' from the name because every drive on this trip is the truck — that belongs in the note, not the title.
scenicDrives_patch.season: THE BIG ONE ON THIS LEG. Two separate problems. (1) Annual: FR 5400 closes for winter, usually 1 Dec. (2) Standing: as of 26 Mar 2026 the road was closed INDEFINITELY from FR 5400-015 (Monument Creek TH) to Harts Pass, from December 2025 rain-and-flood damage plus saturated soils. That closure takes out six trailheads — Robinson, Rattlesnake, Harts Pass, Brown Bear, Slate Pass and Slate Peak — and four campgrounds (Ballard, Riverbend, Harts Pass, Meadows). The Forest Service intended to contract repairs and reopen 'in early summer' 2026, with no date given. Arrive 3 Oct 2027: date is fine, ACCESS IS NOT CONFIRMED. Methow Valley District, 509-996-4000.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: USFS Okanogan-Wenatchee alerts; Methow Valley News, 26 Mar 2026, 'Harts Pass, other Forest Service roads closed indefinitely'

scenicDrives_patch.name: Methow Valley to Twisp and Sun Mountain
scenicDrives_patch.note: Not a designated byway and there is no official route page — it is the valley run south from Winthrop to Twisp plus the climb up to Sun Mountain Lodge, which sits about 1,000 ft above the valley floor and holds the best Cascade view in the Methow. Linked to the state tourism site because nothing more official exists for it; the designated routes in this valley are SR-20 and the wider Cascade Loop, both listed separately.
scenicDrives_patch.season: Valley roads, open year-round. Arrive 3 Oct 2027 — larch and cottonwood colour.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: scenicwa.com (State of Washington Tourism); Sun Mountain Lodge

Skate Creek Road scenic drive (FR 52).entity: Skate Creek Road (FR 52), Gifford Pinchot NF

trails.name: Packwood Lake Trail
trails.was: Packwood Lake Trailhead — a trailhead
trails.note_source: No direct listing url surfaced in search. Name and stop kept; no constructed slug — the fabricated-URL episode is why.

trails.name: Snowgrass Flats and Goat Lake Loop
trails.was: Snowgrass Flat Trail — renamed to the listing's own title
trails.note_source: Seven listed routes reach Snowgrass Flat; this is the classic loop. A 12.4 mi day in the Goat Rocks — arrival is 9-16 Oct, when the high country can already be under snow.

offroad.name: Skate Creek Road (FR 52)
offroad.distance: 23 miles east–west between Packwood and Ashford, joining Hwy 12 to Hwy 706
offroad.difficulty: not published as an offroad grade. Nominally paved, but low-maintenance for years — slumps, potholes and broken edges rather than technical terrain
offroad.season: NO CONFLICT, BUT CLOSE TO THE EDGE. Gifford Pinchot gates FR 52 in winter once snow gets too deep to drive safely, roughly November through April. The stop arrives 9 Oct 2027 — open, with about three to four weeks of margin before the usual gating.
offroad.note: This is the back way to the Nisqually entrance of Mount Rainier and cuts a long detour off the highway route. Being paved it sits on the line between scenic drive and offroad; it is kept here because the surface condition makes it a truck road in practice, and Trails Offroad carries it as a scout route (https://www.trailsoffroad.com/US/washington/scout-routes/670-fs-52-skate-creek). It has been closed outright by landslide in the recent past — check status with Gifford Pinchot rather than assuming it is through.

not_a_route.problem: A thing to check, not a route. There is nothing to link and nothing to drive — it belongs as a note on the stop, or as a reminder attached to the routes it affects.

not_a_route.entry: Snowgrass Flats day hike, Goat Rocks Wilderness
not_a_route.problem: A hike, and one inside designated wilderness where motor vehicles are prohibited outright. Belongs in the trails box. The offroad-relevant part is the forest road to the Berry Patch trailhead, which is a separate entry if it is wanted.

packwood.authority: USDA Forest Service — Gifford Pinchot National Forest
packwood.dogs: Gifford Pinchot NF: dogs must be "on a six-foot leash at all times when in developed recreation areas and on interpretive trails". "There are no leash requirements for most of the forest", though the forest recommends a leash for safety, and "Dogs are NOT allowed to chase game animals."
packwood.dogs_exception: Individual trailheads can carry their own leash requirement — the forest posts it on the trailhead page, so check the specific trail before assuming the off-leash default.

Pets are listed among the items prohibited inside Ape Cave, and the site advises "Please leave your pets safely at home."

forks.authority: National Park Service — Olympic National Park
forks.dogs: Olympic names its pet-friendly routes and closes the rest: "Pets are not permitted on any trails not listed above." The listed trails are Peabody Creek, Madison Falls, Spruce Railroad and July Creek Loop; the listed beaches are "Rialto Beach parking lot to Ellen Creek (1/2 mile)" and the Kalaloch beaches between the Hoh and Quinault Reservations. Leash no longer than 6 feet.
forks.dogs_exception: Rialto is half open: leashed pets may walk from the parking lot to Ellen Creek, about half a mile. Hole-in-the-Wall is a further mile north, past the closure. Hall of Mosses and Sol Duc Falls are closed outright. The nearest pet-legal trail is the Spruce Railroad on Lake Crescent.

scenicDrives_patch.name: La Push Road (SR-110) to Third Beach and La Push
scenicDrives_patch.was_name: La Push Road (SR-110) out to Third Beach/La Push
scenicDrives_patch.note: SR-110 leaves US-101 1.5 mi north of Forks and runs 14 mi west along the Quileute and Sol Duc rivers to La Push. Third Beach parking is on the left at about mile 13; the beach itself is a 1.5 mi walk in through hemlock and spruce to Strawberry Bay. Mora Road branches off it and runs about 5 mi to Rialto Beach.
scenicDrives_patch.season: No seasonal gate — but VERIFY THE MORA BRANCH. In 2026 the park closed Mora Road past Mora Campground to the Rialto Beach parking area from mid-July for storm-damage repairs, expected back 15 Oct 2026. That is a 2026 project, not a 2027 one, and should be clear well before the 25 Oct 2027 arrival; confirm rather than assume. Expect rain in any month — this coast takes over 100 in a year.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: NPS Visiting Mora and Rialto Beach; 2026 Mora Road closure reporting

long-beach.dogs: The Discovery Trail runs into Cape Disappointment State Park, and Washington State Parks lists the park's rule as dogs allowed on leash; the City of Long Beach publishes nothing extra for its half of the trail.

cannon-beach.authority: Oregon State Parks — Ecola State Park
cannon-beach.dogs: Ecola State Park, asked whether pets are allowed: "Yes. Pets must be on a leash not more than six feet long, and kept under physical control at all times." Statewide, pets are allowed in all Oregon state parks except Dabney SRA, Shore Acres SP and named trails at Silver Falls.
cannon-beach.dogs_exception: Snowy-plover beach closures (15 Mar–15 Sep) can shut a beach to pets even on a leash; this stop is outside that window.

No article: 'Catherine Creek' on Wikipedia is a 32-mile creek in NORTHEASTERN OREGON (Grande Ronde valley) and is a different watercourse entirely — rejected on identity. The Columbia River Gorge article's raw text never mentions Catherine Creek.

trails.name: Catherine Creek Arch Loop
trails.season: OPEN, BUT OFF ITS BEST. Low-elevation Gorge oak grassland, walkable year-round. The reason people come is the wildflowers, which peak mid-April through May. Arrive 6 Nov 2027 — bare oak, brown grass, big Gorge views, no flowers.
trails.note: 'Catherine Creek' as written was the recreation area, not a route — it holds several trails. This is the signature one, past a waterfall and up through rocks and oaks to the natural arch. No fee or permit. Dogs allowed on leash; BIKES ARE NOT. Heavy poison oak — long trousers. The paved 1 mi Universal Access Loop is the flat alternative on the other side of Old Highway 8.

trails.season: Open year-round. Arrive 15 Nov 2027 — cold and clear is the good version; the Misery Trail is loose gravel and steps with no shade, and ice on the steps is the November hazard.

trails.name: Todd Lake Loop
trails.season: SEASONAL CONFLICT — LIKELY GATED SHUT. Todd Lake sits about 2.5 mi west of Mount Bachelor, INSIDE the winter closure of the Cascade Lakes Highway. Deschutes County gates the highway between Dutchman Flat and Deschutes Bridge every winter, typically between late October and mid-November — recent published dates are 12, 15, 19 and 21 November. Arrive 15 Nov 2027 sits exactly on that range. The highway does not reopen until mid-May or early June. Assume no vehicle access and check Deschutes County road closures (541-388-6581) before planning a day around it.
trails.note: Easy level loop around an alpine lake with Broken Top and Mount Bachelor above it. If the gate is shut it becomes a snowshoe from the Mt Bachelor Nordic Center.
trails.note_source: Deschutes County road closure notices; USFS Deschutes Todd Lake Day Use Area; AllTrails indexed snippet

Deschutes NF: "Over 95% of the Deschutes National Forest trails are open to dogs off-leash in the summer", but leashes are required on the Three Sisters Wilderness trails "including Todd Lake and Crater Ditch trails" from July 15 to September 15, and at all trailheads and developed recreation sites year-round.

trails.name: Yaquina Head Lighthouse and Cobble Beach Loop
trails.was_name: Cobble Beach / Quarry Cove tide pools
trails.season: TIDE-DEPENDENT, not seasonal. The tidepools are only there at low tide — check the tide chart against the day. Arrive 21 Nov 2027. Harbor seals haul out on the near-shore rocks off both Cobble Beach and Quarry Cove, best seen when the tide is out.
trails.note: BLM's Yaquina Head Outstanding Natural Area, 5 mi north of Newport; entrance fee. A long stairway drops from the observation deck to a beach of smooth black basalt cobbles laid down by Columbia River lava 14 million years ago. DOGS: permitted on the trails and walkways EXCEPT near the lighthouse and IN THE COBBLE BEACH TIDE POOLS. The other tidepool access named in the original entry is the paved, wheelchair-accessible Quarry Cove Trail (1.2 mi, 206 ft — the longest trail in the ONA); no individual AllTrails URL for it was returned by search, so none is recorded.

newport.authority: Bureau of Land Management — Yaquina Head Outstanding Natural Area
newport.dogs: BLM: "Pets may accompany visitors on trails and walkways except near the lighthouse and in the Cobble Beach tide pools", and "must remain on a 6-foot leash at all times". Therapy animals and pets are not allowed inside buildings.
newport.dogs_exception: The tide pools themselves are the one thing at Yaquina Head the dog cannot do — that and the ground near the lighthouse. The rest of the headland's trails and walkways are open on a 6 ft leash.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Otter Crest Loop
scenicDrives_patch.was_name: Otter Crest Loop, a short paved detour off Hwy 101 near Depoe Bay with pullouts at Cape Foulweather and Devil's Punchbowl — check current status, as landslide repairs have periodically restricted the loop.
scenicDrives_patch.note: Short paved detour off US-101 between Depoe Bay and Otter Rock. Otter Crest State Scenic Viewpoint sits 500 ft above the Pacific on Cape Foulweather, named by Cook in 1778, with the 1937 Cape Foulweather gift shop (on the National Register) and a view down to Devil's Punchbowl. Whale watching, and brown pelicans and eagles working the updrafts.
scenicDrives_patch.season: No seasonal gate, but the road's history is the caveat the original entry was pointing at: two landslides in the 1990s destroyed part of the roadway — one dropped a van down the slope — and the stretch was foot-traffic-only behind a concrete barrier for years before reopening in the early 2000s as a ONE-WAY lane with a bike lane. Arrive 21 Nov 2027; confirm current status, storm season is exactly when this road has trouble.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: Oregon Parks and Recreation Department park profile; beachconnection.net Otter Crest Loop history

scenicDrives_patch.name: S-22 Borrego–Salton Seaway (Erosion Road), with the Font's Point spur
scenicDrives_patch.note: TWO DIFFERENT ROADS, and the original entry ran them together. S-22 is the PAVED highway east out of Borrego Springs, nicknamed Erosion Road for the weathered country it crosses — a 21-mile driving tour through the Borrego Badlands with viewpoints, climbing into the Santa Rosa foothills at the east end. Font's Point is the famous overlook, and it is reached by a separate 4-MILE SANDY WASH off S-22: soft, rutted, high-clearance 4WD only, and a standard vehicle will not make it. Pavement in the coach's world, sand in the truck's.
scenicDrives_patch.season: Desert season is roughly October to April; the badlands are unusable in summer heat. Arrive 8 Jan 2028 — ideal. The wash is the hazard, not the calendar: it softens further after rain and this is flash-flood country.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: Visit California Borrego Badlands/Font's Point; DesertUSA Anza-Borrego badlands region; americansouthwest.net

not_a_route.entry: Tumco (Hedges) ghost town, off Ogilby Road

It should move to the points-of-interest box, where the mine history (Hedges, peak ~3,200 residents 1893–1899, renamed Tumco in 1910, abandoned 1911) and the BLM interpretive signage at the parking area are the content. Access from I-8 via S-24 north about 22 mi, then Senator Wash Road. There is a check-in station at Senator Wash.
scenicDrives_patch.season: LTVA permit season runs 15 SEPTEMBER to 15 APRIL — that is when this area exists as a destination and when the winter-visitor population is here. Arrive 14 Jan 2028 — peak of the season, so expect the LTVA busy. Permits: $180 long-term (the full seven months) or $40 for any 14 consecutive days.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Ogilby Road and the Cargo Muchacho mining district
scenicDrives_patch.note: Exit I-8 about 15 mi west of Yuma at Ogilby Road and run north roughly 8 mi; Tumco is signed by BLM. Gold town founded as Hedges, at least 500 people in the 1890s, abandoned 1905, renamed Tumco in 1910 after The United Mines Company. Now BLM land in the Cargo Muchacho Mountains with interpretive signage and a designated parking area. No entry fee. THE TOWNSITE IS CLOSED TO DRIVING — foot travel only past the parking area.
scenicDrives_patch.season: No gate; year-round, but this is open desert with no shade and summer is genuinely dangerous. Arrive 14 Jan 2028 — the right season for it.

scenicDrives_patch.name: US-95 north toward Castle Dome and Kofa
scenicDrives_patch.note: US-95 runs north from Yuma between the Yuma Desert and the Kofa refuge, which begins about 40 mi out on the east side of the highway and covers 665,000 acres. Six entrance roads lead east off the highway — Crystal Hill, Palm Canyon, King Valley, Castle Dome among them; the southernmost, about 40 mi north of Yuma, goes to the southern Castle Dome Mountains. Palm Canyon Road is at MILEPOST 85, then 7 mi of dirt east to the trailhead — Arizona's only native palms, fewer than a hundred left, plus desert bighorn. The refuge was established in 1939 for the bighorn.
scenicDrives_patch.season: No gate. Best season is the cool half of the year; the entrance roads are unmaintained dirt and washboard, and washouts after storms are the constraint. Arrive 18 Jan 2028 — ideal.

offroad.name: Broken Arrow Trail
offroad.distance: about 3.5 miles round trip, Sedona, Red Rock Ranger District, Coconino National Forest
offroad.difficulty: sources genuinely disagree and both are recorded. The Forest Service trail page presents it as moderate with spectacular views; the off-road community rates it hard — slickrock, rock ledges and 'the Steps', with high-clearance 4WD, low range, skid plates and a short wheelbase wanted. Treat it as the harder reading and scout the Steps on foot before committing.
offroad.season: NO CONFLICT. Open year-round; spring is the best of it. The stop arrives 4 Mar 2028 — good weather, but also the start of the busy season on a route already saturated with commercial jeep tours. Go early in the day.
offroad.note: No permit is needed to drive the route, but a Red Rock Pass or an equivalent federal lands pass is required to park at the trailhead. Chicken Point, a wide slickrock overlook, is the usual turnaround and the highlight; Submarine Rock is on the way. Short enough to be a half-day from Camp Verde with the drive up.

offroad.note: No listing found. Coconino NF publishes nothing specific to FR 152 that a search returned, and the detailed accounts are all on hiking blogs and paywalled offroad databases, so this is recorded with no URL rather than a link to something that is really about the hike. Its value is that it cuts the Devil's Bridge hike to about 2 miles round trip instead of the long approach — the road is a way to shorten a walk, not a destination drive. FR 152 is not recommended for pedestrians because of vehicle traffic and dust.

not_a_route.problem: A hike, not an offroad route — 32,000+ reviews on AllTrails as a trail. It belongs in the trails box. What is offroad about it is the access, Dry Creek Road / FR 152, which is now listed separately above.

offroad.name: Cathedral Valley Loop
offroad.distance: 57.6 miles, 6 to 8 hours of slow driving. Most drive it clockwise: Hartnet Road from the Fremont River ford 11.7 miles east of the visitor center, 27.8 miles to Hartnet Junction, then Cathedral Road 29.9 miles back to Highway 24
offroad.difficulty: not graded by NPS, which says high-clearance vehicles can usually manage it without four-wheel drive. That holds only when it is dry — rain or snow can make it impassable to the best high-clearance 4WD
offroad.season: THE FORD IS THE CONFLICT, NOT A GATE. The south end of Hartnet Road fords the Fremont River with no bridge; normally under a foot of water on a rocky bottom, impassable in high water, and NPS says plainly not to attempt it in flood. The stop arrives 28 Mar 2028 — spring runoff and spring storms, the worst combination for that ford, and winter snow can still leave the high sections muddy. There is no seasonal closure to check, only conditions, so this must be phoned in the day before: Capitol Reef visitor center 435-425-3791 (press #1, then #4).
offroad.note: If the ford is up, the loop is not lost — drive Cathedral Road in from the Caineville end as an out-and-back and skip the crossing entirely. That reaches the Cathedrals themselves, which is what people come for. Cell reception is poor to nonexistent on the whole loop, and there is no water; carry recovery gear and tell someone the plan. Rig advice removed from the name per the settled truck-only policy.

torrey.dogs: NPS: "Pets are not permitted on other hiking trails, in public buildings, or in the backcountry." Leash 6 feet or shorter at all times. Pets are allowed "within 50 feet of center line of roads (paved and dirt) open to public vehicle travel", in parking areas, campgrounds, the Chestnut and Doc Inglesby picnic areas and unfenced orchards.
torrey.dogs_exception: Two walkable exceptions the park names: the trail from the visitor center to the Fruita Campground, and the Fremont River Trail from the campground to the south end of Hattie's Field. Hickman Bridge and Cassidy Arch are both closed to pets.

trails.name: Delicate Arch Trail
trails.was: Delicate Arch Trail — no url

trails.name: Mesa Arch Trail
trails.was: Mesa Arch Trail — no url
trails.note_source: Canyonlands Island in the Sky. Sunrise is the famous frame and the crowd is real — the shot list has this stop covered too.

trails.name: Double Arch Trail
trails.was: Double Arch — Windows Section — renamed to the listing's own title
trails.note_source: Arches, Windows Section. Note there is a Double Arch Trail in KENTUCKY with a similar name — this is the Utah listing.

moab.authority: National Park Service — Arches NP and Canyonlands NP
moab.dogs: Arches: pets "are not allowed: on any hiking trails, or anywhere off-trail, even while in a carrier" — leashed pets may go "along established roads or in parking areas" and "in established campgrounds and picnic areas". Canyonlands is stricter still: pets are prohibited "on any hiking trails, or anywhere off-trail, even while in a carrier" and "at any overlooks". Leash 6 feet or less in both parks.
moab.dogs_exception: Mesa Arch is in Canyonlands, where even the overlooks are closed to pets. Arches names Cache Valley Road and Willow Springs Road as places to walk a dog; Delicate Arch, Double Arch and the Windows are not among them.

not_a_trail.problem: Superseded by a researched entry for the same trail under its real listing title.

trails.name: Ouray Perimeter Trail
trails.was: Perimeter Trail — no url

trails.name: Blue Lakes Trail
trails.was: Blue Lakes Trail — no url
trails.note_source: Real and well known, but no direct listing url surfaced. Arrival is 10-15 April, when the Blue Lakes basin is still deep in snow — check before planning around it.

ouray.authority: USDA Forest Service — Grand Mesa, Uncompahgre and Gunnison NFs (Mount Sneffels Wilderness); the Perimeter Trail is City of Ouray
ouray.dogs: Mount Sneffels Wilderness order: dogs are prohibited if "(i) off leash; (ii) not under the direct verbal control of the dog's owner or handler at all times; or (iii) disturbing or damaging wildlife, other animals, people or property". On leash or under verbal control the dog is legal.
ouray.dogs_exception: The Perimeter Trail is a City of Ouray trail, not Forest Service — no municipal rule was sourced, so it is unknown rather than allowed.

Anasazi Heritage Center (Dolores).entity: Canyons of the Ancients Visitor Center and Museum

Petroglyph Point Trail.entity: Mesa Verde's below-the-rim loop to its petroglyph panel. Rejected on identity: 'Petroglyph Point' resolves to Petroglyph Point Archeological Site, which is in Lava Beds National Monument, California -- wrong state, wrong park. Mesa Verde National Park's own text does document this one by name: 'Modern Hopi have interpreted the petroglyphs at Mesa Verde's Petroglyph Point as depictions of various clans of people.'

trails.name: Petroglyph Point Trail
trails.was: Petroglyph Point Trailhead — a trailhead, not a trail
trails.note_source: Mesa Verde. Register at the trailhead; the loop passes a large petroglyph panel.

mancos.authority: National Park Service — Mesa Verde National Park
mancos.dogs: NPS: "Leashed pets are allowed on roads, parking lots, and paved areas on Mesa Top Loop and Park Point but not on trails, in ancestral sites or buildings." Leash 6 ft/1.8 m or shorter; pets may not be tethered or left unattended.
mancos.dogs_exception: Mesa Verde is one of the few parks that opens real trails to dogs, but not on Chapin Mesa: "At Wetherill Mesa, pets are permitted on all trails except for the trails leading into Step House and Long House." Petroglyph Point is a Chapin Mesa trail and is closed to the dog.

Animas River Trail & San Juan Skyway dri.entity: San Juan Skyway Scenic and Historic Byway

Durango & Silverton Narrow Gauge Railroa.entity: Durango and Silverton Narrow Gauge Railroad

links.label: Wikipedia — Durango and Silverton Narrow Gauge Railroad

Durango & Silverton Narrow Gauge Railroa.entity: Durango and Silverton Narrow Gauge Railroad

links.label: Wikipedia — Durango & Silverton Narrow Gauge Railroad

trails.name: Animas River Trail
trails.was: Animas River Trail — no url
trails.note_source: Paved urban river path through Durango — flat, easy and bike-legal.
trails.cruise_reason: A paved, flat 6.2 mi river path rated Easy — the shape that has produced every confirmed cruise on this trip. Paved rather than gravel, so check it suits the dog carrier, but it is the strongest candidate on leg 6.

trails.name: Horse Gulch Trail System
trails.was: Horse Gulch Trail System — a system, not a trail
trails.note_source: Meadow Loop via Horse Gulch Trail is the listed route inside the system. Durango Trails publishes the wider network at durangotrails.org; Horse Gulch Road itself is a 4.1 mi easy non-motorized access route.

durango.dogs: Leashed on both — the City of Durango says leashed dogs are welcome throughout its parks, open space and trails, and a leash is the law inside city limits; voice control applies only on the federal land outside town, not on Horse Gulch.
durango.dogs_source_quote: Leashed dogs are welcome throughout Durango's parks, open space and trails

links.label: Wikipedia — Cumbres and Toltec Scenic Railroad

Cumbres & Toltec Scenic Railroad day tri.entity: Cumbres and Toltec Scenic Railroad; Chama, NM

Reservoir Hill Trail system.entity: The town trail network above Pagosa Springs. Rejected on identity: bare 'Reservoir Hill' resolves to Reservoir Hill, Baltimore, a Maryland neighbourhood. Pagosa Springs, Colorado never mentions Reservoir Hill.

trails.name: Treasure Falls
trails.was: Treasure Falls Trailhead — a trailhead, not a trail
trails.note_source: San Juan National Forest, off US-160 about 15 miles north-east of Pagosa Springs. AllTrails indexes it as a point of interest rather than a trail listing.

trails.name: Piedra River Trail
trails.was: Piedra River Trailhead — a trailhead, not a trail
trails.note_source: USFS lists the full trail between both trailheads at 11.2 mi, easy to strenuous; the AllTrails figure is the common out-and-back. Official page: fs.usda.gov/r02/sanjuan/recreation/trails/piedra-river-trail

pagosa-springs.authority: USDA Forest Service — San Juan National Forest
pagosa-springs.dogs: San Juan NF: "Keep dogs on a leash 6' or shorter" in campgrounds and recreation areas; on wilderness trails dogs must be "under strict leash or voice control". Store dog food in bear-resistant lockers, pack out waste, and keep the dog in the tent or vehicle at night.

official_links.label: Hiking and Camping with Dogs — San Juan NF (USFS)

Walkable historic downtown.entity: Salida's downtown core — the Salida Downtown Historic District, on the National Register since 1984. It has no article of its own; the Salida, Colorado article names and dates the district.

Walk the Colorado Trail out of Angel of.entity: The Colorado Trail where it passes the Angel of Shavano trailhead/campground on the north side of Mount Shavano. 'Angel of Shavano' has no article; the Mount Shavano article documents the Angel of Shavano snow formation the place is named for.

Soak at the Salida Hot Springs Aquatic C.entity: Salida's indoor geothermal pool. The pool itself has no article and the Salida, Colorado article does not mention it (a 'Salida Hot Springs' redirect points there but the text is silent — not used). Its water is piped in from the Poncha Springs hot springs, and the Poncha Springs article documents those springs and the City of Salida's ownership of them.

Pre-runoff wade fishing on the Arkansas.entity: Wading the Arkansas River near Salida before spring runoff. The Arkansas Headwaters Recreation Area is the state park that manages the fishing easements on this reach and is headquartered in Salida.

offroad.name: Aspen Ridge Road (FS 185), east boundary of Browns Canyon
offroad.difficulty: BLM: "High clearance 4x4 vehicles recommended"
offroad.season: Seasonal gate closure 1 Dec – 15 Apr
offroad.note: BLM adds a parking rule that is easy to break by accident: vehicles must remain within one vehicle length of the road when parking. Trails Offroad's listing for the same road (official name "185") gives a high point of 10,301 ft and a typical open window of 30 Apr – 1 Dec, which agrees with the gate dates.

offroad.name: CR 240 above Angel of Shavano to North Fork Reservoir
offroad.distance: 3 mi on CR 240 from US 50 to Angel of Shavano, then 6 mi west to the reservoir
offroad.difficulty: Forest Service: road "is very rough and not recommended for vehicles towing trailers. High clearance vehicles are a requirement"
offroad.season: Campground at the top operates June–September, opening and closing dependent on weather
offroad.note: North Fork is the highest-elevation campground on the Salida Ranger District at 11,000 ft, first come first served, and there is no trash service. Salida Ranger District 719-539-3591 will say how far up CR 240 has melted out.

offroad.name: Fourmile Road / Aspen Ridge
offroad.season: Forest Service: "Seasonal gates are closed December 1 and opened April 30"
offroad.note: The Fourmile Travel Management Area is 100,000 acres of joint Forest Service and BLM land; southern access is from CR 371/375, 304-308, 311, 315, 300-301 and 185. Note the two gate calendars do not match — the Browns Canyon monument roads reopen 15 Apr, the wider Fourmile gates 30 Apr — so an early-May visit is inside both windows but late April is not. The Forest Service publishes no difficulty or vehicle rating for these routes and refers visitors to the Fourmile area map or the Salida Ranger District.

offroad.name: FS Road 1434A, north boundary of Browns Canyon
offroad.season: Seasonal gate closure 1 Dec – 15 Apr
offroad.note: Worth checking before driving out there: the Friends of Browns Canyon access page states that 1434 is "an ATV trail for machines with a maximum width of 50 inches", which a full-size pickup exceeds. BLM's own page calls 1434A an ATV route without giving a width. If the 50-inch limit applies to 1434A as well as 1434, this route is not legally driveable in the truck at all — phone the Salida Ranger District (719-539-3591) rather than assume. Second source: https://brownscanyon.org/plan-your-visit/access-seasonal-closures/

offroad.name: Old Monarch Pass (FS 237)
offroad.difficulty: onX rates it 3 — Easy
offroad.season: onX lists spring, summer and fall
offroad.note: The 52.4 miles is the whole onX route, not the pass crossing — it drops off the west side, crosses Waunita Park and runs north to Pitkin, and onX warns the northern part of that descent is very rocky and rough. The pass itself is 11,375 ft, about 0.6 mi northwest of the US 50 summit, and the graded eastern side is the easy half. Recent status reports on the listing mention downed trees.

offroad.name: Turret Road (FS 184) into Browns Canyon
offroad.difficulty: BLM: "a rugged 4x4 experience into the heart of the Monument"; Friends of Browns Canyon add that "only skilled motorists looking for an extreme 4x4 experience should attempt" it
offroad.season: Seasonal gate closure 1 Dec – 15 Apr
offroad.note: Turret Road ends at a small parking area at the Browns Canyon Wilderness Study Area boundary, where it becomes Turret Trail and mechanised travel stops — so this is an out-and-back, not a through route to the river. The corridor is bighorn sheep, mule deer, lynx and Mexican spotted owl habitat, which is what the winter gate protects. Neither BLM nor the Friends group publishes a mileage. Second source: https://brownscanyon.org/turret-road/

trails.name: River Bench Trail (#6045A), Browns Canyon NM
trails.distance: 5.5 mi round trip to the river

other_links.label: BLM — Browns Canyon National Monument
other_links.note: Managing authority. States 'Roundtrip to the river via the River Bench Trail (#6045A): 5.5 miles, 3 hours'; describes it as the gentle dead-end river-bench route.

other_links.label: Komoot — Turret Trail and River Bench Trail loop
other_links.note: The combined Turret + River Bench loop: 5.4 mi, 558 ft gain, moderate, 2 h 26 min.

other_links.label: Gaia GPS — Ruby Mountain via Turret 6045 and River Bench 6045A
other_links.note: Same combination recorded as a moderate out-and-back.

trails.stats_note: BLM's 5.5 mi is the round trip to the river and is the figure to plan on. AllTrails has no page for #6045A on its own; the 5.4 mi Komoot figure is the Turret+River Bench loop, not this trail alone.

trails.name: Turret Trail (#6045), Browns Canyon NM
trails.distance: 2.7 mi round trip to the river at Little Cottonwood

other_links.label: BLM — Browns Canyon National Monument
other_links.note: Authority: 'Roundtrip to river at Little Cottonwood via Turret Trail (#6045): 2.7 miles, 2 hours'; a steep but short hike with wide views.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Browns Canyon National Monument area
other_links.note: Park-level browse page; source of the 4.5 star / 555 review figure.

trails.stats_note: Distance is BLM's 2.7 mi round trip; the AllTrails rating is for its own 'Turret Trail' listing, which does not publish a matching length in the indexed snippet.

salida-co.dogs: Dogs are fine on the Browns Canyon NM trails (BLM) and on San Isabel NF trails under control; no leash policy is published for the monument and the City of Salida publishes nothing readable for Tenderfoot.
salida-co.dogs_source_quote: Dogs are welcome on most BLM-managed trails. Please check the trail website or call the local BLM field office for specific leash policies.

scenicDrives_patch.name: US Highway 50 over Monarch Pass
scenicDrives_patch.distance: Summit 11,312 ft, about 25 miles west of Salida on US-50
scenicDrives_patch.season: Kept open year-round, but "prone to heavy winter snowfall, often resulting in temporary closures during severe winter storms". Colorado State Patrol: winter driving conditions in the high country run "as early as September and as late as May" — the stop arrives 30 Apr 2028, still inside that band.
scenicDrives_patch.note: No CDOT page dedicated to Monarch Pass exists; repeated searching returned only CDOT's general winter-driving and traction-law pages (codot.gov/travel/winter-driving, codot.gov/travel/winter-driving/tractionlaw) plus third-party cameras. This Wikipedia article was a real search result and was fetched to confirm it resolves. It crosses the Continental Divide between the upper Gunnison basin and the South Arkansas; runaway-truck ramps on both sides and much of the highway three-laned for winter maintenance. A late-April crossing can fall under Colorado's tiered traction law with little notice.

South Main riverwalk.entity: South Main, the new-urbanist riverfront district on the Arkansas in Buena Vista. No article, and the Buena Vista, Colorado article does not mention it. No link.

Cottonwood Hot Springs.entity: Cottonwood Hot Springs Inn & Spa on County Road 306 west of Buena Vista. No article; the Cottonwood Pass article covers the pass road but says nothing about the springs. No link.

Small towns: Nathrop, Granite, Twin Lake.entity: Four settlements up and down the upper Arkansas valley. All four have articles; Twin Lakes needs the Lake County disambiguator, and St. Elmo's article title is spelled 'Saint Elmo'.

links.label: Wikipedia — Twin Lakes, Lake County, Colorado

Soak at Mount Princeton Hot Springs Reso.entity: The resort at the foot of the Chalk Cliffs in Nathrop. It has no article; the Mount Princeton article is about the 14er only and never mentions hot springs, so linking it would send the reader to a peak, not a resort. No link.

Denny Creek trailhead walk.entity: The Denny Creek trailhead on CR 306 into the Collegiate Peaks Wilderness. No article, and the Collegiate Peaks Wilderness article does not name it. No link.

Barbara Whipple trail system straight ou.entity: A town trail network on the east bank of the Arkansas at Buena Vista. No article anywhere. No link.

Ride or walk the Midland Bike Trail.entity: The trail on the old Colorado Midland railroad grade east of Buena Vista. No article; the Colorado Midland Railway article covers the railroad and its grade becoming US 24 but never mentions a rail-trail, so it would not answer the reader's question. No link.

Cottonwood Lake.entity: The small reservoir on Cottonwood Creek south of the CR 306 pass road. No article, and no parent article documents it. No link.

offroad.name: Aspen Ridge
offroad.distance: not published on the free listing
offroad.difficulty: Beginner
offroad.season: Typically open 30 Apr – 1 Dec
offroad.note: Listed under its official road number, 185, and managed by the Salida Ranger District. Rated 4.4 from 47 reviews; high point 10,301 ft. Reviewers report loose rock, washout on the rock climbs and deep ruts, and that the middle section turns to mud after rain or snow — the melt-out date and the driveable date are not the same thing here.

offroad.name: Chinaman Gulch and Carnage Canyon, BLM Fourmile Travel Management Area
offroad.distance: 7.1 mi
offroad.difficulty: Difficult
offroad.season: May through October
offroad.note: FunTreks puts the round trip at about 4 hours with a high point of 8,900 ft, and names the obstacles — Rock Garden, Whale Rock, Double Whammy — most of which have bypasses on the Chinaman side. Carnage Canyon has none of that forgiveness: minimum 35-inch tires, lockers front and rear, and FunTreks tells drivers to carry and use a spill kit. It is one of the most heavily used motorised areas in Colorado, so expect company.

offroad.name: CR 306 west of Collegiate Peaks Campground toward Cottonwood Pass
offroad.season: County: "From November 1st until June 15th this road is not maintained beyond Denny Creek Trailhead"
offroad.note: The road, not the Forest Service, is Chaffee County's — Road and Bridge, 719-539-4591, is who to phone for the plough line. Their published non-maintenance window ends 15 June, later than the tag's "late May"; they aim to open the pass before Memorial Day but only as snowpack allows, and both the Chaffee and Gunnison sides gate independently. Denny Creek Trailhead is the realistic turnaround in mid-May.

offroad.name: Fourmile Area — Natural Bridge
offroad.distance: not published on the free listing
offroad.difficulty: Beginner
offroad.season: Year round
offroad.note: Rated 4.7 from 42 reviews, high point 9,218 ft. The loop runs FS 373 and part of FS 311; surface is mostly sand and smooth dirt with a few mild climbs and only small rocks, which is why it holds a year-round rating while everything above it is gated. The return leg faces the Collegiate Peaks.

offroad.name: Fourmile Travel Management Area general routes
offroad.season: Forest Service: "Seasonal gates are closed December 1 and opened April 30"
offroad.note: 100,000 acres of joint Forest Service and BLM ground. The Forest Service publishes no per-route difficulty and points visitors at the Fourmile area map or the Salida Ranger District instead; the listed uses are hiking, mountain biking, OHV trail and road riding, and ski/snowshoe. Access from the north is via CR 371/375 and CR 304-308.

offroad.name: Mount Antero road (FS 277), off Chalk Creek
offroad.difficulty: Difficult
offroad.season: July–September
offroad.note: FunTreks budgets 6 hours and puts the high point at 13,750 ft. The specific warning is about vehicle size rather than capability: "extremely narrow shelf road with tight switchbacks", and oversize vehicles will have a hard time at the switchbacks — a full-size pickup is the wrong shape for the top of this road even in August. Small SUVs with low range get all but the last half mile. The same road accesses Browns Lake for quiet camping.

offroad.name: Tincup Pass (FS 267) from St. Elmo
offroad.distance: 13 mi
offroad.difficulty: Difficult
offroad.season: July–October
offroad.note: About 2 hours one way, summit 12,154 ft. The blocker is specific and late: one short section of narrow shelf road at 12,000 ft holds snow into early July. Sharp rock near the top is reported to cut tires. Once clear it wants low-range gearing, skid plates and good rubber.

buena-vista-co.dogs: All three are San Isabel NF (Salida Ranger District); the forest permits dogs on its trails and in Collegiate Peaks Wilderness provided they are under control at all times.
buena-vista-co.dogs_source_quote: Pets must be under control at all times. Pets can harass, stress, injure or kill wildlife; introduce disease and disturb fellow hikers. Some wilderness areas require dogs to be leashed at all times.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Mount Princeton Road (CR 162) to Chalk Cliffs
scenicDrives_patch.distance: From Buena Vista, 7 miles south on US-285 then 6 miles west on County Road 162 to the Forest Service information kiosk
scenicDrives_patch.note: Pike-San Isabel NF, Chalk Creek Canyon: "From Buena Vista, Colorado, travel south for about 7 miles on Highway 285. Turn right onto County Road 162, and travel west for 6 miles." The kiosk sits opposite the Colorado Trail (#1776) trailhead. Restriction the authority does publish: "No camping or campfires, except in developed campgrounds" outside the four designated campgrounds, with exceptions near St. Elmo and Hancock. The Forest Service page states no seasonal closure for CR 162 and describes the canyon as "a popular visitor attraction during the summer months". Chaffee County Road & Bridge plows CR 162 through to St. Elmo, so a 7 May arrival should find the graded county road open — the 4x4 passes above St. Elmo are a different question and are not this entry.

Mineral Belt Trail.entity: The 11.6-mile paved loop around Leadville, which has its own article under its full name, Mineral Belt National Recreation Trail.

links.label: Wikipedia — Mineral Belt National Recreation Trail

Leadville historic district.entity: The Leadville Historic District, a National Historic Landmark district covering the town core and 67 mines east of it.

Twin Lakes and the Interlaken ruins.entity: Two things. Twin Lakes, the glacier-carved pair south of Leadville, has an article. The Interlaken resort ruins on the south shore do not, and the Twin Lakes article does not mention them, so only Twin Lakes is linked.

links.label: Wikipedia — Twin Lakes, Lake County, Colorado

Halfmoon Road in the truck.entity: The Halfmoon Creek road southwest of Leadville that serves the Mount Elbert and Mount Massive trailheads. The road has no article; the Mount Elbert article documents the Halfmoon Creek trailheads it exists to reach.

offroad.name: FS Road 125.B, South Mount Elbert trailhead extension
offroad.distance: 1.8 mi
offroad.difficulty: Forest Service: four-wheel drive only, summer season; impassable to vehicles in winter
offroad.season: Summer only
offroad.note: The trail it serves, South Mount Elbert #1481, is 5.8 mi with 4,800 ft of gain from the lower trailhead. The road starts just beyond the lower parking lot; there is a ford about 1.5 mi up, and informal dispersed sites line the first mile if you would rather park and walk. Access is from Leadville: 15 mi south on US 24, west 3.75 mi on CO 82, then right on Lake CR 24 for 1.5 mi.

offroad.name: Hagerman Pass (FS 105), 11,925 ft
offroad.distance: 5 mi west from Leadville on Lake CR 4, then 5.5 mi on FS 105 to the summit
offroad.difficulty: Forest Service: road is "very rough"; "high-clearance, four-wheel drive vehicles are recommended"
offroad.note: The Forest Service page publishes no open or close dates at all for this pass — the seasonal timing in the tag is not theirs and should be checked with the Leadville Ranger District. The 1880s railroad history is the reason the grade exists; west of the summit it continues through White River National Forest past Ruedi Reservoir to CO 82 at Basalt.

offroad.name: Hagerman Pass Road (Road 105)
offroad.distance: 5 mi west from Leadville on Lake CR 4, then 5.5 mi on FS 105 to the summit
offroad.difficulty: Forest Service: road is "very rough"; "high-clearance, four-wheel drive vehicles are recommended"
offroad.note: Same road as the Hagerman Pass entry above — one route, listed twice in this box. The Forest Service publishes no seasonal dates for it.

offroad.name: Halfmoon Road (FS 110) to Elbert Creek and the Mount Massive trailhead
offroad.difficulty: not rated by the Forest Service on this page
offroad.note: The authority page confirms the road and what it reaches — FS 110 follows the southern border of the Mount Massive Wilderness and serves several campgrounds plus the Mount Massive and North Elbert trailheads — but publishes no surface, mileage or vehicle guidance. The Forest's own trail pages add that the road is not maintained in winter and that the last half mile to the trailhead needs high clearance and 4WD. Very busy in summer.

offroad.name: Mosquito Pass (FS 438)
offroad.distance: 9.5 mi
offroad.difficulty: Forest Service: "moderate to difficult, steep and very rocky"
offroad.season: Forest Service: "usually only open for six to eight weeks after the snow melts in July"
offroad.note: The Forest Service signs and numbers this as County Road 12, not 438 — worth knowing at the junction. The tour starts from Fairplay: north on CO 9 for about 4.2 mi, then left onto CR 12, and the interpretive stops begin almost immediately. The brochure is a download from this page as well as a paper copy at the South Park Ranger District.

offroad.name: Mosquito Pass Road
offroad.distance: 9.5 mi
offroad.difficulty: Forest Service: "moderate to difficult, steep and very rocky"
offroad.season: Forest Service: "usually only open for six to eight weeks after the snow melts in July"
offroad.note: Same road as the Mosquito Pass (FS 438) entry above — one route, listed twice in this box. Signed as County Road 12 from the Fairplay side.

leadville-co.dogs: All four are San Isabel NF (Leadville Ranger District); dogs are permitted on forest trails and in Mount Massive Wilderness under control, with a 6-ft leash in developed sites such as the Turquoise Lake campgrounds.
leadville-co.dogs_source_quote: Pets must be under control at all times. Pets can harass, stress, injure or kill wildlife; introduce disease and disturb fellow hikers. Some wilderness areas require dogs to be leashed at all times.

Green River Lakes day trip.entity: The two headwater lakes of the Green River at the north end of the Wind River Range. They have no article of their own. The Squaretop Mountain article documents them directly ('the iconic view of Squaretop and Green River Lakes'), and the Green River article documents the river's headwaters in northern Sublette County in the Wind Rivers.

Scout the alpine trailheads.entity: Advice for the stay rather than a named place — no entity to link. No link.

Skyline Drive up to Elkhart Park.entity: The Pinedale road up to the Elkhart Park trailhead. Neither the road nor the park has an article; the Wind River Range article documents the Elkhart Park Trailhead as the main access to Titcomb Basin.

Photographer's Point via the Pole Creek.entity: The overlook about 4.5 miles up the Pole Creek Trail from Elkhart Park. Neither it nor the trail has an article, and neither the Bridger Wilderness nor the Wind River Range article names either. No link.

Green River Lakes and Squaretop Mountain.entity: Squaretop Mountain, the flat-topped peak above the Green River Lakes, has its own article and it documents the pairing with the lakes. The lakes themselves are covered via the Green River's headwaters.

CCC Ponds wildlife walk.entity: The Wyoming Game and Fish ponds just outside Pinedale. No article, and the Pinedale article does not mention them. No link.

Fremont Lake and Half Moon Lake.entity: Two lakes northeast of Pinedale. Fremont Lake — Wyoming's second-largest natural lake, in the Wind River foothills — has an article. Half Moon Lake does not, and the Pinedale article does not mention it, so only Fremont Lake is linked.

Soda Lake Wildlife Habitat Management Ar.entity: A Wyoming Game and Fish WHMA north of Pinedale. No article under that or any nearby title, and no parent article documents it. No link.

offroad.name: Boulder Lake Road (CR 125 to FS 370780)
offroad.distance: about 24 mi from Pinedale, roughly 10 mi of it dirt and gravel
offroad.note: The Forest's own directions match the tag turn for turn, and add that the dirt and gravel section is simply bumpy rather than technical — no 4WD language anywhere on the page, which is what makes this the sane shakedown day. The campground at the end has 15 sites on the east end of the lake near Boulder Creek.

offroad.name: Green River Lakes Road (FS 370650)
offroad.distance: 25 mi paved on WY 352 to the forest boundary, then 18 mi of dirt — about 50 mi from Pinedale
offroad.difficulty: "While the dirt road to the campground is suitable for 2 wheel drive vehicles, weather can make this road impassable to all but 4 wheel drive vehicles"
offroad.note: One thing to check before the trip rather than at the junction: the Bridger-Teton began a major reconstruction of this road in July 2026 — grading, drainage, culverts and new aggregate — with Phase 2 from the Union Pass Y to Green River Lakes scheduled for Aug–Oct 2026 or summer 2027. It should be finished and in better shape by 2028, but the Forest's conditions page is where any carryover work would be posted: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r04/bridger-teton/conditions/green-river-lakes-road-construction-updates . Lower Green River Lake sits at 8,000 ft; drinking water at the campground only 1 Jul – 15 Sep.

offroad.name: New Fork Lake access (FS 370730 / 370735)
offroad.distance: about 24 mi from Pinedale — 6 mi US 191, 14.4 mi WY 352, 3 mi CR 162, then under a mile on FS 370730
offroad.note: Shorter and less committing than the tag implies — the forest road portion is under a mile, with the 3 mi of county road before it. The Forest publishes no road-surface warning, no high-clearance requirement and no seasonal date for this approach; the only figures on the page are the distances above. Third-party sites describe the last stretch as rocky, but that is not the Forest's wording and is not sourced here.

offroad.name: Union Pass Road (FS 370600)
offroad.note: This is the Forest's own road-conditions page and it is the only official page that names NFSR 600 by number: Union Pass Road runs from the forest boundary to the Green River Lakes Road (NFSR 650) junction, the "Union Pass Y". Phase 1 reconstruction covered exactly that segment in July 2026 with 30-minute delays and one full closure day; work may carry into 2027, so check this page before driving it. The Forest publishes no mileage, difficulty or open date for the road — the Pinedale Ranger District (307-367-4326) and the MVUM are the authority for what is open. The 70-plus-mile Dubois-to-Pinedale figure that circulates online is not a Forest Service number and should not be relied on.

trails.name: Elkhart Park — Photographer's Point

alltrails.name: Photographers Point via Pole Creek Trail

other_links.label: Hiking Project — Photographers Point
other_links.note: Starts at Elkhart Park trailhead on the Pole Creek Trail, ~4.5 mi of sub-alpine forest climbing; about 4 hours round trip.

trails.stats_note: Our entry names the trailhead; AllTrails indexes the hike itself under the Pole Creek Trail. Takes about 4-4.5 hr.

trails.name: Green River Lakes / Highline Trail

alltrails.name: Green River Lakes to Summit Lake via Highline Trail

other_links.label: AllTrails — Green River Lakes Loop
