other_links.note: The realistic day option instead of the full Highline: shores of Upper and Lower Green River Lakes, 4.8 stars from 460 reviews.

other_links.label: USFS — Hike the Highline Trail
other_links.note: Forest Service page for the Highline; notes the west-side lakeshore trail is less well marked than the official east-side trail.

trails.stats_note: 35.8 mi / 4,009 ft is a 14.5-16 hr backpack, not a day walk from camp — the Green River Lakes Loop link is the one worth planning around.

trails.name: Sinks Canyon (Popo Agie Falls)

other_links.label: Hiking Project — Popo Agie Falls
other_links.note: Trailhead is Bruce's Parking Area on Shoshone National Forest land, 3 miles up the road from the Sinks Canyon State Park visitor center.

other_links.label: Trailforks — Popo Agie Falls Trail
other_links.note: Confirms the falls-overlook route and its high viewpoint.

trails.stats_note: No distance or difficulty could be sourced from the indexed snippet, so none is recorded. Note the trail leaves from Shoshone NF, not from inside the state park.

wind-river-ext.dogs: Dogs are welcome on all three: Sinks Canyon State Park requires a leash of 10 ft or less, and the only dog order Bridger-Teton publishes is a winter leash rule on the Jackson district, which does not touch Pinedale or these late-May dates.
wind-river-ext.dogs_source_quote: The Forest Order requires all dogs to be leashed with a tether no longer than six feet, from Dec. 1 to May 1, on designated trails and parking areas on the Jackson Ranger District of the Bridger‑Teton National Forest.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Green River Lakes Road (FR-091)
scenicDrives_patch.distance: 15.6 miles of unpaved road from the Union Pass Road fork to Green River Lake Campground
scenicDrives_patch.season: SEASON CONFLICT — the campground at the end of the road opens July 1 and runs to September 15; the stop arrives 21 May 2028, six weeks early.
scenicDrives_patch.note: Bridger-Teton NF, Pinedale Ranger District. Two things worth carrying. First, the road number: the Forest Service calls it Green River Lakes Road / FS-370650 (NFSR 650), reached by following WY-352 out of Cora until it becomes Union Pass Road / FS-370600, then bearing right after about 3 miles. The card's "FR-091" is not the number the authority uses. Second, "The access road to the campground is not paved" and the destination is shut on the stop's dates — at 8,000 ft in late May this is snow and mud, not a drive. Also live: the Forest began major reconstruction of the road on 6 July 2026 — grading, drainage, culverts and aggregate surfacing — "with potential for additional work in 2027", and phase-2 windows allowed work between August 1 and October 14 or during summer 2027. Phone the Pinedale Ranger District, (307) 367-4326, before committing a day to it.

Climb the Lake Minatare lighthouse.entity: The 55-foot WPA-era mock lighthouse on Lake Minatare northeast of Scottsbluff, which has its own article.

offroad.name: Robidoux Pass / Carter Canyon gravel loop
offroad.distance: 23 mi as a loop — out on Carter Canyon Road, back on Robidoux Road
offroad.note: No land-management agency publishes this route: the pass is a National Historic Landmark on private and county ground, and the reconstructed 1851 Robidoux trading post in Carter Canyon is run by the Friends of Robidoux Trading Post, not a park service. That means no road-condition page, no seasonal gate and nobody to phone about surface after rain. Access is two miles south of Gering on Hwy 71 then eight miles west. Pioneer graves and wagon ruts are visible along the route; self-guided, no facilities. The Nebraska State Historical Society publishes the history of the pass but nothing about the road, and its page would not load for verification, so it is not linked here.

trails.name: Oregon Trail Pathway

other_links.label: OutsideAtlas — Oregon Trail, Gering NE
other_links.note: Lists it as an easy hiking trail in Gering with map and access detail.

trails.stats_note: The AllTrails listing is titled just 'Oregon Trail'; its own text confirms it by describing the covered wagons at the Scotts Bluff NM administrative building as the start of the Oregon Trail Pathway. No star rating or length could be sourced, so neither is recorded.

trails.name: Prairie View Trail

other_links.label: NPS — Prairie View Trail
other_links.note: Authority: the only trail in Scotts Bluff NM that allows bicycling; best views of Saddle Rock eastbound, Mitchell Pass westbound.

other_links.label: NPS — Bicycling at Scotts Bluff National Monument
other_links.note: Source of the 1.2-mile paved length, visitor center to the monument's eastern boundary.

trails.stats_note: Bike-legal status is the NPS's own statement, not inferred. It connects to Gering's Monument Valley Pathway.

scottsbluff-ne.dogs: Unusually for an NPS unit, Scotts Bluff allows leashed dogs on every hiking trail in the monument — only the visitor center is off limits.
scottsbluff-ne.dogs_source_quote: Leashed pets are permitted on all hiking trails in the monument.

Needles Highway (truck only).entity: The Needles Highway through Custer State Park. It has no separate article; it is the northern 14 miles of South Dakota Highway 87, whose article names it.

Hill City and Deadwood.entity: Two Black Hills towns, each with its own article.

Wildlife Loop Road at first light.entity: The 18-mile wildlife loop through Custer State Park's bison range. The road has no article; the Custer State Park article documents 'the wildlife loop' and the 1,400-head bison herd it exists for.

Needles Highway (SD-87) in the truck.entity: Same road, named with its route number — South Dakota Highway 87.

Iron Mountain Road (US-16A) and the pigt.entity: Iron Mountain Road is a signed portion of U.S. Route 16A, whose article names both the road and its pigtail bridges. The Spiral bridge article has a section on the Black Hills pigtail bridge and credits Cecil Gideon's design for Iron Mountain Road.

Sunday Gulch Trail.entity: The loop that drops out of Sylvan Lake into Sunday Gulch. The trail has no article; the Sylvan Lake (South Dakota) article documents the lake it starts from and the Sunday Gulch Creek the gulch is named for.

Jewel Cave National Monument Scenic Tour.entity: The Scenic Tour, the standard half-mile loop tour at Jewel Cave. The monument's article documents the Scenic Tour by name and its 1972 opening.

offroad.name: Black Hills National Forest Forest Road 307 (FR307) area
offroad.note: No route listing exists for FR 307 — not on Trails Offroad, not on onX, and no Forest Service page names the road. It shows up only as a dispersed-camping area in third-party campsite directories. The Forest's Motor Vehicle Use Map is the only authority for whether FR 307 is open and to what, and it is the document to carry: motorised travel off a designated road is limited to 300 ft for dispersed camping, camp 100 ft from any creek and half a mile from developed sites, 14 days in any 60-day period, and open campfires are prohibited in the South Dakota portion of the forest. The MVUM itself is obtained from the Forest's maps and guides page, free from district offices or online: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/blackhills/maps-guides

offroad.name: Captain Crunch (Johnson Siding, near Rapid City)
offroad.distance: not published on the free listing
offroad.difficulty: 10 out of 10 — Trails Offroad calls it possibly "the most difficult, rock-crawling trail in South Dakota"
offroad.note: Filed as a scout route rather than a full trail guide, and rated 5/5 from a single review, so the listing is thin. It is in the "Cereal Bowl" area off Bogus Jim Road and starts where the Got Milk? trail starts, which means you can walk in down the smoother north section to spectate without committing the truck. Sedan-sized boulders, v-notches and steep climbs; purpose-built buggies only. Trailer parking at the Cereal Bowl entrance, no camping on the trail.

offroad.name: China Gulch Road, Black Hills NF (Hill City)
offroad.difficulty: Beginner
offroad.season: Typically open 15 May – 15 Dec
offroad.note: Official road number is 249, Mystic Ranger District; rated 4.2 from 14 reviews, high point 5,743 ft, and it is a through route rather than a loop. It starts in China Gulch and runs into the rougher Nugget Gulch area, with the creek crossings concentrated near the northern end — so the easy rating applies to most but not all of the 12.75 miles.

offroad.name: Lightning Creek Road, Black Hills NF (Custer)
offroad.distance: not published on the free listing
offroad.difficulty: Moderate
offroad.season: Year round
offroad.note: Official road number is 288, Hell Canyon Ranger District; rated 3.7 from 4 reviews, high point 6,579 ft, through route. Crazy Horse Memorial is visible from the northern section. Note the grade is Moderate, not easy as the tag suggests — the free listing gives no reason for that, so it is worth reading the full guide or asking the district before committing.

offroad.name: Moses Hill (between Sturgis and Nemo)
offroad.difficulty: not published on the free listing — Trails Offroad describes it as manageable for beginners in the right vehicle but intimidating to look at
offroad.note: Under a mile long, which makes it an add-on rather than a day. It runs off Vanocker Canyon in Lawrence County, is single-vehicle width the whole way over loose rock, and gets slick and genuinely risky in the wet. Short-wheelbase high-clearance with low range is the recommendation; long-wheelbase vehicles need extra clearance for the rock ledges and low-clearance vehicles will hang up. Rated 5/5 from 6 reviews. No camping on the trail itself; dispersed camping on the roads nearby.

trails.name: Lover's Leap Trail

other_links.label: AllTrails — Lovers' Leap (short version)
other_links.note: A separate 2.5 mi out-and-back listing to the overlook only, +531 ft, 4.6 stars from 218 reviews — the shorter option on the same hill.

trails.stats_note: Takes about 2-2.5 hr. AllTrails spells it 'Lovers'' where our card spells it 'Lover's'.

custer-sd.dogs: Custer State Park allows dogs on its trails on a leash of 10 ft or less, and the Black Elk Wilderness beyond the park boundary allows them leashed or under strict voice control — buildings and swim beaches only are closed.
custer-sd.dogs_source_quote: Pets must be on a leash no longer than 10 feet and are not allowed in any park buildings or on designated swim beaches.

Medora's historic downtown.entity: The town of Medora itself, at the South Unit gate.

Drive the full South Unit Scenic Loop.entity: The scenic loop drive in the South Unit of Theodore Roosevelt National Park. The loop has no article; the park's article documents the South Unit and its scenic drive.

Wind Canyon Trail.entity: A short overlook trail on the South Unit loop. No article, and the Theodore Roosevelt National Park article does not name it. No link.

Ridgeline Nature Trail.entity: A self-guided nature trail on the South Unit loop. No article, and not named in the park article. No link.

Coal Vein Trail.entity: The interpretive trail at the burned lignite seam on the South Unit. No article, and not named in the park article. No link.

Painted Canyon Nature Trail.entity: The trail below the Painted Canyon visitor centre on I-94. No article, and 'Painted Canyon' is not mentioned anywhere in the Theodore Roosevelt National Park article. No link.

Chateau de Morès State Historic Site.entity: The Marquis de Morès's 1883 hunting lodge above Medora. The article is titled without the accent, 'Chateau de Mores', and its text documents the surrounding 128-acre state historic site.

offroad.name: Bell Lake Road / FH2 to the Elkhorn Ranch Unit
offroad.distance: from the South Unit: 8.8 mi gravel on CR 11, 6.5 mi Westerheim Road, 11.7 mi Bell Lake Road, then 3 mi on FH 2 to the parking area. From the North Unit it is Black Tail Road/FH 2 for 12.2 mi gravel, then Bell Lake Road for 3 mi and FH 2 for 3 mi.
offroad.difficulty: NPS: the last 3 miles "sometimes needing 4-wheel drive or high-clearance vehicles", particularly in winter or during and after rain showers
offroad.note: Two things NPS flags that matter more than the road itself: there is no cell signal anywhere on the route, and there are no visitor centres or facilities at the unit. Check conditions at a visitor centre before setting out — that is the park's own instruction, not a suggestion. From the parking area a 0.7 mi mowed path leads to the cabin site.

offroad.name: Little Missouri National Grassland section roads
offroad.distance: 1,033,271 acres — the largest national grassland in the country
offroad.note: The official acreage is 1,033,271, slightly above the 1.025 million in the tag. Two districts split it: McKenzie Ranger District in the north, Medora Ranger District in the south — Medora is the one to phone from this stop. The Forest Service publishes no surface guidance, no 2WD/4WD rating and no gumbo warning on this page, so which section roads are open and to what is a Motor Vehicle Use Map question, not something to infer from the map lattice. The 144-mile Maah Daah Hey Trail crosses the same ground, and the page lists 11 campgrounds and 11 OHV road-riding sites.

medora-nd.dogs: All five are inside Theodore Roosevelt NP, which bars dogs from every trail in both units; leashed dogs are limited to roads, road shoulders, parking areas, campgrounds and picnic areas.
medora-nd.dogs_source_quote: While dogs are not permitted on trails within the park, there are nearby trails where you can take your dogs for some exercise.

Knife River Indian Villages National His.entity: Knife River Indian Villages National Historic Site

Missouri River walking paths.entity: The riverside paths in Bismarck–Mandan. The paths have no article; the entity they follow is the Missouri River.

On-A-Slant Indian Village, in camp.entity: The reconstructed Mandan earth-lodge village inside Fort Abraham Lincoln State Park, where the coach is parked. The village has no article; the park's article (titled 'Fort Abraham Lincoln') documents the replica On-A-Slant Indian Village by name.

Custer House and the Commissary.entity: Two reconstructed post buildings at Fort Abraham Lincoln State Park. Neither has an article; the park article names the Custer House and the re-constructed commissary storehouse.

Walk the park's trail network.entity: 'The park' here is Fort Abraham Lincoln State Park, the campground for this stop. The trail network itself is not described in the article, so the link is to the park.

trails.name: Bloody Knife Trail

other_links.label: ND Parks & Recreation — Fort Abraham Lincoln SP trails
other_links.note: Authority: 'Distance: 1.9 miles', 'Open to: hiking, snowshoeing, horseback riding, mountain biking'.

other_links.label: Trailforks — Bloody Knives Loop
other_links.note: Mapped as part of the Fort Abraham Lincoln trail network.

other_links.label: Hiking Project — Bloody Knife's Loop
other_links.note: Graded intermediate.

trails.stats_note: No AllTrails listing; ND Parks & Recreation is the authority confirming it exists, with the length and the permitted uses.

trails.name: Little Soldier Loop

other_links.label: ND Parks & Recreation — Fort Abraham Lincoln SP trails
other_links.note: Authority: 'Distance: 1.8 miles', 'Open to: hiking, snowshoeing, horseback riding, mountain biking'.

other_links.label: Komoot — Little Soldier Loop
other_links.note: Parking at the main park entrance or near the visitor center.

other_links.label: Gaia GPS — Little Soldier Loop
other_links.note: Independently records 1.8 miles, matching the park.

trails.stats_note: No AllTrails listing. Two community sources and the park agree on 1.8 mi.

trails.name: Mato-tope Trail

other_links.label: ND Parks & Recreation — Fort Abraham Lincoln SP trails
other_links.note: Authority: 'Distance: 1.4 miles', 'Open to: hiking, snowshoeing, mountain biking' — no horses on this one, unlike its neighbours.

other_links.label: ND Tourism — Mato-tope Trail
other_links.note: Begins at the confluence of the Missouri and Heart rivers, looping through the campground; named for the Mandan chief Four Bears.

trails.stats_note: Park and AllTrails agree at 1.4 mi. Takes about 0.5-1 hr.

trails.name: Scouts Trail System

other_links.label: ND Parks & Recreation — Fort Abraham Lincoln SP trails
other_links.note: Authority: 'Distance: 8.8 miles', 'Open to: hiking, snowshoeing, horseback riding, mountain biking'. The backbone of the park's ~20 mile non-motorised network.

other_links.label: National Recreation Trails — Scout's Trail
other_links.note: Federally designated National Recreation Trail inside the park.

trails.stats_note: Named as a system rather than a single path, but the park publishes it as one 8.8 mi entity with one set of permitted uses, so it is kept as listed. No AllTrails page.

trails.name: Young Hawk Interpretive Trail

other_links.label: ND Parks & Recreation — Fort Abraham Lincoln SP trails
other_links.note: Authority: 'Distance: 1.1 miles', 'Open to: hiking, snowshoeing, horseback riding, mountain biking'. Vistas over On-A-Slant Village, the Missouri and Heart rivers and Bismarck.

other_links.label: Trailforks — Young Hawk Interpretive Loop
other_links.note: Mapped within the park network.

trails.stats_note: No AllTrails listing; ND Parks & Recreation confirms it with length and uses.

bismarck-nd.dogs: North Dakota's adopted park use rules allow pets on all Fort Abraham Lincoln trails on a leash of six feet or less, personally attended; only buildings, playgrounds, swimming areas and posted areas are closed to them — so the On-a-Slant earthlodges and the blockhouses mean leaving the dog outside.
bismarck-nd.dogs_source_quote: Pets shall be personally attended at all times and shall be effectively restrained by a portable enclosure or a leash not exceeding six feet [1.83 meters] in length.

Itasca's old-growth pine trails.entity: Itasca State Park's remnant old-growth red and white pine. The park article has a section on them ('the Itasca area's old-growth pine forests are almost as famous as the Mississippi headwaters').

Walk across the Mississippi at the headw.entity: The stepping stones where the Mississippi leaves Lake Itasca. Both the lake and the river have articles, and the lake's article is the headwaters itself.

Wilderness Drive (in the pickup).entity: The one-way loop through the park's Wilderness Sanctuary. It has no article; the Itasca State Park article refers to Wilderness Drive by name.

Aiton Heights Fire Tower.entity: The 100-foot lookout tower in the park. No article of its own; the Itasca State Park article documents 'the historic Aiton Heights Fire Tower' and its 100-foot climb.

Bike the paved trail to the headwaters.entity: The park's paved bike path from the campgrounds up to the Mississippi headwaters. The trail itself is not named in any article; the Itasca State Park article documents biking in the park and the headwaters it leads to.

Douglas Lodge and the CCC-era buildings.entity: Douglas Lodge (1905) and the Rustic Style buildings the CCC added. Neither has a separate article; the Itasca State Park article documents Douglas Lodge as the park's oldest surviving building and the Rustic Style group around it.

Hike a piece of the North Country Nation.entity: The North Country Trail, whose article documents the 9.6-mile section through Itasca State Park's southern tier.

trails.name: Aiton Heights Fire Tower Trail

other_links.label: onX — Aiton Heights Fire Tower
other_links.note: Records a 2.2-mile in-and-out to the tower, which was moved to Itasca in 1937 for fire detection.

other_links.label: MN DNR — Itasca summer trails and facilities map (PDF)
other_links.note: Official park trail map.

trails.stats_note: AllTrails indexes it as 'Itasca Fire Tower Trail'; the 2.2 mi figure is onX's, not AllTrails', and no AllTrails length could be sourced.

trails.name: Bohall Trail

other_links.label: MN DNR — Itasca summer trails and facilities map (PDF)
other_links.note: Official park trail map.

trails.stats_note: Averages 17 minutes; good for birding. No star rating could be sourced, so none is recorded (the listing carries 52 reviews).

trails.name: Dr. Roberts Trail

other_links.label: MN DNR — Itasca summer trails and facilities map (PDF)
other_links.note: Official park trail map.

trails.stats_note: The ~1.9 mi comes from a secondary write-up, not from AllTrails or the DNR, so treat it as approximate. Quiet forest walk along Lyendecker Lake and Lake Itasca.

trails.name: Mississippi Headwaters Trail

other_links.label: Explore Minnesota — Mississippi River headwaters at Itasca
other_links.note: Context for the headwaters and the wider Mississippi River Trail.

other_links.label: MN DNR — Itasca State Park
other_links.note: Authority for the park; the walk across the Mississippi at its outlet.

trails.stats_note: Starts at the Mary Gibbs Mississippi Headwaters Center and is mostly flat. No length or difficulty could be sourced from the indexed snippet.

not_a_trail.problem: A roadside old-growth red pine grove and overlook, not a named hiking trail. The MN DNR's own Itasca summer trails map lists it as a stop on the Main Park Drive tour — 'Include stops at Preacher's Grove and Peace Pipe Vista overlooks' — and it is also a stop on the park's paved multi-use bike trail. No trail database carries a listing of this name, and the DNR does not publish a length for it. Worth stopping at; there is no walk to record.

itasca-mn.dogs: Minnesota state parks welcome leashed dogs, and Itasca posts no trail exception — only buildings, lodging and beach areas are closed to them.
itasca-mn.dogs_source_quote: Pets are welcome in Minnesota's state parks, as long as they are kept on a leash six feet or shorter or effectively restrained by a portable enclosure.

Lakewalk.entity: Duluth's waterfront Lakewalk. It has no article; the Duluth, Minnesota article documents its construction along the new Lake Superior beach.

Cross the Jay Cooke swinging bridge.entity: The 1930s CCC suspension footbridge over the St. Louis River. It has no article; the Jay Cooke State Park article documents it at length as the park's most famous landmark.

Enger Tower and Skyline Parkway (in the.entity: Two named things, each with its own article — the stone observation tower on Enger Hill and the 28-mile scenic byway along the Glacial Lake Duluth shoreline.

Hike Jay Cooke's trail network.entity: The trails in Jay Cooke State Park, whose article covers the park and its NRHP-listed Grand Portage trail.

Hawk Ridge.entity: Hawk Ridge, the raptor-migration reserve above Duluth. Its article is titled 'Hawk Ridge, Duluth' (the bare title is not an article).

trails.name: Duluth Lakewalk

other_links.label: City of Duluth — Lakewalk
other_links.note: Authority: nearly eight miles of paved pedestrian and bicycle trail, Canal Park to Brighton Beach (Kitchi Gammi Park).

other_links.label: TrailLink — Duluth Lakewalk
other_links.note: Rail-trail style listing, Canal Park Museum to 26th Ave East & London Rd.

other_links.label: AllTrails — The Lakewalk: Brighton Beach Park
other_links.note: The far north-east section through Brighton Beach Park with rocky shoreline access.

trails.stats_note: Paved and bike-legal per the City of Duluth — the strongest cruising candidate at this stop. Averages 2 h 19 min end to end.

trails.name: Enger Park / Enger Tower Trail

other_links.label: City of Duluth — Enger Park
other_links.note: Authority for the park; Enger Tower was built in 1939, and the park also holds the American-Japanese Peace Bell.

other_links.label: Hiking Project — Enger Park
other_links.note: A 3-mile out-and-back around the viewpoint over Duluth, St. Louis Bay and Lake Superior.

other_links.label: Komoot — Enger Tower
other_links.note: Collects the various short walks and longer routes that reach the tower.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Enger Park area
other_links.note: Park-level browse page. AllTrails' best-rated route here is 'Lift Bridge to Enger Tower via Superior Hiking Trail', 4.2 stars from 158 reviews — a much longer approach than walking up in the park.

trails.stats_note: No AllTrails page for a trail of this name; only a park browse page and a long Superior Hiking Trail approach from the Lift Bridge. Distance and difficulty are therefore not recorded.

trails.name: Hawk Ridge Nature Reserve Trails

alltrails.name: Plantation, Amity Creek, Powerline, Ridge Loop and Hawk Ridge Trail

other_links.label: Hawk Ridge Bird Observatory — trail maps
other_links.note: The managing organisation's own trail maps for the reserve.

other_links.label: Hawk Ridge Bird Observatory — Hawk Ridge Trails
other_links.note: Trail descriptions and current conditions, including leaf-colour reporting.

other_links.label: City of Duluth — Hawk Ridge
other_links.note: 235 acres of undeveloped land on the highest point of eastern Skyline Parkway; established 1972.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Hawk Ridge Nature Reserve area
other_links.note: Park-level browse page; names Ole's Trail, Middle Trail and the Ridge Loop Trail as the connected path along the rocky ledges.

trails.stats_note: This is a network rather than one path, so the AllTrails link is the composite loop that strings its trails together, not an exact-name match. No single length or difficulty applies.

trails.name: Jay Cooke State Park — Swinging Bridge & river gorge trails

other_links.label: MN DNR — Jay Cooke summer trails and facilities map (PDF)
other_links.note: Authority: names the Silver Creek Trail (Hiking Club Trail) as a 3.5-mile loop that crosses the Swinging Bridge and climbs from the river — mowed grass and bare rock, some hills.

other_links.label: The Outbound — Carlton Trail at Jay Cooke
other_links.note: The south-bank river route from the River Inn visitor centre.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Jay Cooke State Park area
other_links.note: Park-level browse page.

trails.stats_note: Our entry covers the bridge plus a cluster of gorge trails rather than one named route, so no single AllTrails page matches. The DNR's 3.5 mi Silver Creek loop is the concrete version of this walk.

duluth-mn.dogs: Every one of these is open to a leashed dog — city ordinance allows dogs on a 6-ft leash in Duluth parks, Hawk Ridge asks for 4 ft or shorter, and the two state parks follow the statewide DNR rule.
duluth-mn.dogs_source_quote: No dogs, cats or other domestic pets shall be allowed to run at large upon any park. Dogs, cats and other domestic pets shall be considered to be at large if they are not under control of the owner or other responsible person by means of a leash of suitable strength not exceeding six feet in length

Devil's Kettle at Judge C. R. Magney Sta.entity: Judge C. R. Magney State Park

Grand Marais harbor and downtown.entity: The town and its double-bay harbour on Lake Superior — both documented in the Grand Marais, Minnesota article.

Drive the Gunflint Trail.entity: The Gunflint Trail, the 57-mile scenic byway from Grand Marais to Saganaga Lake. Its article is filed under its route designation, County State-Aid Highway 12 (Cook County, Minnesota).

links.label: Wikipedia — County State-Aid Highway 12 (Cook County, Minnesota)

Eagle Mountain, Minnesota's high point.entity: Eagle Mountain in the Misquah Hills, at 2,301 ft the highest point in Minnesota. The disambiguated title is needed — a second Eagle Mountain in northern Minnesota is a Lutsen ski hill.

Artist's Point and the breakwater light.entity: Two things. The breakwater light is the Grand Marais Light, first lit 1922, in Cook County, Minnesota — not the Grand Marais light in Michigan. Artist's Point, the rock point beside it, has no article and is not named in the town's article, so only the light is linked.

offroad.name: Forest roads inland from the Caribou Trail (Cook County Rd 4) toward the Sawtooths
offroad.note: The Forest Service treats this ground as four linked signed routes: Beaver Dam, Moose, Maple Leaf and Mountain View Drives. The route-name signs go up only for the fall colour season, so navigation is by map the rest of the year. USFS publishes no mileage, surface or difficulty for any of the four.
offroad.season: Cook County puts spring load restrictions on gravel roads at 5 tons/axle for a minimum of eight weeks, and notes they not uncommonly run past the MnDOT North Frost Zone dates — a useful proxy for when this gravel is soft. Lifted 26 Jun in 2026.

offroad.name: Superior National Forest gravel spurs off the Gunflint Trail
offroad.distance: 57 miles Grand Marais to Trail's End Campground (the byway itself; the spurs are unmeasured)
offroad.note: The Gunflint Trail is paved — the gravel is all in the spurs off it, and USFS publishes no inventory of them. Forest Service wording for this road network generally: single lane with occasional wide turnouts, you may have to back up for oncoming traffic, and logging trucks use them. Gunflint Ranger District office runs 1 May to 30 Sep. Check the forest alerts page before committing to a day out.

trails.name: Artist's Point

other_links.label: North Shore Visitor — Artist's Point & Grand Marais Harbor
other_links.note: Local guide to the point and the cobblestone harbour walk.

trails.stats_note: Two ways out to the lighthouse — over the rocks, or along the concrete break wall, which is narrow and has no barriers or ropes. Worth knowing before taking a dog.

trails.name: Devil's Kettle, Judge C.R. Magney State Park

other_links.label: MN DNR — Judge C.R. Magney State Park
other_links.note: Authority: the popular hike leads upstream along the Brule River to Devil's Kettle, where the river splits around volcanic rock.

other_links.label: MN DNR — Judge C.R. Magney park map (PDF)
other_links.note: Official park map.

other_links.label: North Shore Experiences — Judge C.R. Magney
other_links.note: Puts the hike at 2.5 miles round trip out of the park's 7 miles of trail.

trails.stats_note: The 2.5 mi round trip is a local guide's figure, not AllTrails' or the DNR's. There are a lot of stairs on the river climb.

trails.name: Shovel Point & Palisade Head, Tettegouche State Park

other_links.label: AllTrails — Palisade Head
other_links.note: The other half of our entry, listed separately: 4.5 stars from 483 reviews, panoramic Lake Superior cliff views.

other_links.label: MN DNR — Tettegouche State Park
other_links.note: Authority: sea caves, a sea stack and Palisade Head.

other_links.label: Lake Superior Circle Tour — Shovel Point Trail
other_links.note: Calls it a 1.9 mile out-and-back from behind the visitor centre and grades it easy.

trails.stats_note: Our card pairs two places AllTrails lists separately; the figures here are Shovel Point's. Distance differs by source (AllTrails 1.4 mi, Circle Tour 1.9 mi) and so does the grade — 64% of AllTrails reviewers call it moderate, the Circle Tour calls it easy. Palisade Head is a separate drive-up cliff.

trails.name: Superior Hiking Trail — Pincushion Mountain segment

alltrails.name: Pincushion Mountain via Superior Hiking Trail

other_links.label: USFS — Pincushion Mountain Trails
other_links.note: Superior National Forest authority page: the view down to Grand Marais, its harbour and lighthouse, with picnic tables at the trailhead.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Pincushion Mountain Overlook via Superior Hiking Trail
other_links.note: The short version — out to the summit overlook only, over boardwalks and rock, instead of the full 10.3 mi segment.

other_links.label: Superior Hiking — Pincushion Mountain Lookout Trail
other_links.note: Access is 3 miles up the Gunflint Trail from Grand Marais.

trails.stats_note: AllTrails grades the full segment challenging and averages 4 h 39 min. The overlook-only listing is the realistic afternoon option. No star rating could be sourced for either.

grand-marais-mn.dogs: The two state parks and the Superior Hiking Trail all take leashed dogs; the City of Grand Marais publishes no rule for Artist's Point, so that one is unanswered.
grand-marais-mn.dogs_source_quote: Pets are welcome in Minnesota's state parks, as long as they are kept on a leash six feet or shorter or effectively restrained by a portable enclosure.

Hike to the mainland sea caves from Meye.entity: The mainland sandstone sea caves on the Lakeshore's 12-mile mainland strip. Meyers Beach has no article and is not named in the park's; the Apostle Islands National Lakeshore article documents both the sandstone sea caves and the mainland unit.

trails.name: Big Bay State Park trails, Madeline Island

other_links.label: Wisconsin DNR — Big Bay State Park hiking
other_links.note: Authority: the Point trail connects with the Bay View Trail near the tip, 1.7 miles including a loop with inland and shoreline segments.

other_links.label: Wisconsin DNR — Big Bay State Park
other_links.note: Sandstone bluffs along 4 miles of Lake Superior shoreline, plus a 1-mile boardwalk.

other_links.label: Komoot — hiking in Big Bay State Park
other_links.note: Routes across the sandstone bluffs, barrier beach and lagoon.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Big Bay State Park area
other_links.note: Park-level browse page.

trails.stats_note: Our entry is the park's trails collectively; the AllTrails link is its most-reviewed single trail. The DNR's 1.7 mi is for the Point trail, not the whole network. Reaching it needs the Madeline Island ferry.

trails.name: Houghton Falls State Natural Area

other_links.label: Wisconsin DNR — Houghton Falls State Natural Area No. 638
other_links.note: Authority: protects unfragmented Lake Superior shoreline supporting bald eagle, merlin, veery, wood thrush and Canada warbler.

trails.stats_note: Takes about 0.5-1 hr. AllTrails publishes no difficulty grade for it, so none is recorded. The 76-acre natural area is just north of Washburn; sandstone cliffs run down into the lake with a beach at the end.

trails.name: Mainland Sea Caves near Meyers Beach

alltrails.name: Meyers Beach Sea Caves via Lakeshore Trail

other_links.label: NPS — Hiking in the Apostle Islands
other_links.note: Authority: from Meyers Beach the trail runs first to the Crevasse, then above the mainland sea caves, then through woods to the campsites.

other_links.label: Travel Wisconsin — Lakeshore Trail at Meyers Beach
other_links.note: Breaks the sections down: 1.8 miles to the Crevasse, 2.4 miles above the sea caves.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Lakeshore Trail Campsite via Meyers Beach
other_links.note: The longer continuation out to the campsite.

trails.stats_note: This is a clifftop hiking trail ABOVE the caves — the caves themselves are reached by kayak in summer and only over the ice in a hard winter, which is not a walk. AllTrails records it as dog-friendly. Sectional distances are Travel Wisconsin's; no single AllTrails length was in the snippet.

bayfield-wi.dogs: Apostle Islands takes leashed dogs on trails and beaches, and Wisconsin state parks permit them on trails but not on beaches; Houghton Falls is owned by the Town of Bayview, which publishes no rule at all.
bayfield-wi.dogs_source_quote: Leashed pets are welcome on trails, beaches, and in campgrounds in the Apostle Islands National Lakeshore.

Presque Isle Scenic Area and the three f.entity: The Presque Isle unit at the park's western end and its three waterfalls. The scenic area has no article; the Presque Isle River article names Manabezho, Manido and Nawadaha Falls — those three — and places the river inside Porcupine Mountains Wilderness State Park.

Porcupine Mountains Visitor Center.entity: The park's visitor centre on South Boundary Road. It has no article, and the Porcupine Mountains article — which is where the state park's own title redirects — never mentions a visitor centre. No link.

Superior beach at Union Bay.entity: The cobble beach at the Union Bay campground. Union Bay has no article and is not named in the Porcupine Mountains article; the water it fronts is Lake Superior.

Copper mining history.entity: Nineteenth-century copper mining in the Porcupine Mountains. The Porcupine Mountains article documents the Nonesuch Mine and the park's status as a cooperating unit of Keweenaw National Historical Park; Copper mining in Michigan is the general article.

Summit Peak observation tower.entity: The tower on Summit Peak, at 1,958 ft the highest point in the Porcupine Mountains. The bare title 'Summit Peak' is a Colorado 13er in the San Juans and is not used; the Porcupine Mountains article documents this Summit Peak.

Swim and beachcomb at Union Bay.entity: Union Bay on Lake Superior. As above, Union Bay itself is not documented; Lake Superior is.

offroad.name: No 4x4 routes inside the park
offroad.note: Confirmed by omission rather than by a quoted ban: the DNR park page lists the park's activities in full — snowmobiling, cross-country skiing, dog sledding, hiking, hunting, metal detecting, paddling — and ORV/ATV riding is absent. The DNR does name ORV riding explicitly at sites that have it, so the omission carries weight, but the actual prohibition text lives in the Land Use Orders of the Director Chapter V, which could not be opened. Treat as an absence of listing, not a quoted rule.

offroad.name: Ottawa National Forest roads toward Bond Falls and Agate Falls
offroad.season: Bond Falls: vehicle access typically mid-May through mid-October, weather depending; the hiking-trail access is open year-round. Ottawa NF routes designated 'Seasonal' are open 16 May through 14 Mar annually.
offroad.note: Bond Falls and Agate Falls are Michigan DNR scenic sites, not Forest Service ones, so their gate dates come from DNR and the road designations from the Ottawa. Watch the Ottawa's 65-inch OHV width rule — it excludes a full-size pickup from the designated OHV trails, but not from Forest Service roads open to highway-legal vehicles on the MVUM. Agate Falls was closed through late 2026 for trestle bridge repairs; long finished by 2028 but worth one re-check.

offroad.name: Shore-road spurs off M-64 east toward Ontonagon
offroad.note: No listing of any kind exists for these spurs — no Forest Service page, no route database, no club page. The road authority is the Ontonagon County Road Commission, which maintains every local shore spur off M-64 and is also the body the DNR names as deciding when South Boundary Road reopens each spring; its site returned 403 and is deliberately not linked here. M-64 itself is fully paved, so all the gravel is in the spurs, and no published inventory names them individually.

offroad.name: South Boundary Road, Union Bay end to Presque Isle end
offroad.season: DNR wording: park roads, including County Road M-107 at the Whitetail parking area and South Boundary Road from Headquarters Road south to the Pinkerton Trailhead, close Dec. 1 through late spring for visitor safety.
offroad.note: There is no fixed reopening date — the roads become designated snowmobile trails over winter and reopen to vehicles only when the Ontonagon County Road Commission deems them safe, so the Union Bay to Presque Isle through-drive is not guaranteed until they say so. The DNR publishes a workaround: the Presque Isle end stays reachable via County Road 519 just east of Wakefield. Park office 906-885-5275.

trails.name: Escarpment Trail

other_links.label: Michigan.org — Porcupine Mts Escarpment Trail
other_links.note: State tourism authority: a high rocky bluff with alpine-like vistas over the park interior.

other_links.label: Michigan Trail Maps — Escarpment Trail
other_links.note: Detailed route description along the ridgeline.

trails.stats_note: The westernmost section follows the ridge north of Lake of the Clouds. No length or grade was in the indexed snippet, so none is recorded. (Ignore a low-quality third-party page describing an 'Escarpment Trail' 4x4 route — that is not this hiking trail.)

trails.name: Lake of the Clouds overlook walkway

alltrails.name: Lake of the Clouds Overlook Loop

other_links.label: The Porcupine Mountains & Ontonagon Area — Lake of the Clouds
other_links.note: Confirms the overlook is reached by a fully accessible walkway — the most photographed feature in the park.

other_links.label: MyHikes — Lake of the Clouds Overlook
other_links.note: Records a 0.2-mile out-and-back and warns of crowds in peak foliage season.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Lake of the Clouds (backcountry route)
other_links.note: A separate, primitive foot-traffic-only route looking down on the lake from several angles — 824 reviews. Not the accessible walkway.

trails.stats_note: Short accessible loop with several viewing points, about half a mile of walking in total. No star rating could be sourced.

trails.name: Presque Isle River waterfall loop (East + West River Trails)

alltrails.name: West River Trail and East River Trail Loop

other_links.label: AllTrails — Presque Isle Falls Loop
other_links.note: The same waterfalls under a different listing, 530 reviews, described as good for kids and families.

other_links.label: Michigan Trail Maps — East-West River Trails
other_links.note: In its final mile the Presque Isle drops more than 100 feet through a steep-sided gorge; the East River Trail is the harder side.

other_links.label: MyHikes — Presque Isle River Waterfalls Loop
other_links.note: Moderate 3-mile hike taking in Manabezho, Manido and Nawadaha Falls.

trails.stats_note: Takes about 1-1.5 hr. Reviewers warn it is NOT a loop during spring thaw, when high water cuts the link between the east and west trails and park maps do not show it. No star rating could be sourced for this listing.

trails.name: Summit Peak observation tower

other_links.label: The Porcupine Mountains & Ontonagon Area — Summit Peak
other_links.note: Climb to the top of the old watch tower for panoramic views over the wilderness.

trails.stats_note: Out-and-back, about 0.5-1 hr. Highest point in the Porcupine Mountains at 1,958 ft, with a 50-foot tower on top. AllTrails publishes no difficulty grade, so none is recorded.

trails.name: Union Mine Interpretive Trail

other_links.label: Michigan.org — Porcupine Mts Union Mine Trail
other_links.note: State tourism authority: a waterfall trail rich with copper-mining history.

other_links.label: Michigan Trail Maps — Union Mine Trail
other_links.note: Best when water is high or during spring runoff.

trails.stats_note: Takes about 0.5-1 hr; AllTrails grades it moderately challenging. Ten interpretive plaques on the loop. Park entry needs a Michigan Recreation Passport for the vehicle; arriving on foot or by bicycle does not.

trails.name: Visitor Center Nature Trail

alltrails.name: Porcupine Mountain Wilderness Visitor Center Trail Loop

other_links.label: Michigan DNR — Porcupine Mountains Visitor Center
other_links.note: Authority for the visitor centre this trail loops from.

trails.stats_note: Takes about 0.5-1 hr; a flat interpretive loop. No star rating could be sourced.

porcupine-mountains-mi.dogs: Michigan DNR welcomes leashed dogs on state park trails, and the Porkies post no trail exception — the park's own backcountry cabins are pet-friendly and most are reached only on foot.
porcupine-mountains-mi.dogs_source_quote: Pets, such as dogs, are welcome in state parks and campgrounds, some overnight lodging facilities, state forest campgrounds, state-managed harbors, state-designated trails and boating access sites (with the exception of 33 locations with seasonal dog restrictions).

scenicDrives_patch.name: M-64 Lake Superior shore, Silver City to Ontonagon
scenicDrives_patch.distance: Silver City to Ontonagon is about 13 miles on M-64; the Ontonagon - Lake Superior Route road tour that contains this stretch is roughly 125 miles
scenicDrives_patch.note: The Porcupine Mountains & Ontonagon Area visitor bureau's road-tours page. Six tours are listed: Porcupine Mountains - Lake Gogebic Loop (~120 mi), Ontonagon - Lake Superior Route (~125 mi), Ontonagon - Victoria Dam Loop (~55 mi), Waterfalls and the Paulding Light (~100 mi), Keweenaw Cruisin' Tour (~200 mi) and the Lake Superior Circle Tour (1,300 mi). The M-64 segment is described only as offering "breathtaking Lake Superior vistas" — no pavement type or seasonal guidance is given for it, so none is recorded. The whole corridor is on the Lake Superior Circle Tour route.

Climb Sugarloaf Mountain.entity: The 470-ft quartzite knob on CR-550 north of Marquette. It has no article — the bare title 'Sugarloaf Mountain' is the peak in Rio de Janeiro, and no Michigan-disambiguated title exists. The Marquette article does not mention it either. No link.

Watch an ore boat load at the Upper Harb.entity: The LS&I ore dock in Marquette's Upper Harbor. The dock has no article; the Marquette, Michigan article documents it by name loading iron ore pellets onto lake freighters, and 'ore boat' is the Lake freighter article.

Ride or walk the Iron Ore Heritage Trail.entity: The Iron Ore Heritage Trail across the Marquette Iron Range, which has its own article.

Little Presque Isle and the CR-550 shore.entity: Little Presque Isle, the state-forest shore 7 miles north of town on CR-550. It has no article. Presque Isle Park is a different place — the city park peninsula inside Marquette — so linking it would be the wrong location. No link.

offroad.name: Co. Rd. AAA (Triple A Road), Yellow Dog Plains
offroad.distance: 11.9 mi, Big Bay to Yellow Dog Plains, +1,060 ft
offroad.difficulty: Moderate (the site's own scale)
offroad.note: Only the eastern half is suitable for standard vehicles — at the western edge of Yellow Dog Plains the road deteriorates into large puddles, big rocks and steep inclines that challenge even high-clearance vehicles, so plan to turn around there and run it as an out-and-back from Big Bay. There is no signage marking the turn off County Road 510; navigate by odometer. Naming trap: the same road is Co. Rd. AAA in Champion Township but Co. Rd. KAA in Powell Township, so signs and maps will disagree along its length. This source is a driving-route site, not a land manager — the turn-around advice is uncorroborated by any authority.

offroad.name: County Road 510
offroad.season: Marquette County seasonal weight restrictions historically go on mid-March and come off mid-May — in 2026, on 5 Mar and lifted 8:00 a.m. 18 May. Loads cut to 65% of normal legal load; the pickup is nowhere near the limit, but the dates mark when the dirt section is soft.
offroad.note: No route database lists this road. The Road Commission publishes an All Season Roads list by township and a status line on 906-486-4491 opt. 2.

offroad.name: Old CR-510 steel bridge over the Dead River
offroad.distance: 271.0 ft structure, 265.0 ft main span, 19 ft roadway width
offroad.note: The fact that changes the plan: the bridge is CLOSED to vehicles — open to traffic 1921, closed 2010 — so you cannot drive it. Marquette County left it standing for its historic value and it remains open to pedestrians, with a walkway approaching it on an even grade; signs read 'MCRC Property Enter At Own Risk'. It is the longest pin-connected highway truss span in Michigan and the type is extremely rare in the state. Reach it from the old CR 510 approaches, now County Road JWW and County Road JHH, or view it east of the new crossing. Park and walk, not a drive.

trails.name: Hogback Mountain Trail

other_links.label: Travel Marquette — Hogback Mountain
other_links.note: City tourism authority page with trail and seasonal information.

other_links.label: onX — Hogback Mountain
other_links.note: Puts it at about 4 miles out-and-back; trailhead off Beagle Club Road.

trails.stats_note: About 5 miles north of downtown Marquette off County Road 550. Marked with white/blue blazes; mostly flat until a steep rock finish to a 360-degree view. AllTrails says 3.2 mi, onX about 4 mi.

trails.name: Presque Isle Park loop trails (Black Rocks)

other_links.label: AllTrails — Presque Isle Park area
other_links.note: Park-level browse page for the forested peninsula at the north tip of Marquette.

trails.stats_note: No length or difficulty could be sourced from AllTrails for this listing, so neither is recorded — a secondary site puts the loop at about 2.2 mi and easy, which is worth confirming on the ground. Black Rocks is the cliff section on the loop — 20-to-30-foot volcanic cliffs locals jump from; it is a feature of this park, not a separate trail.

trails.name: Sugarloaf Mountain Trail

other_links.label: Michigan.org — Sugarloaf Mountain
other_links.note: State tourism authority: a short hike to arguably the best view in the Upper Peninsula.

trails.stats_note: Summit is 470 feet above the lake, reached by a 3,200-foot trail with dedicated pathways and wooden stairways — short, steep and stepped rather than long.

marquette-mi.dogs: Presque Isle Park is closed to animals outright — the dog cannot leave the truck there; Sugarloaf is Michigan DNR land and takes a leashed dog, and no authority could be identified for Hogback.
marquette-mi.dogs_source_quote: Animals are prohibited at the City’s Presque Isle Park, unless confined to a motor vehicle, at all public bathing beaches, at Park Cemetery, and at any special events where signs are posted specifically prohibiting animals with the exception of service animals under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA).

Chapel Loop to Chapel Rock and Beach.entity: The Chapel Basin loop in Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore. Chapel Rock, Chapel Beach and the loop have no articles of their own; the Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore article documents the Chapel area (Chapel Falls and Chapel Lake) and the cliffs the loop runs along.

Grand Island.entity: Grand Island offshore from Munising — administered as the Grand Island National Recreation Area within Hiawatha National Forest, which is the article that documents the island, its ferry and its shoreline.

links.label: Wikipedia — Grand Island National Recreation Area

offroad.name: Chapel Road (H-58 to Chapel Basin trailhead)
offroad.distance: 5 miles north off Alger County Road H-58, about 15 miles east of Munising; 17.8 mi from Munising, 34.2 mi from Grand Marais
offroad.difficulty: "a rough, backcountry road" — NPS wording; NPS publishes no rated scale
offroad.note: Heavy congestion in summer and early fall, and the trailhead lot often fills by 9 am — an early start matters more than the road does. Seasonal vault toilet, no drinking water. NPS publishes no winter gate date for this road; the park's conditions page carries only weather and ski grooming and has no road section at all.

offroad.name: H-58 spurs to Miners Beach, Little Beaver Lake and Hurricane River
offroad.note: NPS publishes distances to each spur but not the length of the spurs themselves: Miners Castle Road 5.2 mi from Munising, Little Beaver Lake Road 22.8, Hurricane River lower entrance 40.8 and upper 41.1. No difficulty or seasonal gate dates are published for any of them.

offroad.name: Hiawatha National Forest roads south of H-58
offroad.distance: over 2,000 miles of Forest Road open to motorized use, forest-wide
offroad.note: The MVUM classifies by permission, not difficulty — 'Roads Open to All Vehicles' versus 'Roads Open to Highway Legal Vehicles Only', and the pickup is the latter. Hard rule, verbatim: motor vehicle use off designated routes, including for game retrieval, is prohibited, with penalties up to $5,000 or 6 months regardless of the presence or absence of signs. Seasonal routes are flagged per-road on the sheet's Seasonal and Special Designation Table, not by one forest-wide date. MVUMs are reissued annually — pull a fresh one before the trip.

trails.name: Munising Falls Trail

other_links.label: NPS — Munising Falls
other_links.note: Authority: a paved 800-foot trail up a cool shaded canyon along Munising Creek to a 50-foot waterfall, inside the city limits where Washington Street becomes Sand Point Road.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Munising Falls (point of interest)
other_links.note: AllTrails carries the falls only as a point of interest, not as its own trail listing.

trails.stats_note: No AllTrails trail page exists for this walk — only a point-of-interest entry and a 42.4-mile Lakeshore Trail backpacking route that passes it. The NPS confirms the trail and its length. Paved and very short.

munising-mi.dogs: Pictured Rocks names its pet trails one by one: Miners Castle is open, Chapel, Mosquito and Log Slide are explicitly closed, and Munising Falls appears on neither list.
munising-mi.dogs_source_quote: Your leashed pet is welcome in these areas: … Miners Castle - Paved Trails, Overlook Platforms … These areas are CLOSED to pets: … Chapel Trails and Chapel Beach … Mosquito Trails and Mosquito Beach … Log Slide and Nearby Dunes

scenicDrives_patch.name: County Road H-58
scenicDrives_patch.season: Open and fully plowed only in the warm season. NPS: in winter "H-58 is only plowed from Munising heading east to Adams Trail", and inside the park "Sand Point Road is the only park road plowed in winter" (roughly December 1 to March 31). The stop arrives 25 Jul 2028 — no conflict.
scenicDrives_patch.note: Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore: H-58 is "the main road that travels through the national lakeshore", running Munising to Grand Marais, and is "suitable for vehicles of all sizes". The warnings the NPS does publish are about sharing it, not driving it: it is a "curvy road", "long sections of H-58 have very little shoulder or no shoulder at all", and it is "used by large logging trucks and many types of ORVs". No length is published on the NPS page, so none is recorded.

Upper Falls and the accessible boardwalk.entity: The Upper Falls, the 48-foot single drop. The Tahquamenon Falls article documents the Upper Falls; the boardwalk itself is not described in any article.

Lower Falls and the rowboat crossing.entity: The Lower Falls and the island in the middle of them. The Tahquamenon Falls article documents both, including that the island is reached by rowboat from the basin below (or the 2022 footbridge).

River Trail between the falls.entity: The four-mile trail linking Upper and Lower Falls. It has no article and is not named in either the Tahquamenon Falls or the state park article, which mention only the North Country Trail. No link.

Tahquamenon Falls Brewery & Pub at Camp.entity: The brewpub at the Upper Falls. No article, and neither 'Camp 33' nor the brewery appears in the state park article. No link.

Paddling the lower Tahquamenon.entity: The Tahquamenon River below the falls. Its article documents canoeing on the river.

Upper Falls.entity: The Upper Falls, documented in the Tahquamenon Falls article.

Lower Falls, four miles downstream.entity: The Lower Falls. The Tahquamenon Falls article gives the same distance — about 4 miles downstream — and the five smaller falls around the island.

Camp at the river mouth.entity: The Rivermouth campground unit at the Tahquamenon's mouth. The unit has no article; the Tahquamenon River article documents the mouth at Whitefish Bay and the state park article documents the park's campgrounds.

Tahquamenon Falls Brewery and Pub.entity: Same brewpub as above, second wording. No article, not documented in any parent. No link.

offroad.name: Crisp Point Light access roads (Luce County / forest roads west of Whitefish Point)
offroad.distance: CR 412 Crisp Point Rd, CR 423 to Singleton's Driveway and CR 502 to Crisp Point — 11.60 miles; approach CR 414 Pike Lake Rd, CR 407 to just west of Pike Lake — 11.27 miles
offroad.season: Luce County Road Commission seasonal roads list, Rev. 03/07/2023: not maintained for public travel from November 1 to April 30. The lighthouse society adds that the last 7 miles of CR 412 are usually open by the end of May, and that snow can make the road impassable even in spring.
offroad.note: This is the road authority's own seasonal-roads list, so it is the harder source than the lighthouse society's directions page the sibling entry links. Worth knowing the winter status: the road becomes Snowmobile Trail 8, and the society's own warning is not to drive it when there is snow. Watch for ATVs on the dirt.

offroad.name: Lake Superior State Forest two-tracks toward the Two-Hearted River mouth
offroad.distance: CR 423, CR 414 to the Mouth of the Two Hearted — 4.34 miles (Luce County Road Commission)
offroad.season: The county-road spine in is not maintained for public travel November 1 to April 30.
offroad.note: Honest limit: the graded county roads that get you in are fully documented, but no authority page describes the individual named two-tracks off them — treat the spine as listed and the two-tracks themselves as unlisted. This Newberry-approach directions page is the distinct source (the sibling entry carries the Paradise approach): roughly 37 miles, about 1 hour 10 minutes, and once off M-123 the roads are all dirt or sand, narrow and curvy. The society's own line is that they cannot guarantee you won't get stuck.

offroad.name: Vermilion Road toward the old Coast Guard station
offroad.distance: roughly 13 miles: from Paradise north on N. Whitefish Rd 5.2 mi, left on Vermilion Rd, 0.6 mi keeping right, then 6.1 mi on the straightest road, then 1.3 mi to the preserve
offroad.note: This is not a drive-through. Motorized vehicles, including ATVs and snowmobiles, are prohibited on the Vermilion Point preserve itself, so you drive the road to the boundary and walk to the old life-saving station — if the card implies driving to the station, that is wrong. Dogs are NOT allowed at the preserve 1 May to 15 August; leashed only the rest of the year. 175 acres, 9,240 ft of Lake Superior frontage, station first built 1876. Vermilion Road is in Chippewa County and is absent from the Luce County seasonal list; whether it carries its own seasonal designation is unknown.

trails.name: Clark Lake Loop

other_links.label: Michigan DNR — Tahquamenon Falls hiking trails map (PDF)
other_links.note: Authority: 'Clark Lake Loop (5.2 miles)', with a warning that conditions vary, fallen trees and wet areas are likely and cell service is minimal.

other_links.label: Michigan.org — Tahquamenon Falls Clark Lake Loop
other_links.note: Open to hiking, cross-country skiing and snowshoeing; begins at the Clark Lake Road parking lot and runs through pine forest.

trails.stats_note: Permitted uses are Michigan.org's — hiking, XC ski and snowshoe, with no mention of bikes. A recent AllTrails review measured the loop at 5.3 mi. Neither AllTrails nor the DNR publishes a difficulty grade for it, and no star rating could be sourced, so neither is recorded.

trails.name: Giant Pines Loop

other_links.label: Michigan.org — Tahquamenon Falls Giant Pines Trail
other_links.note: Authority: a 3.8-mile hiking trail through hemlocks and streams, named for two giant white pines on the route.

other_links.label: Hiking Project — Giant Pines Loop Trail
other_links.note: Graded intermediate.

trails.stats_note: Michigan.org says 3.8 mi, AllTrails 3.5 mi. Takes about 1-1.5 hr and AllTrails reviewers describe it as good for children and families.

trails.name: Lower Falls island loop

other_links.label: Michigan DNR — Tahquamenon Falls hiking trails map (PDF)
other_links.note: Official park trail map covering the Lower Falls area.

trails.stats_note: The AllTrails listing describes about 0.2 miles paved plus 0.4 miles of gravel road along the river with falls views, and notes loaner wheelchairs at the 'Fact Shack' by the Upper Falls parking lot. The river splits around a wooded midstream island reached by an island bridge or by rented rowboat. No star rating could be sourced; the listing carries 1,600 reviews.

trails.name: Tahquamenon River Trail (Lower Falls to Upper Falls)

other_links.label: Michigan DNR — Tahquamenon Falls hiking trails map (PDF)
other_links.note: Official park trail map for the river trail between the two falls.

trails.stats_note: Takes about 3.5-4 hr. The ground around the Lower Falls gets very muddy; accessible toilets at both ends and an off-road track chair is available. AllTrails' park page gives this trail 4.6 stars but the review count was not legible in the snippet, so no rating is recorded.

trails.name: Tahquamenon Falls Wilderness Loop

other_links.label: Michigan DNR — Tahquamenon Falls hiking trails map (PDF)
other_links.note: Official park trail map.

trails.stats_note: Graded moderately challenging, averaging about 3 hours. Quiet — the listing carries only 46 reviews and no star rating could be sourced.

tahquamenon-falls-mi.dogs: Tahquamenon Falls says it outright — leashed dogs on all trails and viewing platforms; Whitefish Point is a USFWS refuge unit that also allows them on lead, except inside the piping plover nesting closure at the tip.

scenicDrives_patch.name: M-123 loop: Rivermouth to Lower Falls to Upper Falls
scenicDrives_patch.distance: The park covers nearly 50,000 acres and stretches 13-plus miles; the byway that strings its three units together is 63 miles end to end
scenicDrives_patch.note: Michigan DNR. The park's own General Management Plan states "M-123 is a federally designated scenic byway, which provides access to the three main areas of the park" — Upper Falls, Lower Falls and Rivermouth are all on M-123, which is what makes this a drive rather than three separate outings. Rivermouth sits where the Tahquamenon River meets Whitefish Bay, south of Paradise; Lower Falls is inland west of Paradise. No official mileage between the individual units is published, so none is recorded. Arrival 31 Jul 2028 is mid-season with no closure in play.

scenicDrives_patch.name: M-123 west to Newberry
scenicDrives_patch.note: The Tahquamenon Scenic Byway, a Pure Michigan Byway: "a 63-mile journey through Michigan's Eastern Upper Peninsula", following M-123 to "experience the thunder of Tahquamenon Falls and the northern hospitality of villages like Newberry and Paradise, Michigan". Originally designated a Michigan Scenic Heritage Route in 1997 from Galloway Creek to County Road 500; all of M-123 north of M-28 carries the designation. MDOT's own byways index is at michigan.gov/mdot/travel/tourists/byways. The byway site promotes winter recreation but publishes no statement on winter road access, so no season field is claimed.

offroad.note: No listing exists for this as a named 4x4 route; this is the road authority confirming the roads and how they are managed. Live caution as of mid-2026: four separate M-119 segments were closed after April 2026 flooding, plus Lower Shore Dr — the corridor was still under FEMA disaster recovery. The park page adds that the shoreline outside pet-friendly areas is closed to pets April through August.
offroad.note: DNR names Nebo Trail, South Boundary Trail, Swamp Line Trail and Sturgeon Bay Trail as two-tracks, and notes many visitors ride Waugoshance Point Road. Park is 11 miles west of Mackinaw City, 26 miles of Lake Michigan shoreline. The dog is the binding constraint here, not the truck — check the arrival date against April 15 to August 31 before planning this one. Recreation Passport required for vehicle entry.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Grand Trunk backroads to West Montrose
scenicDrives_patch.note: The destination is sourced; the backroads themselves are not. Explore Waterloo Region: "The West Montrose Covered Bridge is Ontario's last remaining covered bridge. Located in Woolwich Township, the bridge has a 198-foot span across the Grand River. Built in 1881." THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS: the bridge carries a legal posted load limit of 3 tonnes and "should not be crossed by trucks, buses, tractors or other heavy vehicles", and the Region of Waterloo has confirmed "The legal posted load limit of 3 tonnes will be maintained after the proposed bridge rehabilitation. The Region and Township do not wish to attract more and heavier vehicles." Three tonnes is about 6,600 lb — a half-ton pickup clears it, a loaded three-quarter-ton diesel may not. Weigh or check the door-jamb GVW before driving across rather than after. No named "Grand Trunk backroads" route is published by any authority; the approach roads are ordinary township roads.

offroad.season: Ontario Parks states conservation reserves do not have operating dates.
offroad.note: Material change the existing note predates: this land was re-designated in 2023. Point Petre Provincial Wildlife Area and the Ostrander Point Crown Land Block are now the Monarch Point Conservation Reserve, 1,607 ha, regulated under the Provincial Parks and Conservation Reserves Act, 2006 — so any framing of it as MNRF Crown land is out of date. The regulation notice says vehicle use "will be permitted to continue on trails, or off trail to retrieve game, as long as the values the conservation reserve was created to protect are not adversely impacted," and warns that timing restrictions or trail closures could be added later. No management plan with a road inventory exists yet, so no authority publishes mileage, ratings or gate dates. Sandbanks Provincial Park (613) 393-3319 is the only way to get a current answer.
