offroad.distance: approximately 350 km of gravel roads in the township, many of them seasonal, across 1,048 km²
offroad.season: Two separate restrictions, and the second is the one that bites. Reduced loads are usually in effect from March 1st to mid-May. Seasonal Roads — Class 6B and Class 6C — are CLOSED between November 15 and April 15. That is an outright closure of the seasonal gravel, not a weight limit.
offroad.note: Manager of Public Works 613-259-2398 ext. 239; road emergency 613-264-7329.

perth-on.dogs: The three trails inside Murphys Point are fine on a two-metre lead — Ontario Parks lists no park-specific restriction there. The Rideau Trail is the open question: the Rideau Trail Association says dogs are barred from many portions and does not say which, so the Perth section cannot be called either way without asking them.
perth-on.dogs_source_quote: In many portions of the trail dogs are not permitted! (dogs are not permitted on official Rideau Trail Association hikes). Where dogs are permitted, keep them on a leash.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Tay Canal / Perth heritage loop
scenicDrives_patch.note: The Rideau Canal Heritage Tour, central section — a driving loop that starts and ends in Perth, "originally laid out as a military settlement in 1816 to help protect the inland water route connecting Lake Ontario with the Ottawa River". Roads used are County Roads 43, 17, 16, 29 and 14 plus Highways 8, 42 and 15; stops are Smiths Falls (Railway Museum, Detached Lock, Visitor Centre), Kilmarnock Lock, Toledo, Forfar and Narrows Lock, where one of the four blockhouses built by Colonel By in 1830-31 still stands. Two caveats: no total distance is published for the loop, and it does NOT include Merrickville, which sits on a different section of the tour (rideau-info.com/canal/driving/). For the Tay itself, Parks Canada is the authority — "The Tay Canal branch of the Rideau Canal extends from Beveridges Lockstation to the town of Perth. The canal ends in the middle of the town at a large turning basin lined with timber crib wharves" (parks.canada.ca/docs/r/on/rideau/whl-lhm/chap2/chap2a1/chap2a1q). Lockstation operating season is not stated on the driving-tour page; an 18 Sep arrival is near the end of the Rideau navigation season, so boats locking through is a check-first, not a given.

Mirror Lake walk.entity: Mirror Lake, the 124-acre lake in the centre of Lake Placid village — the article confirms the village of Lake Placid, town of North Elba, not another New York Mirror Lake.

High Peaks Wilderness day hikes.entity: The High Peaks Wilderness Area, the largest Forest Preserve wilderness in the Adirondack Park.

Drive the Whiteface Veterans' Memorial H.entity: The Whiteface Veterans Memorial Highway (NY 431) to the summit parking area. No separate article; the Whiteface Mountain article documents the highway by name, its 1929 construction and the summit tunnel and elevator.

Walk the gorge at High Falls Gorge.entity: The privately run gorge walk on the Ausable River. No article of its own; the Wilmington, New York article lists High Falls Gorge as a location on NY 86 south of Wilmington village.

Day-run into Saranac Lake.entity: Saranac Lake, New York, the village west of Lake Placid.

Paddle straight off your campsite at Fis.entity: Fish Creek Pond and its state campground in the Adirondacks. No article contains the phrase 'Fish Creek Pond' at all; the Saranac Lakes Wild Forest and Saint Regis Canoe Area articles, which cover the surrounding land, never mention it, and the only 'Fish Creek Ponds' hit is a one-line gazetteer entry in Harrietstown, New York, which documents nothing about the ponds or the campground.

offroad.name: Upper Works Road (CR 25A)
offroad.distance: 3.3 mi
offroad.difficulty: 1 (Easy) — onX rates it 1/10 for smooth, well-maintained gravel and dirt with no significant obstacles
offroad.season: Best spring, summer, fall. Neither the Town of Newcomb nor DEC publishes a winter plowing status or gate date for this road.
offroad.note: Ends at a large parking area with a pit toilet, and passes the historic McIntyre Blast Furnace of the Tahawus ghost town — you can drive to the gate, the rest of the ghost town is on foot. The road follows the Hudson close to its source, past marshes and ponds. Naming caveat worth carrying: the Town of Newcomb and DEC call the county route CR 25 (Tahawus Road), not CR 25A, and the Town states the old parking lot at the terminus of Upper Works Road is closed, with parking moved to a 60-car lot by the MacNaughton Cottage and unauthorised vehicles towed. The draw is history and trailhead access rather than the driving.

offroad.name: Deer Pond Road
offroad.distance: 2.2 mi
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — rated 2/10, mostly easy dirt with minor potholes and muddy puddles after rain
offroad.season: DEC requires parking reservations from Memorial Day weekend until the gates close for winter in late November or early December.
offroad.note: Resolved to the Essex Chain Lakes Complex in Newcomb, where DEC calls it the Cornell/Deer Pond Road — not Moose River Plains. Ends at a large parking area on the edge of the Essex Chain Lakes Primitive Area with a pit toilet and a gate; you continue on foot to the water. Several roadside dispersed camp spots along it. DEC's own wording for the roads here: pickup trucks, SUVs and other high axle vehicles are recommended, four wheel drive will serve even better. Beavers occasionally flood portions of the road.

offroad.name: Otter Brook Road
offroad.distance: 2.9 mi, out-and-back
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — not very difficult, but one vehicle wide and needing some higher clearance toward the end
offroad.season: Best spring, summer, fall. DEC publishes no fixed gate dates for Otter Brook Road itself; the parent access, the Limekiln Lake–Cedar River Road, is a seasonal road that opens mid-May.
offroad.note: DEC-maintained, in the Moose River Plains Complex, and it sees very little traffic. Surface alternates sandy two-track and well-maintained gravel; it ends at a bog where a small snowmobile bridge crosses the South Branch of the Grass River. Live closure to check before going: a bridge failure at Payne Brook has forced all Moose River Plains access to the Limekiln Lake/Inlet entrance, with the Cedar River Headquarters gate closed — approach from the west. DEC Region 5 Northville 518-863-4545.

offroad.name: Lake Glen Road
offroad.distance: 6.6 mi
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — an established forest access road with a stable base, no deep waterholes or large rocks
offroad.season: Best summer and fall; no gate dates published by anyone.
offroad.note: Runs around the southern flank of 3,550 ft Saddleback Mountain through the Adirondack Forest Preserve. Side-trail access at the western end is blocked by a forest products company that owns most of the surrounding land. Honest limit: this is the one Adirondack route no authority confirms — no DEC page, unit management plan or roads-open-to-motor-vehicle-use listing names it, and because it runs between Forest Preserve and private industrial timberland its legal access basis is genuinely unestablished. Recent reports include downed trees needing recovery boards in Dec 2025.

lake-placid-ny.dogs: Cascade and Porter are DEC Forest Preserve and take dogs, but the leash is compulsory the whole way — they sit in the zone where DEC requires a leash at all times, not just above 4,000 ft. Mount Jo is on the Adirondack Mountain Club's Heart Lake property and ADK publishes no pet policy for it; the managing authority for the Owl's Head trail could not be established, so both are blank rather than assumed.
lake-placid-ny.dogs_source_quote: Dogs must be leashed at all times in the Eastern Zone of the High Peaks Wilderness

Cross to Burlington for a proper town da.entity: Burlington, Vermont — the city named in the headline, eleven miles south across the lake.

Drive out to Isle La Motte and Saint Ann.entity: Both named things have their own articles: Isle La Motte, the northernmost Champlain island, and Saint Anne's Shrine — confirmed as the Isle La Motte shrine on Lake Champlain (site of Fort Sainte Anne, 1666), not one of the several other Saint Anne shrines.

Grand Isle–Plattsburgh ferry.entity: The route has no article of its own, but the Lake Champlain Transportation Company article documents it under its own heading 'Grand Isle-Plattsburgh' — an ice-breaking route with 24-hour year-round service between Grand Isle, VT and Cumberland Head, Plattsburgh, NY — which is exactly the claim in this entry.

Run the causeway drive up US Route 2 thr.entity: US Route 2 is the named thing; the Vermont article covers the Grand Isle County section that crosses Lake Champlain 'over several bridges' and lists the South Hero junction. Knight Point State Park, the North Hero day-use park named in the note, is confirmed separately — sand beach, boat rentals and the Campmeeting Point Natural Area with its rare plant species.

Snow Farm Vineyard & Distillery.entity: A working winery and distillery on West Shore Road. No Wikipedia article; the only mention anywhere is a one-line directory row in List of wineries in New England ('Snow Farm Vineyard and Distillery - South Hero'), which documents nothing about it. The card already carries the winery's own site.

Walk the shoreline at Grand Isle State P.entity: Grand Isle State Park in Grand Isle, Vermont — the 226-acre lakeshore park; the article confirms the lean-to and cabin sites, hot showers and trailer sanitary station this entry relies on. Disambiguated from the Louisiana park of the same name.

Watch the sunset from the west shore.entity: A viewing direction, not a place: 'the west shore' of South Hero across the widest part of Lake Champlain to the Adirondack High Peaks. Nothing named, and linking the lake or the High Peaks would point at neither the shore nor the sunset window this entry is about.

south-hero-vt.dogs: Split stop: the two Missisquoi NWR trails take a leashed dog under the refuge's own rule, but Vermont publishes nothing reachable for Mount Philo or Niquette Bay, so treat both state parks as unknown until Vermont State Parks is phoned.
south-hero-vt.dogs_source_quote: Pets must be leashed and under the control of the owner while on the refuge.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Sandbar Causeway (US-2, Milton to South Hero)
scenicDrives_patch.note: Vermont State Parks' Sand Bar page — "Sand Bar State Park takes its name from a natural sandbar between South Hero Island" and the town of Milton on the mainland; the park address is 1215 US Route 2, Milton. The causeway carrying US-2 across it was built in the 1950s on top of an 1850s bridge, over a sandbar formed by Lamoille River sediment. Fetching vtstateparks.com returned HTTP 403 (bot detection), so the listing is confirmed from the search result's own title and snippet and no season dates are recorded. Sand Bar is a day-use beach park with a short summer season, so a 28 Sep arrival will likely find the park itself closed while US-2 across the causeway stays open — check the park's season before planning a stop rather than a drive-through.

Stowe village and foliage drives.entity: Stowe, Vermont and the roads around it.

Covered bridges.entity: Stowe's covered bridges, chiefly the 1844 Gold Brook Covered Bridge (Emily's Bridge), the state's only 19th-century covered bridge on wooden Howe trusses carrying a public road.

links.label: Wikipedia — List of covered bridges in Vermont

Drive the Mount Mansfield Toll Road in t.entity: The toll road up Mount Mansfield, Vermont's highest peak.

Climb Camel's Hump.entity: Camel's Hump, the 4,083 ft Green Mountains peak.

Base yourself at Gold Brook and stay put.entity: Gold Brook Campground on VT 100 south of Stowe village. No article. Wikipedia's 'Gold Brook' hit is the Gold Brook Covered Bridge (Emily's Bridge, 1844) — a different thing on the same stream, already linked from the 'Covered bridges' entry on this stop — so it is rejected here on identity.

Time it for peak colour.entity: Foliage timing for the Stowe/Waterbury elevation band, not an entity. The places the note names for dropping elevation — Mount Mansfield and the notch — are already linked from the Mansfield toll road and Smugglers Notch entries on this stop.

trails.name: Stowe Pinnacle Trail
trails.was: Stowe Pinnacle Trail — no url
trails.note_source: Stowe's most popular and hardest trail. No direct listing url surfaced in search. Name kept; no constructed slug.

other_links.label: Vermont Trail Finder — Stowe Pinnacle
other_links.note: Half a mile of false flat, then a staircase-like climb; an overlook spur partway up faces Mount Mansfield. Puts the round trip at just under 5 mi from either trailhead.

other_links.label: Go Stowe — Stowe Pinnacle
other_links.note: Two trailheads: Upper Hollow Road is 3.6 mi round trip, the Pinnacle Meadows lot cuts it to about 2.6 mi.

trails.stats_note: The elevation gain is AllTrails' own 476 m converted. Published distances vary a lot with which of the two trailheads you use — 2.6 to 5 mi round trip — so check the lot before setting out.

trails.name: Bingham Falls Trail
trails.was: Bingham Falls — no url

trails.name: Moss Glen Falls Trail

alltrails.name: Moss Glen Falls Trail and VAST 100 Trail

trails.was: Moss Glen Falls (Stowe) — no url
trails.note_source: No direct listing url surfaced in search. Name kept; no constructed slug.

other_links.label: Go Stowe — Moss Glen Falls
other_links.note: Five minutes' drive from Stowe village; the falls themselves are about a quarter-mile from the trailhead.

other_links.label: Vermont Trail Finder — Moss Glen Falls
other_links.note: Directions: VT-100 north 3 mi, right on Randolph Road, right on Moss Glen Falls Road, lot on the right after 0.5 mi. Plowed in winter as a bus turnaround.

trails.stats_note: Two very different walks share this name. The 5.2 mi / 941 ft figure is the full trail continuing onto the VAST 100 corridor — this is the listing AllTrails confirms as 'near Stowe'. The waterfall itself is a quarter-mile from the parking area, so most visits are under a mile. A separate short AllTrails entry with 1,133 reviews exists but its town could not be confirmed, and a third, 0.1 mi with 161 reviews, is the unrelated Moss Glen Falls at Granville.

trails.name: Mount Mansfield via Sunset Ridge

alltrails.name: The Chin (Mount Mansfield) via Sunset Ridge Trail

trails.was: Mount Mansfield via Sunset Ridge / — no url
trails.note_source: No direct listing url surfaced in search. Name kept; no constructed slug.
trails.stats_note: AllTrails gives 4.5–5 hr. Other sources put the same route at 6.0–6.6 mi and rate it Hard; the ridge above treeline is exposed alpine tundra and there is no shelter on it.

trails.name: Mount Mansfield via Sunset Ridge / Long Trail

alltrails.name: Sunset Ridge and Long Trail Loop

other_links.label: AllTrails — Mount Mansfield Loop Trail
other_links.note: Maple Ridge, Long Trail and Sunset Ridge combined, 2,970 reviews — the bigger version of the same day.

trails.stats_note: AllTrails describes this as one of the most popular routes in Underhill State Park — up Sunset Ridge, back along the Long Trail on the ridge — but published no distance, gain or difficulty in any search result, so none is recorded here.

trails.name: Sterling Pond Trail

other_links.label: Go Stowe — Sterling Pond
other_links.note: Trailhead is in Smugglers' Notch, which closes to through traffic in winter; the pond is Vermont's highest trout pond.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Spruce Peak via Sterling Pond Trail
other_links.note: Continuation past the pond to Spruce Peak; parks at the Smugglers' Notch visitor centre.

trails.stats_note: AllTrails says 1 h 37 min for 2.2 mi. Published gain ranges from ~950 to ~1,320 ft across sources — it is short and steep either way, rocky with exposed roots.

offroad.name: Patterson Brook Road (Fire Service 50)
offroad.distance: 5.2 mi, out-and-back
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — easy driving, but care is needed because active logging changes road conditions; a chainsaw for blowdowns helps
offroad.season: Green Mountain National Forest, official: most GMNF roads are closed during the winter months from December 15 to May 1, with some exceptions. FR 50 Patterson Brook, Rochester district, currently listed Open.
offroad.note: The one route in this set with a real land-manager behind it. Borders the Bread Loaf Wilderness, climbing from 1,043 ft near Granville to 1,868 ft. Dispersed off-grid campsites along FR 50, no permit, 14-day limit, and no cell service. Stream crossings are on good bridges.

offroad.name: Symonds Mill Road
offroad.distance: 4.1 mi
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — "country dirt roads"
offroad.season: Best fall, summer, spring. No town or state mud-season restriction found for this road.
offroad.note: The one Vermont route in this set that is genuinely local to the stop — Wolcott/Elmore, about 20 minutes from Stowe. Mostly packed gravel with some muddy sections; these are working farm roads, so watch for farm equipment and livestock. Pairs with Woodbury Mountain Road if you want a longer day.

offroad.name: Big Hollow Road
offroad.distance: 6.2 mi
offroad.difficulty: 3 (Easy) — varied surface from packed gravel to dirt to mud
offroad.season: Best fall and summer. A status report of 14 Apr 2026 has it Temporarily Closed for a posted seasonal closure, with no stated opening day — consistent with a Vermont Class 4 mud-season closure. Best avoided during spring sugaring season.
offroad.note: Location flag worth resolving before the trip: this listing sits at 44.227, -73.056, which is Starksboro in Addison County — west of the Green Mountain spine and about 35 miles from Stowe, not the Fayston Big Hollow Road. Fayston's town roads page and its 2020 Town Plan both fetch clean with no mention of a Big Hollow Road, so no listing for the Fayston one could be sourced. Starts as farm gravel, becomes a standard Class 4 road with small obstacles, past abandoned homes and maple sugaring equipment; narrows at a log landing halfway, then an older, less-used trail out into a field with horses.

offroad.name: Top of the World
offroad.distance: 3.8 mi
offroad.difficulty: 3 (Easy) — maintained gravel that washes out on the steeper climbs, with water bars that can catch a low bumper
offroad.season: Best time listed as summer only.
offroad.note: Same location flag as Big Hollow: this runs the powerlines on the Vermont side of Moore Reservoir, near Waterford in Caledonia County — roughly 50 miles east of Stowe, a long day trip rather than a local run. No Roxbury or Northfield 'Top of the World Road' could be sourced anywhere. The payoff at the top is a view over Moore Reservoir toward New Hampshire. Many offshoots from mild to wild; the final climb is where 4WD matters if it has washed out. Expect ATV and side-by-side groups on a fine day. Reports through 2026 say a washout has been repaired and the route rebuilt into an easy dirt road.

trails: Mount Mansfield via Sunset Ridge / Long Trail
dogs_unpublished.authority: Vermont Dept. of Forests, Parks and Recreation / Vermont State Parks (C.C. Putnam State Forest, Mount Mansfield State Forest, Underhill State Park, Smugglers' Notch State Park), with the Green Mountain Club maintaining the Long Trail sections

It names Stowe Pinnacle in passing as a dog hike but states no permission.

Search index for vtstateparks.com and fpr.vermont.gov pet pages returned only third-party guides (dogtrailrules, petfriendlytravel, Burlington Free Press), never an official sentence

Aug 2026 pass — tried the rule as LAW rather than as a park page, since the park pages are the part that 403s. The adopted rule is Code of Vermont Rules 12 020 009, 'VISITOR CONDUCT AND FEES AND CHARGES FOR STATE PARK SERVICES AND COMMERCIAL ACTIVITIES ON DEPARTMENT LANDS'. Every route to its text failed, listed below.

https://secure.vermont.gov/SOS/rules/ — LOADS (so the Vermont 403 is not domain-wide, it is specific to the parks sites). But it carries PROPOSED rules only, and points to LexisNexis for adopted ones.

http://www.lexisnexis.com/hottopics/codeofvtrules/ — the Secretary of State's designated publisher of the Code of Vermont Rules. 301-redirects into advance.lexis.com, a JavaScript container that returns no rule text.
https://sos.vermont.gov/rules/ — 403
https://regulations.justia.com/states/vermont/agency-12/sub-agency-020/chapter-009/section-12-020-009/ — 403. This is the one page a search actually surfaced with the right citation, and it refused.

https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/vermont/12-020-009 — loads, but only as an agency index; Cornell LII carries no Vermont rule text at this citation (it does carry North Dakota's, which is how Bismarck was settled).

https://lite.duckduckgo.com/lite/?q=%22Vermont+State+Parks%22+rules+%22pets%22+leash+rabies+certificate+official+PDF — returned Burlington Free Press, Hipcamp and a vtstateparks.com tag page. No official rule text anywhere in the index.
dogs_unpublished.action: Phone Vermont State Parks on 1-888-409-7579 (or parks@vermont.gov) and ask two things: are dogs permitted on Mount Mansfield's Sunset Ridge and the Long Trail over the summit ridge, given the alpine zone, and is there any dog restriction on the Putnam State Forest trails at Stowe Pinnacle and Moss Glen Falls. One call settles all six. Worth doing before arrival — this is a 4-night hard-anchored stop on 1 Oct 2028 and the trails are most of what the stop is for.

Sutton's Mont Sutton area.entity: Mont Sutton and the town of Sutton, Quebec in the Eastern Townships.

Settle into the Lac-Stukely campground.entity: The Lac-Stukely camping sector of Mont-Orford National Park. The campground has no article; Lake Stukely's article confirms the lake borders a large part of the park, and the park article documents camping.

Visit the Abbaye Saint-Benoit-du-Lac.entity: The Benedictine abbey on Lake Memphremagog. English Wikipedia has no separate abbey article — the community article Saint-Benoit-du-Lac is the abbey and its cheese-making facility, and nothing else.

Make one run into Sherbrooke.entity: Sherbrooke, the Eastern Townships' main city.

trails.name: L'Étang-Fer-de-Lance (Parc national du Mont-Orford)

alltrails.name: Fer-de-Lance Pond and Campeur Hill (Étang Fer-de-Lance et colline du Campeur)

other_links.label: Hiking Project — Sentier de l'Étang-Fer-de-Lance
other_links.note: Short walk to a viewpoint over the marsh and the mountains behind it.

trails.stats_note: AllTrails' listing bundles the pond loop with the Colline du Campeur; about 42 min. Its own trailhead page for the sentier is a POI, not a route.

trails.name: Le Mont-Chauve (Parc national du Mont-Orford)

other_links.label: AllTrails — Mont-Chauve via Sentier du Pékan
other_links.note: The long way in off the Pékan: 10.3 mi, challenging, about 4 h 56 min, 54 reviews.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Mont Chauve via le Castor et des Loutres
other_links.note: Third approach; the summit is 599 m.

trails.stats_note: Étang aux Cerises is the Mont-Orford sector this trail leaves from, which is how the listing was confirmed as the right Mont Chauve — there is another of the same name at Saint-Zénon. Reviewers call it technical, heavy on roots and rock, with a steady climb from about the 5th km. AllTrails published no distance for this variant; only the en-locale URL was returned.

trails.name: Le Pékan (Parc national du Mont-Orford)
trails.stats_note: About 2 h 16 min, near Orford. Forest trail running along a lake.

trails.name: Panorama Trail, Owl's Head (Mansonville)

alltrails.name: Owls Head via Panorama Trail and Abénakis-Maçonique Trail

other_links.label: Municipalité de Potton — Owl's Head hiking trails
other_links.note: The municipality manages the three hiking trails on Owl's Head Mountain — Panorama, Abénaquis-Maçonnique and Anaconda — and all leave from the same parking lot. This is the authority confirming Panorama is a summer hiking trail and not a ski run.

other_links.label: Owl's Head — hiking
other_links.note: Resort's own page; all trails lead to the summit, average elevation 540 m.

other_links.label: Trailforks — Sentier Panorama
other_links.note: 4 km singletrack, graded black diamond.

trails.stats_note: Distance is published two ways — Trailforks 4 km one way as black-diamond singletrack, Plein air À la carte 5.2 km as a loop — so no single figure is recorded. It is steep either way.

eastern-townships-qc.dogs: Sépaq publishes a dog map for Mont-Orford that draws every trail either "Chien autorisé" or "Chien interdit", and only a short list is green: l'Étang-Fer-de-Lance and the Mont-Chauve loop are among them. Le Pékan is not — the whole Mont-Orford massif network it runs through, including the summit routes, is drawn in red. Owl's Head is a private resort and takes leashed dogs on all its trails including Panorama.

Kancamagus Highway.entity: The Kancamagus Highway, the eastern 32 miles of New Hampshire Route 112 from Lincoln to Conway. It redirects to the route article.

Run the Kancamagus Highway end to end.entity: The same Kancamagus Highway, driven Conway to Lincoln.

Get up to Cathedral Ledge.entity: Cathedral Ledge above Echo Lake. No article of its own; the Echo Lake State Park article documents Cathedral Ledge and the mile-long auto road to its top.

Climb Mount Chocorua.entity: Mount Chocorua, the 3,490 ft easternmost Sandwich Range peak.

offroad.name: Jefferson Notch Road
offroad.distance: 8.4 mi
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — wide enough for vehicles to pass almost anywhere, though storms leave ruts and washouts
offroad.season: Gate dates, from 11 opening and 10 closing reports 2016–2026: opens usually around June 12, as late as June 24; closes usually around November 29, as early as November 3. The Forest Service itself publishes only status plus a last-updated date and the note "Not maintained for winter travel, Snowmobile trail system" — these dated figures are crowdsourced, not a WMNF publication.
offroad.note: Highest elevation reached by a public road in New Hampshire, and one of the last WMNF roads to open each spring — an early-autumn stop is well inside the window, a spring one would not be. Many dispersed campsites, mostly on the north side toward Valley Road, 14-day max and you must occupy the first night. Mostly a car and a half wide.

offroad.name: Sandwich Notch Road
offroad.distance: 7.9 mi
offroad.difficulty: 1 (Easy) — the easiest of the local set; well-maintained forest road
offroad.season: Opens usually around May 12, as late as June 3; closes usually around October 28, from 14 opening and 8 closing reports 2013–2026. Note the late-October closing average — this is the one road in the set that can shut before the others. WMNF lists it as maintained by the town of Sandwich and NOT maintained for winter travel.
offroad.note: FR 98. Established 1801 and laid out as a route from the Pemigewasset valley to the seacoast; cellar holes still line it. Points of interest along the way: Upper and Lower Hall Ponds, Kiah Pond, Gillman Hall Cemetery and Beede Falls.

offroad.name: Tripoli Road
offroad.distance: 8.2 mi
offroad.difficulty: 1 (Easy) — very well maintained and mostly gravel; the hardest parts are the few stretches of unmaintained, badly deteriorated pavement
offroad.season: Opens usually around May 21, as late as May 31; closes usually around November 19, as early as November 1, from 12 opening and 10 closing reports 2015–2026.
offroad.note: FR 30. Built by the Forest Service in 1934 with CCC help and named for the Tripoli Mill; runs the pass between Mt Tecumseh and Mt Osceola. Popular for trailhead and campsite access. Bear and moose activity especially at night, and no cell service in the middle section.

offroad.name: Slippery Brook
offroad.distance: 4.6 mi. WMNF describes FR 17 and FR 38 together as a 7-mile road system commonly known as Town Hall Road.
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — gravel, well maintained in the summer months
offroad.season: Opens usually around May 24, as late as June 26; closes usually around November 29, as early as November 14, from 12 opening and 10 closing reports 2014–2026. Multiple gates close depending on snow levels and it is not maintained in winter.
offroad.note: This is National Forest System Road 17, in Jackson and Chatham. Camping and fire restrictions are in force 1 June 2026 to 1 June 2031: no camping within a quarter mile of the road except at designated sites marked with a tent symbol, and no wood or charcoal fires in the same band except at those sites — pressurised-fuel stoves are permitted. Worth knowing before planning a fire.

offroad.name: East Branch Saco River
offroad.distance: 3.3 mi
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — dirt road, not plowed in winter, with one rough spot near the end by the beaver bog
offroad.season: Opens usually around May 26, as late as June 24; closes usually around November 24, as early as November 9, from 10 opening and 10 closing reports 2016–2026.
offroad.note: Resolved: this is East Branch Road, FR 38 — the East Branch of the Saco, in Jackson and Chatham, not the East Branch Pemigewasset — and it is the companion to Slippery Brook FR 17 in the Town Hall Road system. Well-maintained dirt and gravel hugging the river, with pull-offs for camping and trailheads and a bridge crossing; dead-ends at a hiking trail. The same quarter-mile camping and fire restrictions as FR 17 apply through 2031.

trails.name: Arethusa Falls

alltrails.name: Arethusa Falls via Bemis Brook and Arethusa Falls Trails

other_links.label: AllTrails — Arethusa Falls (all routes)
other_links.note: Four trails reach the falls; this page lists them.

other_links.label: Waterfalls Guide — Arethusa Falls
other_links.note: 140 ft horsetail on Bemis Brook in Crawford Notch State Park; puts the direct route at 2.6 mi round trip with about 900 ft of climbing.

trails.stats_note: AllTrails indexes the Bemis Brook variant, which adds the lower cascades. The direct Arethusa Falls Trail is shorter — 2.6 to 3.1 mi depending on source.

trails.name: Boulder Loop Trail
trails.stats_note: AllTrails' 3.5 mi includes the ledge spur; NH Family Hikes gives the loop itself as 3.1 mi with 920 ft of gain. The trail climbs a series of ledges to open views over the Swift River valley.

trails.name: Diana's Baths

other_links.label: Vermont/NH Trail Finder — Diana's Baths
other_links.note: Scenic waterfall and swimming area on Lucy Brook in the White Mountain National Forest.

trails.stats_note: About 24 min. AllTrails files it under Intervale; it is in Bartlett, just west of North Conway, and is one of the most heavily used short walks in the valley.

trails.name: Mount Willard
trails.stats_note: About 1 h 52 min, from the Crawford Notch depot. The slug is 'mount-willard', not 'mount-willard-trail'.

trails.name: Sabbaday Falls
trails.stats_note: About 18 min, off the Kancamagus Highway; AllTrails files it under Bartlett.

north-conway-nh.dogs: All five take dogs. The White Mountain National Forest welcomes them and names Diana's Baths itself as a developed trail where the leash is required; Arethusa Falls and Mount Willard sit in Crawford Notch State Park, where NH State Parks permits pets "on hiking trails and designated dog walk area only", six-foot leash.
north-conway-nh.dogs_source_quote: Yes. Dogs are welcome in the White Mountain National Forest; however, they must be leashed when in developed recreation areas such as campgrounds, picnic areas, trailhead parking lots, and on developed trails (Diana's Baths, for instance).

Drive the Cadillac Summit Road in the pi.entity: The summit road up Cadillac Mountain in Acadia National Park.

Do the Park Loop Road properly.entity: The 27-mile Park Loop Road around eastern Mount Desert Island.

Walk or ride the carriage roads.entity: Acadia's Rockefeller-financed carriage road system. It has no separate article; the Acadia National Park article documents the historic carriage roads and the ban on motor vehicles.

Circle Jordan Pond and have the popovers.entity: Jordan Pond in Acadia, its shore path, and the popovers served at the Jordan Pond House.

Photograph Bass Harbor Head Light.entity: Bass Harbor Head Light on the southwest side of Mount Desert Island.

bar-harbor-me.dogs: ALLOWED on most trails — 100 miles of trail and 45 miles of carriage road, leash 6 ft. Acadia is one of the most dog-friendly national parks on this entire trip. Six trails are closed to pets outright: Precipice, BEEHIVE, Ladder Trail to Dorr Mountain, Beech Cliffs, Perpendicular (Mansell Mountain), and Jordan Cliffs between Penobscot East Trail and the carriage road. Nine more are "not recommended".
bar-harbor-me.dogs_note: The Beehive is named on this card AND is one of the six trails Acadia closes to dogs — the iron-rung climb. Everything else here is open to the dog, including Cadillac South Ridge and Gorham Mountain.

trails.name: Cadillac Mountain South Ridge Trail
trails.was: Cadillac Mountain South Ridge Trail — no url
trails.note_source: Dogs permitted — Acadia allows them on most trails, and this is one of them.

trails.name: Beehive Trail
trails.was: Beehive Trail — no url
trails.note_source: The iron-rung climb from Sand Beach. One of only six Acadia trails CLOSED to dogs. AllTrails indexes it as a point of interest and inside a combined Precipice loop that is itself marked CLOSED; no clean standalone listing surfaced.

other_links.label: Earth Trekkers — The Beehive Trail guide
other_links.note: Source of the distance, gain and difficulty here: 1.4 mi loop, 450 ft, strenuous.

other_links.label: Your NP Guide — Beehive Trail
other_links.note: 450–520 ft of gain over 1.4–1.9 mi, with hands-on scrambling on iron rungs.

trails.stats_note: The stats here are from trail guides, not AllTrails — the AllTrails result published only its review count. This is an iron-rung climb with steep cliff drop-offs beside the trail; not a dog route and not a route to reverse in a queue.

trails.name: Gorham Mountain Trail
trails.was: Gorham Mountain Trail — no url
trails.note_source: No direct listing url surfaced in search. Name kept; no constructed slug.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Gorham Mountain Loop
other_links.note: The far busier listing at 9,826 reviews — the loop version off the Park Loop Road.

trails.stats_note: AllTrails published no distance or grade for either listing in search. Secondary sources put the round trip at about 3.5 mi with roughly 525 ft of gain, moderate. The Cadillac Cliffs variant on the way up is harder than the main line.

trails.name: Jordan Pond Path
trails.was: Jordan Pond Path — no url
trails.note_source: No direct listing url surfaced in search. Name kept; no constructed slug.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Jordan Pond Path and South Bubble
other_links.note: 3.6 mi loop rated challenging, 3,983 reviews — the pond circuit plus the climb up South Bubble.

trails.stats_note: The 3.3 mi comes from several independent guides that agree; AllTrails' own snippet gave only the review count. Flat on the east side, rough plank-and-rock on the west.

trails.name: Ocean Path
trails.was: Ocean Path (Ocean Trail) — no url
trails.note_source: No direct listing url surfaced in search. Name kept; no constructed slug.
trails.stats_note: AllTrails published no distance in search; independent GPS tracks give 4.2–4.5 mi round trip with 499–577 ft of cumulative gain along the shore between Sand Beach and Otter Point. The southern end opens onto exposed rock above the sea stacks. The slug carries a '--2' suffix.

offroad.name: Seal Cove Road
offroad.distance: NPS gives 2.17 miles, from the park boundary in Southwest Harbor to State Route 102; onX measures its own track at 2.7 mi, probably including connectors. Use the NPS figure.
offroad.difficulty: NPS publishes no scale; it described spring conditions as "Deep ruts, exposed culverts, and downed wood." onX rates it 2 (Easy).
offroad.season: Acadia's gravel roads close to motor vehicles around November 15 and reopen by May 15, weather and conditions permitting.
offroad.note: NPS opens this one first of the three west-side fire roads each spring, so it is the safest bet at the shoulders. Runs from Tremont Road at the west end to Main Street at the east, giving access to several trailheads plus Western Mountain Road. Recent reports call it washboarded with no significant views — the quiet is the point, not the scenery.

offroad.name: Western Mountain Road
offroad.distance: NPS: 3.32 miles including connecting unpaved roads (onX independently measures 3.3 mi)
offroad.difficulty: onX rates it 2 (Easy) — non-technical unless after heavy rain or in winter
offroad.season: Closes around November 15, reopens by May 15 weather permitting. NPS has published delayed spring openings for this road specifically after winter freeze-thaw damage, opening it only after Seal Cove Road.
offroad.note: NPS extent is from the park boundary west of the Worcester landfill to Seal Cove Pond. These are multi-purpose roads with walkers and cyclists as well as cars, so drive them accordingly. A loop from the Bald Mountain parking area via Western Mountain Road to Seal Cove Road runs roughly 3.2 miles. Gravel forestry surface with soft sand spots that turn to mud after heavy rain, and not always wide enough for two vehicles to pass.

offroad.name: Long Pond Fire Road
offroad.distance: 4.2 mi
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — non-technical unless after heavy rain or during winter
offroad.season: NPS: on November 15, gravel roads in the park close to motor vehicle traffic, including Seal Cove Road, Western Mountain Roads and the Long Pond Fire Road. Reopened by May 15, weather and conditions permitting.
offroad.note: One of the few dirt roads in Acadia where you get away from the crowds. Starts at Tremont Road and reaches several trailheads plus a good swimming spot on Long Pond, Hodgdon Pond and Seal Cove Pond. Gravel forestry road with soft sand that turns muddy after rain; not always wide enough for two vehicles. Park entrance pass required. On the winter snowmobile question, the park's unplowed fire roads are generally open to snowmobiles, but no authority page names this road specifically — 36 CFR 7.56 designates the Long Pond TRUCK Road, which is a different road.

offroad.name: Donnell Pond
offroad.distance: 3.3 mi
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — a gravel road with some rough washed-out areas, getting progressively rougher
offroad.season: Best spring, summer, fall. Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands publishes no gate dates but warns that many access roads are not plowed in winter unless timber harvesting is under way.
offroad.note: Mostly wide open, though some spur roads narrow considerably, and sections double as snowmobile trail in winter. Camping is allowed but campfires are prohibited outside established sites. A damaged bridge has turned people around partway, with the road continuing beyond it. The state authority for the unit is Maine BPL's Donnell Pond Public Reserved Land page, which names Black Mountain Road and Dynamite Brook Rd but publishes no road condition detail — Eastern Public Lands Office (207) 941-4412. Caveat: the listing's start point sits toward the Tunk Lake end, so which of the unit's gravel roads this actually is cannot be confirmed.

offroad.name: Narraguagus Lake
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — mostly gravel with a few muddy spots, easily driven in 2WD or 4WD
offroad.season: Best spring, summer, fall. No gate dates published, and probably none exist to find.
offroad.note: This is the start of a much larger northward system signed as Trail 501, reaching genuinely remote country and ending below a large group of wind turbines before continuing to South Spectacle Pond Road — so it is as long as you want it to be. Recent reports mention construction vehicles and heavy traffic near the turbines. Honest limit: no authority — Maine BPL, IF&W, land trust or town — confirms a road here by name, and it is most likely private timberland under permissive access, which is why no published gate dates exist.

bar-harbor-me.dogs_source_quote: There are 100 miles (161 km) of hiking trails and 45 miles (72 km) of carriage roads in the park where pets are permitted.

Camden & Rockland harbor towns.entity: Camden and Rockland, the two mid-coast harbour towns.

Drive the Mount Battie Auto Road.entity: The Mount Battie Auto Road in Camden Hills State Park. It has no article; the park article documents Mount Battie and records the auto road's completion in 1965.

Hike to Maiden Cliff.entity: The Maiden Cliff Trail in Camden Hills State Park, documented in the park article along with the monument to Elenora French.

Walk the Rockland Breakwater.entity: The Rockland Harbor breakwater and the 1902 light at its end.

Use Lake St. George itself.entity: Lake St. George State Park in Liberty, Maine, where the coach is parked.

links.label: Wikipedia — Lake St. George State Park

offroad.name: Frye Mountain - High Ridge to Getchell
offroad.distance: 6.3 mi listed; just over 8 miles as driven, including a 3-mile out-and-back spur to a second cemetery
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — gravel roads, mostly wide enough for two vehicles to pass
offroad.season: Best spring, summer, fall. Maine IF&W closes WMA roads seasonally after the firearm deer season ends, to protect the road infrastructure — but publishes no calendar date for it, tying the closure to the end of the season instead. Do not assume a date; this one needs a call.
offroad.note: A west-to-east crossing of the Frye Mountain State Game Management Area, passing Carter Cemetery. A few sections at lower elevations can flood. The WMA is about 5,200 acres across Knox, Montville and Morrill in Waldo County; IF&W has no dedicated page for it, so the Lands Management Program page is the best official source available.

offroad.name: Bald Mountain Trail
offroad.distance: 1.3 mi
offroad.difficulty: 3 (Easy) — one vehicle wide and entirely uphill, with sections around 25-degree incline, washouts, loose rock, and ledges near the summit
offroad.season: Best spring, summer, fall; no gate dates published.
offroad.note: Location flag: this listing sits at 44.831, -68.482, in inland Hancock County — 50-odd miles northeast of Camden and much closer to the Bar Harbor/Ellsworth stop, so it may be filed under the wrong stop. It is genuinely a driving route, not a hiking listing. The Camden-area Bald Mountain is a Coastal Mountains Land Trust preserve on Barnestown Road whose published activities are hiking, birding and snowshoeing, with no evidence of a drivable summit road — so if the Camden mountain was meant, there is nothing to link. Summit is shared with a hiking trail; a few snowmobile side trails off it are not 4x4 friendly.

offroad.name: Quarry Road Trail
offroad.distance: 2.4 mi
offroad.difficulty: 3 (Easy) — two steep inclines and some rocky terrain
offroad.note: Three problems, any one of which is disqualifying. It is in Waterville — the trailhead is behind the Home Depot — roughly 45 miles inland from Camden, so it is on the wrong stop. It is reported Permanently Closed with an official closed sign, by three separate people between Oct 2024 and Aug 2025. And its access classes are single track, 50-inch and 60-inch only, with no full-width class, so it is an ATV/UTV trail the pickup does not fit. Recommend dropping it rather than linking it.

trails.name: Mount Battie Trail / Nature Trail

other_links.label: AllTrails — Mount Battie via Nature Trail Trailhead
other_links.note: The Nature Trail half of this entry: 2.8 mi out-and-back with 639 ft of gain — longer but far gentler than the direct Mount Battie Trail.

trails.stats_note: The card entry names two ways up and AllTrails lists them separately. The direct Mount Battie Trail is short and steep — 1.2 mi and rated challenging; the Nature Trail approach is 2.8 mi at an easier grade.

camden-me.dogs: All four are fine. Maine's Bureau of Parks and Lands allows leashed pets throughout its parks and publishes no trail closure at Camden Hills; the only blanket ban is on state park beaches from 1 April to 30 September, which this late-October stay clears anyway.
camden-me.dogs_source_quote: Pets must be on a leash under the physical control of the pet handler and must not be left unattended.

scenicDrives_patch.name: US Route 1 Midcoast Maine (Rockland-Camden-Belfast)
scenicDrives_patch.note: Maine Office of Tourism's regional page, fetched and confirmed to exist, covering Belfast, Camden and Rockland. It is a destination page, not a route page — it publishes no Route 1 mileage, no drive description and no seasonal notes, so none is recorded here. No stretch of US-1 through the Midcoast carries a Maine Scenic Byway designation; searching returned only commercial roundups for this corridor. Maine's MidCoast & Islands regional DMO also runs a route planner at mainesmidcoast.com/route-planner/ if a stop-by-stop itinerary is wanted.

Climb Monument Mountain.entity: The quartzite ridge at Great Barrington and Stockbridge, and the Trustees reservation on it. The bare title 'Monument Mountain' is a set-index page covering several summits including one in Indiana, so the disambiguated Berkshire County article is used.

Go north to North Adams and the Mohawk T.entity: North Adams and the Mohawk Trail across northern Massachusetts.

Use October Mountain State Forest as a w.entity: October Mountain State Forest, the largest state forest in Massachusetts.

offroad.name: Country Road
offroad.distance: 1.8 mi
offroad.difficulty: 1 (Easy) — well-maintained gravel road
offroad.season: Not maintained in winter. October Mountain State Forest is open sunrise to one half-hour after sunset.
offroad.note: This is the main entrance road into October Mountain State Forest, the largest state forest in Massachusetts at 16,500 acres, and it gives access to several areas of the park with views over the wetlands to the west. Worth knowing the forest's other reputation: DCR states the OHV trails at October Mountain are challenging and only suitable for the intermediate to expert rider — that is a different trail set from this road.

offroad.name: Beartown Mountain Road
offroad.distance: 3.2 mi
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — unmaintained, with mildly stepped sections where the gravel thins and plenty of holes and ruts that fill with runoff
offroad.season: DCR: Beartown State Forest OHV season is open May 1st to the last Sunday in November, weather permitting; park hours sunrise to sunset. A late-October visit is inside that window.
offroad.note: Begins at Route 102 at an unlocked gate and runs south into the park, with remnants of old pavement still showing before the gravel starts about 2 miles in. Crosses the Appalachian Trail 0.2 mi from the end and finishes in a residential dirt lot.

offroad.name: Mount Wilcox Road
offroad.distance: 4 mi listed; the full loop is 4.3 miles
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — two cars wide in places, soft shoulders, steeper climbs on loose gravel; unmaintained after snow
offroad.season: Same DCR Beartown window: OHV season May 1st to the last Sunday in November, weather permitting.
offroad.note: The main loop through Beartown State Forest, starting and ending off Benedict Pond Road and climbing from 1,600 to 2,100 ft. A short spur breaks off halfway to the summit, but the fire tower there is gated with no public access.

offroad.name: Ashley Lake Road
offroad.distance: 2.3 mi
offroad.difficulty: 3 (Easy) — a very bumpy road with occasional mud holes and small ledges that deepen in wet seasons
offroad.season: Best spring, summer, fall.
offroad.note: Currently obstructed, and this is the live problem: a report of 26 Jul 2026 describes a massive downed tree about 500 feet in from the south that ATVs and dirt bikes can pass but full-size vehicles cannot, and 2025 reports describe another tree plus heavy overgrowth that will stripe a full-size truck. Part of the route is a corduroy road — logs laid across the direction of travel — which is very rough. It runs through October Mountain State Forest past Ashley Lake, Sandwash Reservoir, Clapp Pond and Mud Pond, and the north end exits at a gate on Washington Mountain Road that has turned people around. No Pittsfield water-department access restriction could be sourced either way.

offroad.name: Greylock Road
offroad.distance: 2.9 mi
offroad.difficulty: 1 (Easy) — no harder than many dirt roads, but not frequently maintained, so fallen trees often block it
offroad.season: onX: open June through October only. For context, DCR's separate Mount Greylock Auto Roads ran May 16 to October 30 in 2026 — so a 27 October arrival clears both, but only by about three days and only weather permitting.
offroad.note: Resolved: this is a separate gravel road, NOT one of DCR's paved Notch/Rockwell/Summit auto roads — it is a quieter alternative ascent that eventually meets the paved main road and continues to the peak. Two status reports describe downed trees worth turning back for, so the gate date is not the only thing that can stop you. Note DCR's new rule that vehicles over 22 feet are prohibited on the Greylock Auto Roads and to the summit; the pickup is unaffected.

not_a_trail.entry: Summit / Bascom Lodge area walk (Mount Greylock)
not_a_trail.problem: Not a trail — it is the summit plateau of Mount Greylock, reached by Notch Road or Rockwell Road, with Bascom Lodge and the Veterans War Memorial Tower on it. No named short walk exists at the summit itself. The nearest named path is the Overlook Trail, which AllTrails describes as a connector between the Hopper Trail and the summit and which other sources give as 3.2 mi around the south and west sides — a different and much longer outing than an area stroll.

berkshires-ma.dogs: All four take leashed dogs. DCR's rule for Mount Greylock State Reservation is "Pets must be on a leash and attended at all times" with no trail closures, and the Trustees of Reservations require the same at Monument Mountain. mass.gov refuses automated fetching, so the DCR wording was read from the search index entry for its own page rather than the page itself.
berkshires-ma.dogs_source_quote: Pets must be on a leash and attended at all times.

Litchfield's historic green.entity: The green at the core of the Litchfield Historic District, a National Historic Landmark district in Litchfield, Connecticut.

Walk the trails at White Memorial.entity: The White Memorial Foundation's ~4,000 acres of trails at Litchfield, Connecticut.

Circle Lake Waramaug.entity: Lake Waramaug in Kent, Warren and Washington, Litchfield County, Connecticut.

Spend an afternoon on the Litchfield gre.entity: The same Litchfield green and historic district.

offroad.name: Del Reeves & North Mulford Roads
offroad.distance: 5 mi
offroad.difficulty: 1 (Easy) — nothing technical, a few bumps and the occasional mud hole after rain
offroad.season: Best time listed as spring, summer, fall AND winter — the only route in this set rated for all four, with a December snow run reported Open.
offroad.note: Forest correction that matters for planning: this is Meshomasic State Forest in Portland, not Naugatuck — roughly 35 to 45 miles east, across the Connecticut River, so it cannot be run from the same base as Cold Springs Road. Unmaintained, mostly dirt with some gravel. Numerous pull-offs, and one highlight is an old Nike missile site. The best-evidenced of the four, with status reports running through Aug 2026 and all reporting Open.

offroad.name: Del Reeves Road
offroad.distance: 3.2 mi
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — a simple forest road, straightforward to navigate
offroad.season: Best spring, summer, fall. Graded state forest road, closed at sunset.
offroad.note: Also Meshomasic State Forest in Portland, not Naugatuck — same 35-to-45-mile eastward correction as the linked version above. Mostly dirt with a few gravel sections; doable in nearly any vehicle, but the ruts deepen and it turns muddy after rain. Several good pull-offs along it. Land owner of record is Connecticut DEEP.

offroad.name: Cold Springs Road
offroad.distance: 0.8 mi
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — unmaintained, weather-sensitive, mostly one vehicle wide with multiple deep ruts and small off-camber sections
offroad.season: Best summer and fall.
offroad.note: The only one of the four that really is in Naugatuck State Forest. Runs directly alongside an active railroad, and ends at the Spruce Brook Trail parking area. A minimum of 12 inches of ground clearance is recommended for the ruts and mud holes. Worth a call to CT DEEP Forestry first: the DEEP West Block map carries the notice that the roads and trails in that block are multi-use non-motorized except snowmobiles, and since this road ends at a West Block trailhead the likeliest reading is that it is an approach road with the non-motorized rule applying beyond the parking area — but DEEP does not say so, and none of these four road names appears on either Naugatuck map.

offroad.name: Filley Road
offroad.distance: 1.8 mi
offroad.difficulty: 1 (Easy) — very simple dirt and gravel; proper throttle control needed to avoid slipping in 2WD
offroad.season: Best spring, summer, fall and winter.
offroad.note: Third forest, third correction: this is Cockaponset State Forest, not Naugatuck. It serves as an entrance to the Cockaponset trail system and opens onto further trails in the forest — worth taking as a way in rather than as a destination in itself.

litchfield-hills-ct.dogs: All four take leashed dogs. CT DEEP permits pets on a leash across state parks and forests — Kent Falls and Macedonia Brook both list "Yes, on leash" for picnic areas and hiking trails, and Mohawk the same. White Memorial is private land trust ground and its rule is a leash at all times.
litchfield-hills-ct.dogs_source_quote: Pets on a leash are permitted in most state parks and forests, but not allowed in buildings, swimming areas, or state park campgrounds.

scenicDrives_patch.name: South Litchfield Hills Scenic Drive
scenicDrives_patch.note: No route by this name exists. Connecticut designates scenic roads formally — "Connecticut has over the past several years designated several sections of its rural two-lane highways as Scenic Roads" — and CTDOT publishes the designated segments on this interactive map, which is the authority for which Litchfield-area roads actually carry the designation. Searching the byway and tourism listings returned a "Litchfield Hills Scenic Byway", a "Litchfield Hills Loop Drive" and a "Litchfield Hills Scenic Loop" from third-party sites, but nothing under the card's name and no official route bearing it. Recorded as unlisted rather than matched to a differently-named loop.

Rhinebeck's historic village.entity: The village of Rhinebeck, New York.

Catskill foothills color drives.entity: The Catskill Mountains west of the river.

FDR's Springwood and the first president.entity: Springwood, FDR's birthplace at Hyde Park, and the FDR Presidential Library — the first presidential library.

Wikipedia — Franklin D. Roosevelt Presidential Library and Museum

Walk the Walkway Over the Hudson.entity: The Walkway over the Hudson state historic park on the old Poughkeepsie railroad bridge.

Olana — Frederic Church's Persian villa.entity: Olana, Frederic Edwin Church's Persian-influenced house above the Hudson at Greenport.

Minnewaska carriage roads on the Shawang.entity: The carriage roads in Minnewaska State Park Preserve on the Shawangunk Ridge.

Riverside walking at Mills Norrie, six m.entity: Mills-Norrie State Park at Hyde Park — the collective name for Margaret Lewis Norrie State Park and the adjoining Ogden Mills & Ruth Livingston Mills State Park, as the Norrie article states.

Wikipedia — Ogden Mills & Ruth Livingston Mills State Park

trails.name: Storm King Mountain via Stillman Trail

other_links.label: AllTrails — Stillman Trail
other_links.note: The Stillman on its own, 60 reviews — from a small trailhead on Mountain Road, wide at first then singletrack, over the tops of Storm King and Butter Hill.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Storm King Mountain via Storm King Highway
other_links.note: Alternative start from the Route 218 pull-off, 105 reviews.

trails.stats_note: The popular route is the loop above — it parks at the Route 9W picnic area and climbs the Stillman over the summit. AllTrails published no stats in search; an independent GPS track gives the loop as 2.4 mi with 541 ft of gain. The Stillman Trail is also indexed separately, but with only 60 reviews.

hudson-valley-ny.dogs: The two NPS sites are explicitly open to pets on their trails — that covers the FDR loops, the Hyde Trail out to Bard Rock and the Vanderbilt grounds — and the Walkway takes leashed dogs on the deck, though only service animals in the elevator. Storm King is the gap: NY State Parks publishes no pet policy on its Storm King page, and its own FAQ says the policy lives on the individual park page.
hudson-valley-ny.dogs_source_quote: Much of the Home of Franklin D. Roosevelt National Historic Site is accessible to pets—the developed areas, some of the gardens, and our trails.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Route 9W along the Hudson
scenicDrives_patch.note: Chronogram's Route 9W road trip: the route runs the Hudson's west bank through Rockland, Orange, Ulster and Greene counties, passing Nyack, Bear Mountain, West Point, Newburgh, Highland, Kingston, Saugerties and Catskill, and "was the primary route for car travel between New York City and Albany west of the Hudson River" before the Thruway. No total mileage is published for the drive on that page. Note that the Palisades Scenic Byway, which comes up alongside 9W in searches, is a different road — it is the Palisades Interstate Parkway and Henry Hudson Drive, not 9W.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Storm King Highway (NY-218)
scenicDrives_patch.distance: 3-mile scenic segment of NY-218; a 5.5-mile stretch was the closure length
scenicDrives_patch.note: New York State's own release on the September 13, 2024 reopening. This road has a demonstrated habit of going away: more than eight inches of rain on July 9-10, 2023 "caused a portion of State Route 218 to collapse down the mountainside", taking out a nearly 300-foot-wide swath and closing it for about fourteen months; the rebuild added an oversized box culvert and an armored embankment rated for a 500-year event. Rockfall has closed it in other years too. No weight or vehicle restriction is stated in the release, and no winter-maintenance policy is published — worth a same-week check of NYSDOT status before driving out, rather than a season field this entry cannot source.

Delaware Water Gap National Recreation A.entity: Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area

Climb Mount Tammany from Dunnfield Creek.entity: Mount Tammany, the 1,526 ft Kittatinny peak forming the New Jersey side of the Gap. Dunnfield Creek, the trailhead, has no article and is not documented in the Tammany article, so only the mountain is linked.

links.label: Wikipedia — Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area

Dingmans Falls boardwalk.entity: Dingmans Falls, the 130 ft fall at the north end of the recreation area; its title redirects to the Delaware Water Gap waterfalls list, which describes it.

links.label: Wikipedia — List of waterfalls in the Delaware Water Gap

Raymondskill Falls.entity: Raymondskill Falls on Raymondskill Creek, Pike County — the tallest in Pennsylvania; same redirect target, described in the list.

links.label: Wikipedia — List of waterfalls in the Delaware Water Gap

offroad.name: Big Pocono State Park summit road
offroad.season: Park closed early December, reopens the first week of April; sunrise to sunset when open
offroad.note: DCNR warns of steep grades and says not to attempt the drive with a trailer in tow. It also states municipal road maintenance is not provided on the access roadway and that seasonal closures of it will occur, so the April reopening is a target rather than a promise. DCNR publishes no length for the summit loop; the 1.4-mile figure that circulates is not on the official page and is not recorded here.

offroad.name: Old Mine Road, NJ side north of Millbrook Village
offroad.note: NPS treats this as a windshield tour of a roughly 250-year-old route and notes the original unpaved roadbed survives on foot at spots such as the Van Campen Inn and Hamilton Ridge near Millbrook. The park publishes no mileage, no surface breakdown and no seasonal closure for the drive itself; the page directs road-condition questions to the park at the number it lists.

trails.name: Bushkill Falls Trail

other_links.label: Bushkill Falls (operator)
other_links.note: Bushkill Falls is privately operated and gated; four colour-coded trails, paid admission. The Red Trail is the full eight-waterfall circuit and the one AllTrails indexes.

delaware-water-gap-pa.dogs_source_quote: Pets are allowed almost everywhere in the park. Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area encompasses more than 70,000 acres and has over 150 miles of trails, most of which are pet-friendly.

Drive the battlefield auto tour in the t.entity: The auto tour through Gettysburg National Military Park.

Little Round Top and Devil's Den on foot.entity: The two second-day positions on the Union left. 'Devil's Den' resolves to the Gettysburg boulder field on Houck's Ridge, confirmed by the article's own text.

Caledonia's iron furnace, on your doorst.entity: The Caledonia Furnace, Thaddeus Stevens' ironworks. No separate article; Caledonia State Park is named for the furnace and documents Stevens' 1837 ownership.

Pine Grove Furnace and the Appalachian T.entity: Pine Grove Furnace State Park and the Appalachian Trail Museum inside it.

Gettysburg town and the Lincoln connecti.entity: Gettysburg and Lincoln's Gettysburg Address, delivered there in November 1863.

offroad.name: Caledonia to Pine Grove Furnace forest roads

offroad.note: DCNR's forest page confirms the authority and links a Michaux State Forest Recreation Guide PDF, but publishes nothing about which roads are open, gated or seasonally closed. trails.stats_note: AllTrails has a point-of-interest page for Little Round Top and says two trails reach it, but no trail listing carries the name. NPS publishes no single length for the summit paths. Confirmed to exist by the National Park Service; recorded unlisted rather than linked to a route that is not the same walk.

gettysburg-pa.dogs: Gettysburg NMP welcomes leashed dogs everywhere on the battlefield grounds and trails; only park buildings, the visitor center and the National Cemetery are closed to them.
gettysburg-pa.dogs_source_quote: Pets must be restrained on a leash at all times while in the park.

Appalachian Trail access.entity: The Appalachian Trail itself, which runs straight through Harpers Ferry; the AT article's West Virginia section covers this stretch.

Lower Town, the Stone Steps and Jefferso.entity: Harpers Ferry's Lower Town Historic District and the Jefferson Rock outcrop above it. The park article documents the Lower Town district and lists Jefferson Rock; Jefferson Rock has its own article. The Stone Steps (the cut-rock stair up to the rock) have no article and are not named in either.

links.label: Wikipedia — Harpers Ferry National Historical Park

Maryland Heights.entity: The cliff across the Potomac in Maryland, not Maryland Heights, Missouri (which is what the bare title resolves to). The Elk Ridge article states the ridge's southern end, part of Harpers Ferry NHP, is known as Maryland Heights; the park article documents the Maryland Heights section.

links.label: Wikipedia — Harpers Ferry National Historical Park

Appalachian Trail Conservancy headquarte.entity: The ATC, whose headquarters the article places in Harpers Ferry, West Virginia.

C&O Canal towpath.entity: The Chesapeake and Ohio Canal towpath opposite Harpers Ferry; the park article covers the towpath trail and its Harpers Ferry section.

trails.name: Weverton Cliffs (Appalachian Trail)

other_links.label: Appalachian Trail Conservancy
other_links.note: ATC's own hike page, with the trailhead directions: from US 340 take MD 67 North to the first right at Weverton Cliff Rd; large paved lot on the right.

trails.stats_note: 1.7 mi / 570 ft / 4.8 from 5,765 reviews are AllTrails' own figures via its Weverton Cliffs point-of-interest page; the trail listing title showed 5,817 reviews in a later crawl, so the count is still climbing. Average 1–1.5 hr. The slug carries a --3 suffix — it is not derivable from the name.

harpers-ferry-wv.dogs: Leashed dogs are permitted throughout Harpers Ferry NHP including the Maryland Heights climb, and on the C&O Canal towpath and the Appalachian Trail up to Weverton Cliffs.
harpers-ferry-wv.dogs_source_quote: Pets must be kept on a six-foot leash at all times while visiting any area of the park.

scenicDrives_patch.name: US-340 through the Potomac/Shenandoah Water Gap
scenicDrives_patch.note: NPS: "Harpers Ferry NHP's Visitor Center is located along US Route 340 in West Virginia", 8 miles east of Charles Town, WV and 20 miles southwest of Frederick, MD. The park's own directions run US 340 in from three sides — north from Charles Town, south from Frederick, and north from Front Royal via Shenandoah NP. The directions page carries no description of the gap itself, no distances for the scenic stretch and no seasonal conditions; the park's separate Scenic Vistas page (home.nps.gov/hafe/learn/nature/scenicvistas.htm) is where the water-gap view is described. Nothing published on either page about winter driving, so no season field is claimed.

Skyline Drive.entity: The 105-mile parkway through Shenandoah National Park in Virginia — verified as the Virginia road, not another Skyline Drive.

Staunton's historic downtown.entity: Downtown Staunton, listed as the Beverley Historic District (131 contributing buildings in downtown Staunton).

Walk the Blue Ridge Tunnel.entity: Claudius Crozet's Blue Ridge (Crozet) Tunnel at Rockfish Gap, reopened in 2020 as a walking trail.

Humpback Rocks.entity: The greenstone outcrop on Humpback Mountain at Blue Ridge Parkway milepost 5.8 in Augusta/Nelson County, Virginia. NOTE: the title 'Humpback Rocks' resolves to rocks off South Georgia in the South Atlantic; the Virginia formation is at 'Humpback Rock'.

Downtown Staunton and the Blackfriars Pl.entity: Downtown Staunton (Beverley Historic District) and the Blackfriars Playhouse, which redirects to its operator, the American Shakespeare Center.

Woodrow Wilson Presidential Library and.entity: The Woodrow Wilson Presidential Library and Museum in Staunton, which contains the birthplace Manse.

Sherando Lake and Grand Caverns as weath.entity: Grand Caverns at Grottoes, Virginia, and Sherando Lake. Sherando Lake has no article; the Blue Ridge Parkway article documents it by name at milepost 16 as a recreation area in George Washington National Forest 4.5 miles from the parkway.

staunton-va.dogs: Shenandoah allows leashed dogs on most of its trails, but both trails on this card — Stony Man and every Old Rag route — are on the park's short prohibited list.
staunton-va.dogs_note: Two of this stop's trails are on Shenandoah's short prohibited list — Stony Man's blue-blazed summit portion and the Old Rag trails (Ridge Access, Ridge, Saddle). Everything ELSE in the park is open to the dog, which still makes this one of the best stops on the trip for walking together; it is just that both trails currently named here happen to be exceptions. Worth adding dog-legal Shenandoah trails to this card.

offroad.name: George Washington NF gravel roads, North River / Todd Lake district
offroad.season: Todd Lake Recreation Area open mid-May to late October
offroad.note: Forest Service directions run 1.1 miles on SR 718 (Stokesville Road) to the FR 95 / FR 101 junction, then 3.1 miles on FR 95 (North River Road) to Todd Lake. The page does not state whether FR 95 is gravel or paved and publishes no vehicle restriction. FR 95 is also the lower end of the North River Trail, which climbs to FR 85 (Shenandoah Mountain Road) — the same road as the Reddish Knob route below, so the two can be linked.

offroad.name: Reddish Knob road (FR 85 from Briery Branch, west of Harrisonburg)
offroad.difficulty: onX rating 2 (Easy) — "easy dirt and gravel trail with just a few rutted and rocky spots"
offroad.season: onX lists spring, summer, fall and winter
offroad.note: onX rates this for high-clearance, full-width vehicles and puts the observation point at 4,397 ft. The adjoining Flagpole Knob route meets it at Briery Branch Gap and has its own onX listing at 12.8 miles, also difficulty 2 — the pair make one long day if the weather holds. Note the two are not equivalent: Flagpole's FR 85 approach is reported as much rougher than the Reddish Knob asphalt spur.

trails.name: Stony Man Trail

Historic downtown Lexington.entity: The Lexington Historic District, the NRHP district covering the town's historic core.

Natural Bridge.entity: The 215-ft natural limestone arch in Rockbridge County, Virginia.

Devils Marbleyard.entity: The boulder field on Bluff Mountain. It has no article of its own; the James River Face Wilderness article names 'the Devils Marbleyard' as a rock outcrop within the wilderness.

Lexington's historic core on foot.entity: Same Lexington Historic District, walked rather than driven.

Blue Ridge Parkway from the James River.entity: The Parkway's northern Virginia section and the James River it crosses at milepost 63.8, both documented in the Parkway article.

Buena Vista and the Maury River valley.entity: The city of Buena Vista, Virginia and the Maury River, which the river article traces past Lexington and Buena Vista in Rockbridge County.

lexington-va.authority: National Park Service — Shenandoah / Blue Ridge Parkway
lexington-va.dogs: Natural Bridge State Park is a Virginia state park, and leashed dogs are allowed on all of its trails including Cedar Creek under the arch.

offroad.name: George Washington & Jefferson NF gravel roads, North Mountain west of Lexington
offroad.note: Unlisted. No Forest Service page and no off-road database covers this road network as a named route. The forest's Motor Vehicle Use Map is the only authority on which of these roads are open and to which vehicle class, and GWJNF publishes one forest-wide MVUM rather than per-district ones — so plan from the MVUM, not from a route listing.
offroad.season: GWJNF seasonal roads: "Many seasonal roads are closed during the freeze-thaw of winter to protect roads surfaces from damage, typically closing on January 10 and reopening April 1." The stop arrives 2 Dec 2028 for 4 nights, so it clears the gate date by about five weeks — but only just, and the Forest states opening and closing dates vary by road, with some roads separately gated for wildlife.

offroad.name: George Washington National Forest roads (near Natural Bridge, off Rt. 812)
offroad.note: Unlisted, same situation as North Mountain: the Forest Service publishes district topographic maps and a single forest-wide MVUM, but no page for this road network and no named route in any off-road database. The MVUM carries the vehicle-class and seasonal designations for each road.
offroad.season: Same GWJNF winter policy — seasonal roads typically close January 10 and reopen April 1, dates varying by road. A 2 Dec arrival is ahead of it.

offroad.name: James River Face Wilderness access roads (Belfast Trail / Petites Gap)

The page grades the Belfast Trail itself Moderate to Difficult over 2.3 miles — that is the walk to the Devil's Marbleyard boulder field, not the drive. The Forest Service says nothing about the road's surface or its FS 35 designation, so no surface claim is recorded.

Highest-rated trail in Natural Bridge State Park.

offroad.name: Cunard river access road
offroad.season: Closed every November through March, from the Brooklyn Mine Trail parking lot down to the river; open April to October. NPS says this pattern continues through 2027.
offroad.note: This is the annual winter closure for road and drainage work, not weather. When open, NPS reports the lower sections are gravel and there are one-lane stretches that cause delays. The closure takes out vehicle, bike and pedestrian access to the Cunard river access, the angler's access and Brooklyn campground together. The park's closures page was last updated 6 Aug 2026 — check it again before the stop.

offroad.name: Fayette Station Road (CR 82)
offroad.distance: 8 mi
offroad.season: No seasonal closure published
offroad.note: One-way, and the binding restriction is height not length: NPS states vehicles over 12 ft tall cannot complete the route because of the clearance under a railroad bridge, and does not recommend large vehicles, RVs or trailers on the hairpins. Allow 30–45 minutes without stops. The road passes under the New River Gorge Bridge three times.

offroad.name: Keeneys Creek Road down to Nuttallburg
offroad.distance: about 4 mi — NPS gives ~3.5 mi to the wayside exhibit and 0.5 mi more to the Nuttallburg parking area
offroad.note: NPS calls it narrow, winding and steep, part paved and part gravel, with much of it single lane so drivers have to pull off to let others by. Trailers, RVs and motorhomes are specifically advised against — limited parking and difficult to turn around at the bottom. Separate from the road, the Keeney's Creek Rail Trail is closed above the Conveyor Trail junction for flood damage.

offroad.name: WV 25 to Thurmond
offroad.distance: 7 mi from the Glen Jean exit off US 19
offroad.note: The NPS directions page gives the seven miles but publishes no surface or vehicle guidance for WV 25 — the 'narrow, winding, not recommended for RVs or trailers' description that circulates is not on an NPS page that could be opened here, so it is not recorded as fact. Worth knowing separately: the Rend Trail, which starts at Thurmond, is closed from both trailheads until roughly December 2027 per the park's road and trail closures page.

new-river-gorge-wv.dogs: New River Gorge is one of the most dog-open parks on the whole route — the NPS states plainly that leashed pets are allowed on every trail in the park.
new-river-gorge-wv.dogs_source_quote: Pets are allowed on all trails at New River Gorge National Park and Preserve.

Floyd Country Store Jamboree.entity: The Floyd Country Store's Friday Night Jamboree. The store has no article; the Floyd, Virginia article documents the Jamboree by name in its Arts and culture section.

Blue Ridge Parkway access (truck touring.entity: The Blue Ridge Parkway, which passes just south of Floyd.

Friday Night Jamboree at the Floyd Count.entity: Same Friday Night Jamboree, documented by name in the Floyd, Virginia article.

Rock Castle Gorge at Rocky Knob.entity: Rock Castle Gorge in the Rocky Knob Recreation Area at Parkway mileposts 167–174; the recreation-area article names the gorge and its National Recreation Trail.

Winery run along the Parkway.entity: The Blue Ridge Parkway itself, as the touring route. Linked for the road that is named; the Parkway article does not document wineries, so this is a link to the Parkway, not to the wineries.

Day trip to Roanoke.entity: The city of Roanoke, Virginia, the largest city on the Parkway.

The walk itself is the Buffalo Mountain Trail, which AllTrails describes as following the Oak and Barrens Loop Trail to the highest point in Floyd County; 409 reviews, no star rating or distance in any indexed snippet. Summit elevation 3,971 ft per third-party guides. No length published by Virginia DCR that could be sourced this pass.

floyd-va.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed on all the Blue Ridge Parkway trails here; Buffalo Mountain Natural Area Preserve publishes no pet rule at all, so treat it as unknown until DCR Natural Heritage is phoned.
floyd-va.dogs_source_quote: Dogs are allowed on trails, but must be on a leash.

Blowing Rock village.entity: The town of Blowing Rock, North Carolina.

Moses Cone Manor carriage roads — but ch.entity: Flat Top Manor and its carriage trails in Moses H. Cone Memorial Park; the park article names the manor and its 25 miles of carriage trails.

links.label: Wikipedia — Moses H. Cone Memorial Park

Ski at Beech or Sugar Mountain.entity: Beech Mountain (skiing and Beech Mountain Resort documented in the mountain article) and the village of Sugar Mountain, whose article places it next to Sugar Mountain Ski Area. Neither resort has its own article.

Blowing Rock and Tweetsie at Christmas.entity: The town of Blowing Rock and the Tweetsie Railroad theme park, which the town article names as a local attraction.

offroad.name: Brown Mountain OHV Trail System, Pisgah NF
offroad.distance: 34 mi of designated trails
offroad.season: Closed 1 January to the first weekend in April, along with Curtis Creek Campground, on the Grandfather Ranger District seasonal closure list (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/northcarolina/about-area/faqs/seasonal-closures)
offroad.note: This is a ticketed OHV trail system, not a forest-road drive — passes go through Recreation.gov. Before counting on it: the Forest Service page defines the ATV class here as under 60 inches wide and does not state anywhere that full-size 4WD trucks may use the system. The commonly repeated claim that Jeeps and 4WDs are limited to Trail 8 and part of Trail 1 is not on any Forest Service page that could be opened, so it is unverified. Call the Grandfather Ranger District before driving out.

offroad.name: Pisgah NF gravel roads around Edgemont and Mortimer
offroad.season: Mortimer Campground open 31 March to 31 October; the Grandfather Ranger District closure list gates the Mortimer area 1 November to the first weekend in April
offroad.note: The Forest Service confirms the campground and its position in the Wilson Creek Wild & Scenic corridor south of Grandfather Mountain, but publishes no road numbers, mileage or surface for the Edgemont loop. Neither Roseboro Road (FSR 981) nor Edgemont-Pinola Road (FSR 464) has a Forest Service page, so their condition is unsourced. Note this stop's route and the Wilson Creek entry below share the same road corridor from opposite ends.

offroad.name: Wilson Creek Gorge / Brown Mountain Beach Road, Pisgah NF
offroad.distance: not published on the free listing
offroad.difficulty: not published on the free listing

The listing places it in Adako, Caldwell County, running through the Wilson Creek Gorge past the Mortimer ghost town. The Forest Service's Wilson Creek Wild and Scenic River Area page confirms the area is open all year but says nothing at all about the road.

other_links.note: 'This easy 2.7-mile loop circles the shoreline of 47-acre Price Lake.' Blue Ridge Parkway milepost 297.

other_links.note: Family hike around the Parkway's largest lake; boat rental at the campground.
