boone-nc.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed on the Blue Ridge Parkway trails at Moses Cone, Julian Price and Beacon Heights, and Grandfather Mountain State Park permits them too — though the park itself warns the Grandfather Trail's ladders and cables are not suitable for animals.
boone-nc.dogs_source_quote: Dogs are allowed on trails, but must be on a leash.

scenicDrives_patch.name: NC-105 (Boone toward Foscoe/Grandfather Mountain entrance)
scenicDrives_patch.distance: 19 miles Boone to the Grandfather Mountain entrance
scenicDrives_patch.note: Grandfather Mountain's own directions page: "Take NC 105 South to Linville. Turn left at the stoplight and take US 221 North 2 miles to the entrance of Grandfather Mountain." Worth carrying: the entrance is on US 221, not on NC 105 — NC 105 is the Boone-Foscoe-Linville leg and you turn off it at Linville. No published winter closure for the approach; the page carries no seasonal statement at all, so ice on the 4,000 ft section is an unsourced unknown rather than a documented closure.

scenicDrives_patch.name: US-321 (Boone to Blowing Rock)
scenicDrives_patch.note: High Country Press's scenic-drives roundup lists "Blowing Rock to Boone via US 321 & US 221 — Connecting two of the High Country's most popular towns, this route passes Glen Burney Trail". Listing confirmed from the search result's own title and snippet; the page itself answered HTTP 429 when fetched, so nothing beyond the snippet is recorded. Explore Boone's own five-scenic-drives article does NOT list US-321 or NC-105 — its five are the Blue Ridge Parkway, Doc & Merle Watson Highway (8 mi), Mission Crossing (17 mi), Little Parkway (18 mi), New River Valley Byway (32 mi) and the High Country Road Trip Loop (50 mi), which is the better menu if a designated route is wanted.

Downtown Asheville.entity: Downtown Asheville, listed as the Downtown Asheville Historic District.

Walk out of camp into Bent Creek.entity: Bent Creek and its Lake Powhatan recreation area south of Asheville — the campground the stop uses. Lake Powhatan and Bent Creek Experimental Forest have no articles; the Bent Creek article documents both.

Craggy Gardens and Craggy Pinnacle.entity: Craggy Gardens and the Craggy Pinnacle overlook trail on the Parkway. Neither has a standalone article; the Great Craggy Mountains article documents both by name with the milepost.

Pisgah Ranger District waterfalls on US.entity: The waterfalls along US 276 in the Pisgah Ranger District — Looking Glass Falls being the best known. The ranger district has no article; the forest article has a Waterfalls section and the US 276 article covers the Brevard–Waynesville run through Pisgah.

Downtown Asheville and the Grove Park gi.entity: Downtown Asheville and the Omni Grove Park Inn, whose article documents the National Gingerbread House Competition held there each November–December.

links.label: Wikipedia — The Omni Grove Park Inn

offroad.name: Bent Creek gravel road network, from camp
offroad.note: Worth checking before planning a drive here. The Forest Service research station — this is an experimental forest, roughly 6,000 acres, the oldest federal one east of the Mississippi — permits hiking, biking and horseback riding on designated trails, and describes the gravel roads themselves as open to bicycles, horses and hikers. It nowhere says the road network is open to private motor vehicles, and it asks that research study sites not be disturbed. Treat this as a bike-and-walk network from camp unless the Pisgah Ranger District says otherwise.

offroad.name: Curtis Creek Road (FR 482), Old Fort
offroad.season: Closed 1 January to the first weekend in April (Grandfather Ranger District), together with Curtis Creek Campground
offroad.note: The Forest Service closure list writes this road as FR 428, not FR 482 as the card has it. One of the two numbers is wrong and it is worth settling with the Grandfather Ranger District rather than discovering it at a junction. No Forest Service page publishes the road's length or surface. Separately, this whole district was closed after Hurricane Helene and has been reopening in stages, so confirm current status close to the date.

offroad.name: FR 475 past the Davidson River fish hatchery toward Gloucester Gap
offroad.note: The forest's live Helene status page is the right authority here, but FS 475 is not named on it — only Yellow Gap Road is. Forest Service news coverage that could not be opened directly reports FS 475 open from US 276 to Cove Creek Group Campground and closed from there to the Daniel Ridge trailhead for a bridge replacement; that is not recorded as fact. This road is the one that reaches Gloucester Gap at the FS 471 junction, so a closed middle section breaks the through route. Call the Pisgah Ranger District.

offroad.name: Yellow Gap Road (FR 1206), Pisgah Ranger District
offroad.note: Currently not a through route. The Forest Service Helene status page has FR 1206 open from US 276 near the Cradle of Forestry as far as Wolf Ford Horse Camp, and closed from Wolf Ford Horse Camp to North Mills River Campground — so it is an out-and-back from the 276 end, not the Brevard-to-Mills River link. No length is published by the Forest Service.

asheville-nc-v3.dogs: All four are dog-legal on a leash — Triple Falls and Hooker Falls under the NC Forest Service in DuPont, Bearwallow under Conserving Carolina, and Mount Pisgah under the Blue Ridge Parkway.
asheville-nc-v3.dogs_source_quote: Your dog may be friendly, but other dogs may not be. Protect your dog by keeping it on a leash.

Deep Creek trails.entity: The Deep Creek area of Great Smoky Mountains National Park. Deep Creek has no article of its own; the park article names it as one of the park's major valleys and most accessible areas.

links.label: Wikipedia — Great Smoky Mountains National Park

Deep Creek waterfalls, two miles from to.entity: The Deep Creek falls (Tom Branch, Indian Creek, Juney Whank) just outside Bryson City. None have articles; the park article covers the Deep Creek valley and its streams and waterfalls, and names Bryson City as an adjacent town.

links.label: Wikipedia — Great Smoky Mountains National Park

Kuwohi road is gated — walk it instead.entity: Kuwohi, the peak formerly named Clingmans Dome, and its paved summit road off Newfound Gap Road (the article documents the road; the winter gate closure is not in it).

The Road to Nowhere.entity: Lakeview Drive, the unfinished North Shore Road out of Bryson City. The article's first line gives 'Road to Nowhere' as its alternative name. NOTE: the bare title 'Road to Nowhere' resolves to the Talking Heads song — rejected.

bryson-city-nc.authority: National Park Service — Great Smoky Mountains
bryson-city-nc.dogs: PROHIBITED on trails, with exactly two exceptions: the Gatlinburg Trail and the Oconaluftee River Trail. Leash 6 ft on those. None of the Deep Creek trails on this card qualify, so the dog stays at camp or walks the Oconaluftee River Trail, which starts on the Cherokee side. NPS actively discourages bringing pets because most trails are off limits to them.
bryson-city-nc.dogs_exception: Gatlinburg Trail and Oconaluftee River Trail only.
bryson-city-nc.dogs_note: Oconaluftee is the accessible one from this side — the Bryson City stop already names the Oconaluftee Visitor Center in its highlights, so the dog-legal walk is the one you were going to anyway.

offroad.name: Cove Creek Road / Old NC 284 into Cataloochee
offroad.season: The park's seasonal road schedule lists Cataloochee Road as open year round, two-lane gravel, subject to weather closures. Old NC 284 has no fixed dates — the park closes it in severe weather or heavy rain.
offroad.note: NPS describes Cove Creek as a winding gravel road with steep drop-offs and no guardrails, narrow enough that drivers may have to stop or back up to pass. Old NC 284, the back way in from Big Creek, is also winding gravel. Post-Helene the Cataloochee entrance road was open to vehicles only as far as Beech Grove School with the upper section closed — from the park's reopening release, https://www.nps.gov/grsm/learn/news/great-smoky-mountains-national-park-to-reopen-portions-of-cataloochee-on-april-4.htm. Confirm before the drive.

offroad.name: Heintooga Ridge Road / Heintooga Round Bottom Road
offroad.season: Heintooga Ridge Road 15 May – 31 Oct. Heintooga Round Bottom Road: opening date TBD, as is Straight Fork Road, both still recovering from Hurricane Helene.
offroad.note: Two different roads under one name and only the first half is confirmed. Heintooga Ridge Road is paved and two-way, and motorhomes, buses and vans longer than 25 ft are prohibited — the towed pickup is fine. The Round Bottom (Balsam Mountain) half, the one-way gravel descent toward Cherokee that makes this a through route rather than a dead end, had no published opening date when checked. Do not plan the loop until the park posts a date.

offroad.name: Parson Branch Road
offroad.distance: 8 mi
offroad.season: 1 May – 9 Nov
offroad.note: One-way gravel leaving Cades Cove — you exit at US 129 and cannot come back the way you came. NPS recommends high clearance and restricts large vehicles. It reopened in 2022 after a six-year closure for hazard trees, and the park still closes it for high water, so it is the least dependable of the four here.

offroad.name: Rich Mountain Road
offroad.season: 10 Apr – 9 Nov
offroad.note: One-way out of Cades Cove toward Townsend, with the park's standard restriction on these roads — no motorhomes, buses, or vans longer than 25 ft, and no passenger vehicles towing trailers. The schedule publishes no length. Same one-way trap as Parson Branch: it is a way out of the cove, not a there-and-back.

trails.name: Noland Divide Trail

other_links.label: HikingProject
other_links.note: 'Long and steep, with the greatest net gain in elevation of any trail in the Smokies.'

other_links.label: Smokies 900
other_links.note: Elevation profile and GPX for the full trail.

other_links.label: Explore Bryson City
other_links.note: Trailhead is by the Deep Creek entrance, a short drive from downtown Bryson City.

trails.stats_note: Distance and gain are from third-party trail guides (11.3–11.6 mi one-way, 4,689–4,750 ft), not from AllTrails, which surfaced no figures for the base listing — only for the much longer 18.3 mi and 34.9 mi loops built on top of it. As a one-way ridge climb this is a shuttle or a turnaround, not a loop.

bryson-city-nc.dogs_source_quote: Only two trails permit leashed pets: the Gatlinburg Trail and the Oconaluftee River Trail.

West Rim Loop Trail, straight from camp.entity: The 4.8-mile West Rim Loop Trail at Cloudland Canyon State Park, named and described in the park article.

Waterfalls Trail down into the canyon.entity: The Waterfalls Trail and its 600-step staircase into Cloudland Canyon, named in the park article.

Point Park and the Battle Above the Clou.entity: Point Park on Lookout Mountain, and the 1863 Battle of Lookout Mountain it commemorates. Point Park has no article; the military-park article lists 'Lookout Mountain Battlefield and Point Park' as one of its four areas, and the battle article opens with 'also known as the Battle Above the Clouds'.

links.label: Wikipedia — Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park

Chickamauga Battlefield.entity: Chickamauga Battlefield, listed in the military-park article as one of its four main areas, and the September 1863 battle fought there.

links.label: Wikipedia — Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park

Chattanooga riverfront in the truck.entity: Chattanooga's Tennessee River waterfront — the Riverwalk, Riverpark and Coolidge Park, documented in the city article — and the Walnut Street Bridge pedestrian crossing.

Foster Falls and Fiery Gizzard.entity: Foster Falls and the Fiery Gizzard Trail, both units of South Cumberland State Park. Foster Falls has no article; the state-park article names it as the park's tallest waterfall and a distinct area, and the trail article runs from Tracy City to Foster Falls.

offroad.name: Cherokee National Forest gravel roads above the Ocoee (US 64 corridor)
offroad.note: The authority is the 2024 Ocoee Ranger District Motor Vehicle Use Map (https://www.fs.usda.gov/media/233244) plus a companion sheet of seasonal and special vehicle designations (https://www.fs.usda.gov/media/233242) — both linked from this page and both confirmed to resolve. They are scanned PDFs and could not be read as text here, so the actual gate dates are not transcribed; the seasonal sheet is the one to open on a phone before driving. Paper copies are free at the Forest Service offices in Benton and Cleveland.

offroad.name: Prentice Cooper State Forest road network, above the Tennessee River Gorge
offroad.season: Tower Drive past Pot Point Gate closed 20 Dec – 15 Mar. Tower Drive south of Pot Point Road, plus Elder Point, Long Point and Inman Point, closed to motorized use from late April to early July for turkey nesting.
offroad.note: Two things beyond the gates. Motorized vehicles must stay on designated roads and the forest speed limit is 25 mph. And during managed hunts everything west of SR 27 (Suck Creek Road) is closed to all visitors except licensed hunters — the hunt dates are set by TWRA each year and are the thing most likely to shut this stop's day out, so check the WMA calendar rather than assuming the gate dates cover it.

trails.name: Cloudland Canyon — West Rim Loop Trail

other_links.label: Georgia State Parks — Cloudland Canyon trails
other_links.note: The park describes West Rim as a lollipop-style hike with a three-mile loop in the middle; other guides call the whole thing a five-mile lollipop.

other_links.label: AllTrails — alternate West Rim start
other_links.note: Second listing starting from the small lot off Cloudland Canyon Park Road.

trails.stats_note: Highest-rated trail in the park by a wide margin. 4.9 mi / 718 ft are AllTrails GPS; Georgia State Parks describes the loop portion as three miles, so published and GPS lengths measure different things.

trails.name: Cloudland Canyon — Waterfalls Trail (Cherokee Falls & Hemlock Falls)

alltrails.name: Cherokee Falls and Hemlock Falls Trail

other_links.label: Georgia State Parks — Cloudland Canyon trails
other_links.note: 'The strenuous Waterfalls Trail begins at the Main Trailhead and drops quickly down into the canyon depths to two sizable waterfalls, Cherokee and Hemlock Falls.' Note the park says STRENUOUS where AllTrails says moderate — the difference is roughly 600 stairs back out of the canyon.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Bear Creek Trail variant
other_links.note: Longer route linking the two falls via Bear Creek Trail.

trails.stats_note: Distance/gain are AllTrails GPS (1.9 km / 138 m). Difficulty is the disagreement that matters: AllTrails grades it moderate, Georgia State Parks grades it strenuous. Take the park's grade — the descent is stairs the whole way and has to be reclimbed.

trails.name: Signal Point / Julia Falls Overlook (Cumberland Trail)

alltrails.name: Signal Point Park to Edwards Point

other_links.label: Cumberland Trail Conference
other_links.note: The Signal & Edwards Points section is the southern terminus of the Cumberland Trail. Trail-managing authority for the section.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Signal Point Park area page
other_links.note: Area browse page — candidate for AREA_BROWSE_ALLTRAILS.

trails.stats_note: The 5.4 mi / 875 ft figure is the full Signal Point to Edwards Point out-and-back, which is the only route AllTrails indexes here. Julia Falls Overlook alone is signed at 0.4 mi from Signal Point — a fraction of the listed route, and the shorter walk if the day is short. Julia Falls is a wet-weather waterfall. 1,160 reviews, no star rating surfaced.

trails.name: Tennessee Riverwalk

other_links.label: TrailLink
other_links.note: 13 miles, 1503 Middle St to 4637 Amnicola Hwy, Chattanooga. Rail-trail database entry — the right source for surface and access points.

other_links.label: Visit Chattanooga
other_links.note: Paved and mostly flat; biking, walking and running all normal use.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Riverwalk short path
other_links.note: 255 reviews. A downtown segment of the same route if the full 11 mi is too much.

trails.stats_note: AllTrails traces 11.1 mi point-to-point; TrailLink and the city publish 13 mi and local guides say 16 mi as extensions open. Paved throughout — the strongest cruise candidate on this card. 589 reviews on the AllTrails listing, no star rating surfaced.

trails.name: Sunset Rock (Lookout Mountain, via West Brow Rd spur)

other_links.label: Southeast Tennessee tourism
other_links.note: Sunset Rock is a scenic overlook on Lookout Mountain's western bluff, inside Chickamauga & Chattanooga National Military Park.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Sunset Rock point of interest
other_links.note: Lists the longer approaches, including the climb from near the historic Cravens House, for anyone who wants more than the spur.

trails.stats_note: 0.2 mi / 98 ft is the West Brow Road spur only — effectively a car-park viewpoint walk, which matches our entry. The Cravens House approach is a genuine climb and a different day. Parking on West Brow is about eight spaces. 434 reviews, no star rating surfaced.

chattanooga-tn.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome on all five — the NPS battlefield units at Signal Point and Sunset Rock (Point Park itself is the one closure), Georgia State Parks at Cloudland Canyon, and the City of Chattanooga on the Riverwalk.
chattanooga-tn.dogs_source_quote: Pets are more than welcome in the park. However, please remember to keep them leashed at all times.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Lookout Mountain Scenic Highway / Ochs Highway (up to Point Park)
scenicDrives_patch.note: Tennessee River Valley Geotourism lists this under "Scenic Byways or Routes, Scenic Route" as the Lookout Mountain Scenic Parkway, with directions "take S. Broad Street from downtown Chattanooga to community of St. Elmo, following the signs to Rock City; take Ochs Hwy. up Lookout Mountain". The entry page loaded but rendered only navigation and its category labels, so the route text is recorded from the search result snippet. At the top, Point Park is the NPS unit — admission $10 per adult, ages 16 and over (nps.gov/chch). The NPS page's Directions and Hours & Seasons sections did not populate on fetch, so no winter hours are recorded.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Suck Creek Road / TN-27 along the Tennessee River Gorge
scenicDrives_patch.distance: Prentice Cooper State Forest is 26,945 acres, roughly 10 miles west of Chattanooga
scenicDrives_patch.season: SEASON CONFLICT — the forest's interior roads are closed annually Dec. 20 to March 15; the stop arrives 6 Jan 2029, inside that window.
scenicDrives_patch.note: Tennessee Division of Forestry, the managing authority: "State Highway 27 (Suck Creek Road)" divides Prentice Cooper State Forest. TN-27 itself is a state highway and stays open, but the drive-out-to-the-overlooks part does not — "The following roads are closed annually from Dec. 20 to March 15...Tower Drive past Pot Point Gate, All side roads, Haley Road". Separately, during scheduled big game hunts "the area west of State Highway 27 (Suck Creek Road) is closed to all visitors except licensed hunters", with the area east (Edwards Point) staying open. Turkey-nesting closures through July 14 affect Persimmon Road, all roads past Pot Point Gate on Tower Drive, Inman Point, Long Point and Elder Point Roads. On a 6 Jan arrival this is a highway drive along the gorge plus Edwards Point, not a forest-road day.

Sunset Trail.entity: The park's 10-mile Sunset Trail. No Wikipedia article, and the Hot Springs National Park article never uses the word 'Sunset' — it says only that there are 'numerous hiking trails'. Left bare rather than linked to a park page that does not document it.

Hot Springs Mountain Drive and the Tower.entity: Hot Springs Mountain Tower atop Hot Springs Mountain in the national park, reached by Hot Springs Mountain Drive. The road has no article. IMPORTANT: the title 'Hot Springs Mountain' is a peak in San Diego County, California — rejected; the tower article confirms the Arkansas mountain.

offroad.name: Ouachita National Forest gravel roads, Lake Ouachita north shore
offroad.note: The managing authority for the whole north shore — about 406,000 acres. The page names a Winona Scenic Drive but publishes no mileage, road numbers or surface for it, and no individual road pages exist. One live alert on the page has Henderson Hill Road (FSR 689) partially closed. Which roads are open, and to what vehicle class, lives only on the forest's MVUM.

trails.name: Hot Springs Mountain Trail & Tower

alltrails.name: Hot Spring Mountain Loop via Gulpha Gorge Trail

other_links.label: NPS — Hot Springs Mountain Trail
other_links.note: 'Hot Springs Mountain Trail is an easy stroll around the top of the mountain with several scenic overlooks. Distance (one way): 1.7mi (2.7km)'

other_links.label: NPS — Hot Springs and North Mountain trails overview
other_links.note: How the mountain-top trails connect; easiest to reach from Bathhouse Row.

other_links.label: AllTrails — bigger loop with Goat Rock
other_links.note: 4.6 star rating; the park's most popular running route, adding Goat Rock and the Gulpha Gorge descent.

other_links.label: HikingProject — Hot Springs Mountain Loop
other_links.note: Loop version of the summit walk.

trails.stats_note: Watch the mismatch: our entry is the easy 1.7 mi summit stroll to the observation tower (NPS figure), but the AllTrails listing that sits at the /hot-springs-mountain-trail slug is titled 'Hot Spring Mountain Loop via Gulpha Gorge Trail' and starts with a steep climb out of Gulpha Gorge. AllTrails surfaced no distance, gain or rating for it. Use the NPS length. The Mountain Tower itself is a paid, separately-operated observation tower at the top.

hot-springs-ar-v3.dogs: Hot Springs NP welcomes leashed dogs on all 26 miles of its trails — only the federal buildings on Bathhouse Row are closed to them.
hot-springs-ar-v3.dogs_source_quote: Dogs are welcome on all 26 miles of the Hot Springs National Park trails.

Cedar Falls Trail.entity: The CCC-built Cedar Falls Trail from Mather Lodge into the canyon, named and described in the park article.

Seven Hollows Trail.entity: The Seven Hollows Trail at Petit Jean. No article, and the state-park article never uses the word 'Hollows'. Left bare.

Rock House Cave Trail.entity: Rock House Cave, listed in the park article among Petit Jean's geological and archaeological features.

Bear Cave Trail.entity: Bear Cave, listed in the park article alongside Rock House Cave, the Grotto and Turtle Rocks.

Museum of Automobiles.entity: The Museum of Automobiles at Winrock, adjacent to Petit Jean State Park.

Mount Nebo day trip in the truck.entity: Mount Nebo near Dardanelle and the state park atop it, both covered in the mountain article.

trails.name: Cedar Falls Trail
trails.was: Rock House Cave / Bear Cave Trail — a different trail
trails.note_source: Arkansas' most photographed place: from Mather Lodge steeply down Cedar Creek Canyon to the 95 ft falls. No direct listing url surfaced in search. Name kept; no constructed slug.

other_links.label: Arklahoma Hiker
other_links.note: Logs it as 2 mi out-and-back starting behind Mather Lodge.

trails.stats_note: AllTrails describes it as one of Arkansas' most photographed places: from Mather Lodge it drops steeply into Cedar Creek Canyon to a 95 ft waterfall. Distance/gain are AllTrails GPS; no AllTrails difficulty grade surfaced, and the descent-then-reclimb makes third-party grades range from moderate to strenuous — do not read 'easy' into the absence.

trails.name: Rock House Cave / Bear Cave Trail

other_links.label: AllTrails — Petit Jean Rock House Cave Trail
other_links.note: The other half of our entry: a short, easy trail to Rock House Cave, a large rock shelter, and the Turtle Rocks.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Rock House Cave and Lookout Trail
other_links.note: Longer variant taking in the lookout.

other_links.label: Arklahoma Hiker — Bear Cave Trail
other_links.note: Logs Bear Cave at 0.5 mi. Access from Highway 154.

trails.stats_note: Our entry bundles two separate trails that AllTrails lists apart. The stats given are Bear Cave Trail's (1.2 mi / 127 ft, 0.5–1 hr, 1,110 reviews; no star rating surfaced). Bear Cave is a maze under and between giant sandstone boulders — good with a dog on a lead, awkward with anything wide.

petit-jean-ar.dogs: Arkansas State Parks allow leashed pets throughout the park, so all three trails including Cedar Falls are open to the dog; only public buildings and swimming areas are closed.
petit-jean-ar.dogs_source_quote: Pets or other animals brought into state parks will be appropriately leashed, caged, or otherwise restrained so as to be under the direct physical (not verbal) control of the owner.

Signal Hill summit trail.entity: Signal Hill, the 2,753-ft summit of Mount Magazine and the highest point in Arkansas, named in the mountain article.

Cameron Bluff overlooks.entity: The Cameron Bluff overlooks and campground, named in the state-park article.

Signal Hill Trail.entity: Same Signal Hill summit, the state highpoint.

North Rim Trail.entity: The North Rim Trail at Mount Magazine. No article, and neither the mountain nor the state-park article names it. Left bare.

Mossback Ridge Trail.entity: Mossback Ridge, the mountain's 2,700-ft second summit, named in both the mountain and state-park articles.

Cameron Bluff Overlook Drive.entity: The Cameron Bluff overlook road; the state-park article names Cameron Bluff and documents the CCC-built mountain road that became the Mount Magazine Scenic Byway.

Cove Lake.entity: Cove Lake below the mountain, created by one of the two CCC dams named in the state-park article; the AR 309 article also places it on the Mount Magazine Scenic Byway. NOTE: 'Cove Lake State Park' is in Tennessee — not linked.

trails.name: Signal Hill Trail
trails.was: Bear Hollow Trail — a different trail
trails.note_source: To the highest point in Arkansas at 2,753 ft. No direct listing url surfaced in search. Name kept; no constructed slug.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Mount Magazine State Park
other_links.note: Area browse page — candidate for AREA_BROWSE_ALLTRAILS.

other_links.label: Arklahoma Hiker
other_links.note: Logs a 1.4-mile loop around the north and east of Signal Hill.

trails.stats_note: Signal Hill is the highest point in Arkansas at 2,753 ft. AllTrails 1.8 mi / 252 ft vs Arklahoma Hiker's 1.4 mi loop. The only trail in this block with a complete set of AllTrails figures.

offroad.name: Ozark National Forest gravel forest roads (Cove Lake / Magazine vicinity)
offroad.note: Unlisted. The Mt. Magazine Ranger District is the managing authority and its office page confirms the district, but the Forest Service publishes no page for Cove Lake or for the district's forest-road network, and no off-road database carries a named route here. The district's only current road alert is Morgan Mtn Rd, partially closed for road repair. Plan from the Ozark-St. Francis MVUM.
offroad.distance: The Magazine Mountain Ranger District carries 274.9 miles of MVUM-designated motorized routes — 245.5 miles of roads and 29.4 miles of trails

offroad.name: Ozark National Forest roads on the north flank of Magazine
offroad.note: Unlisted, same as the Cove Lake network above — the district page is the only authority that confirms these roads are Forest Service, and nothing publishes their numbers, surface or gate dates. Note this stop carries two offroad entries for what may be the same road network; worth folding into one with `same_as` if the tags agree.
offroad.distance: 37.3 miles of trail in three loops — Huckleberry Mountain Trail 18.8 mi, Apple Loop 12.2 mi, Bell Springs Loop 6.6 mi
offroad.difficulty: Not published by the Forest Service; Trails Offroad and onX both paywall their grades
offroad.season: The Forest publishes no seasonal closure. A third-party MVUM-derived index lists the Huckleberry Mountain route as seasonal June-March, which would put a 23 Jan 2029 arrival inside the open window — worth confirming against the current MVUM, which prints seasons of use per route.

mount-magazine-ar.dogs: Arkansas State Parks allow leashed pets on park trails, so Signal Hill and Cameron Bluff are both walkable with the dog; the lodge building itself is not.
mount-magazine-ar.dogs_source_quote: Pets or animals other than service animals for individuals with disabilities will not be permitted in public buildings or at swimming beaches or pools at any time.

Boxley Valley elk viewing.entity: Boxley Valley, listed on the NRHP as the Big Buffalo Valley Historic District, and the Buffalo National River elk herd — the park article states the park is home to the state's only elk herd.

links.label: Wikipedia — Big Buffalo Valley Historic District

Boxley Valley elk.entity: Same Boxley Valley cultural landscape and the same elk herd.

links.label: Wikipedia — Big Buffalo Valley Historic District

Lost Valley Trail.entity: Lost Valley, named in the Buffalo National River article as an access point on Arkansas Highway 43 between AR 21 and Ponca. The trail itself has no article.

Steel Creek and the Roark Bluff river be.entity: Steel Creek access on the Ponca section, named in the Buffalo National River article. Roark Bluff, the bluff above it, is not named in any article and has none of its own.

AR-7 Scenic Byway run.entity: Arkansas Highway 7, designated an Arkansas Scenic Byway and National Forest Scenic Byway, running through Jasper.

Erbie and the old homesteads.entity: Erbie, described in the Buffalo National River article as the historic community where the river reaches the Springfield Plateau. It has no article of its own.

trails.name: Whitaker Point Trail (Hawksbill Crag)
trails.was: Buffalo River Trail (Ponca to Steel Creek) — a different trail; Hawksbill Crag is the marquee walk here
trails.note_source: The narrow sandstone overhang 200 ft above the valley — the most photographed spot in the Ozarks.

trails.name: Lost Valley Trail
trails.note_source: Along Clark Creek past natural bridges to Eden Falls and Cobb Cave. Crushed rock to natural surface. No direct listing url surfaced in search. Name kept; no constructed slug.

other_links.label: NPS — Hike the Lost Valley Trail
other_links.note: 'Lost Valley Trail is an easy to moderate hike with occasional benches on the first portion for resting.' Buffalo National River is the managing authority.

other_links.label: Buffalo Outdoor Center
other_links.note: Directions: from Ponca, south on Hwy 43 about 1.5 miles to the paved turnoff on the right. Large car park.

trails.stats_note: 2.4 mi / 249 ft are AllTrails GPS; the difficulty grade is the NPS one. Follows Clark Creek past natural bridges to Eden Falls. Most-reviewed trail in this whole block and the most popular running trail in Arkansas.

trails.name: Buffalo River Trail (Ponca to Steel Creek segment)

other_links.label: Komoot
other_links.note: Moderate 4.1-mile hike with river views and bluffs. A second Komoot trace of the same segment (e2813520458) grades it easy at 4.5 mi.

other_links.label: Buffalo Outdoor Center — Ponca to Steel Creek
other_links.note: Starts at the Ponca access; cross the Ponca low-water bridge to pick up the trail.

other_links.label: Arklahoma Hiker
other_links.note: Puts the Ponca low-water bridge to Steel Creek Campground stretch at 2.2 miles one way, 4 miles out-and-back.

trails.stats_note: No AllTrails listing for the HIKING segment. The AllTrails result that matches this name — 'Buffalo River Paddle Route from Ponca to Steel Creek' — is a float trip, not this walk, and has deliberately not been linked. Lengths disagree by source: 2.2 mi one way (Arklahoma Hiker), 4.1 mi (Komoot), 4.5 mi (Komoot alternate), 4.6 mi (secretfalls) — the segment is walked both one-way and out-and-back. Buffalo National River (NPS) is the managing authority.

offroad.name: AR-43/74 Ponca-Boxley Valley Loop (truck-only)
offroad.note: These are paved state highways, not forest roads — NPS routes visitors to the Jasper/Ponca upper district via Highway 7 or Highway 43 south from Harrison. The park publishes no loop mileage. One genuine warning from the park: GPS is unreliable in this area and has sent numerous visitors the wrong way onto dirt roads, which matters more here than the pavement does.

offroad.name: Cave Mountain / Fallsville forest roads
offroad.note: Unlisted. Neither the National Park Service nor the Forest Service publishes a page naming these roads, and no off-road database carries them as a route. The nearest sourced statement is the park's blanket warning that access roads in this area may be unpaved, in some cases extremely rocky, and may require four-wheel drive and/or high clearance. Fallsville sits on the Ozark NF Big Piney district, so its MVUM is the authority for that half.

offroad.name: Cave Mountain Road (to Hawksbill Crag trailhead)
offroad.note: Unlisted, and this is the weakest-sourced route in this batch. It is a Newton County road running to the Upper Buffalo Wilderness trailhead, so it belongs to neither the park nor the Forest Service, and neither publishes anything on it. Every description of it as rough, rocky and steep, and every 'about four miles to the parking area' figure, is user-generated. The park's general warning about unpaved, extremely rocky access roads needing 4WD or high clearance is the only sourced statement that applies.

offroad.name: Erbie Road
offroad.note: The park has no page for Erbie Road itself; what it does publish is the general rule that access roads here may be unpaved, in some cases extremely rocky, and may require four-wheel drive and/or high clearance. An Erbie campground map PDF exists and resolves at https://www.nps.gov/buff/planyourvisit/upload/Erbie-Campground-Map-Final-Edit-2017.pdf (confirmed 200; contents not readable as text here) and would be the thing to open on a phone.

offroad.name: Kyles Landing entrance road
offroad.note: Same position as Erbie — the only sourced statement is the park's warning that access roads may be unpaved, extremely rocky and may require 4WD and/or high clearance. The widely repeated figures of roughly 2.8 to 3 miles of steep gravel off AR 74 are not on any NPS page that could be opened, so they are not recorded. Both Kyles Landing campground map URLs that surfaced return 404, so there is no PDF to fall back on.

jasper-ponca-ar.dogs: Buffalo National River bans pets on most of its trails — Lost Valley is out — but names the Ponca-to-Steel Creek section of the Buffalo River Trail as one of the few where they are allowed; Hawksbill Crag is Ozark National Forest land, where dogs are permitted under restraint.
jasper-ponca-ar.dogs_source_quote: Pets are not allowed in any government buildings, caves, or on most park trails.

Ozark Folk Center State Park.entity: The Ozark Folk Center, the Arkansas living-history state park at Mountain View.

Mountain View courthouse square.entity: Courthouse Square at Mountain View and the 1922 Stone County Courthouse on it; the city article describes the impromptu folk jam sessions around the square.

Blanchard Springs Recreation Area.entity: Blanchard Springs, whose caverns article covers the site in Ozark–St. Francis National Forest north of Mountain View. The recreation area as such has no separate article.

Sylamore Scenic Byway.entity: The Sylamore Scenic Byway through the Sylamore Ranger District of the Ozark National Forest in Stone County, Arkansas.

White River winter trout.entity: The White River of Arkansas and Missouri; the article's Angling section documents the trout fishery from the Beaver Lake tailwaters down to Guion.

offroad.name: Push Mountain Road & Sylamore Ranger District forest roads
offroad.season: Alert opened 7 April 2025 after the 2025 storms and stands until further notice
offroad.note: Push Mountain Road itself is a state highway, not a forest road, and the Forest Service publishes nothing on it. What this alert does settle is the district's gravel network after the 2025 floods and tornado: Cole Fork Road is still closed, and the Syllamo mountain-bike system including the Jack's Branch and Bad Branch loops and its trailhead is still closed for tornado damage. Barkshed, Gunner Pool and Blanchard Springs campgrounds and day-use area have all reopened.

offroad.name: Sylamore District forest roads to Gunner Pool and Barkshed
offroad.season: Both sites open all year; water at Gunner Pool is seasonal, April to November
offroad.note: The Forest Service gives the road numbers for both. Gunner Pool is FSR 1102, gravel, and the Forest Service calls the approach a steep, winding dirt road not recommended for large recreation vehicles. Barkshed is AR 14 west from Mountain View 17.3 miles, then FSR 1115 (gravel) 2.1 miles, then FSR 1112 1.4 miles — https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/ozark-stfrancis/recreation/barkshed-recreation-area — also not recommended for large trailers or RVs. Both reopened after the 2025 storms.

trails.name: Ozark Folk Center State Park grounds trail

other_links.label: Arkansas State Parks — Ozark Folk Center
other_links.note: Fetched and read: the managing authority's own park page names NO trail and publishes NO trail length for the grounds. The park is open mid-April to mid-November. Guided walks such as the 'Herbs, History & Healing Hike' appear as events, not as a marked trail.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Whitewater Creek Trail
other_links.note: The nearest real listing, 194 reviews: it connects the Ozark Folk Center to the Stone County Amphitheater and City Park in Mountain View. This is the walk that gets you off the grounds and into town — a better use of an afternoon than the grounds paths.

trails.stats_note: Recorded as unlisted, not as a failure: Arkansas State Parks confirms the park but does not publish a named grounds trail, and no trail database indexes one. The grounds paths are craft-village walkways rather than a trail. Nothing invented.

mountain-view-ar.dogs: Dogs are fine on the North Sylamore Creek Trail and on the Ozark Folk Center grounds, but they are barred from Blanchard Springs Caverns and its visitor centre, so the Dripstone tour means leaving the dog in the coach.
mountain-view-ar.dogs_source_quote: Pets are not allowed in the Visitor Center or Caverns: seeing-eye dogs and service dogs are an exception.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Arkansas Scenic 9 (Mountain View to Clinton)
scenicDrives_patch.distance: AR-9 runs 94.41 miles in total; the Clinton-to-Mountain View leg crosses Van Buren and Stone counties
scenicDrives_patch.note: Worth correcting on the card: AR-9 is NOT an Arkansas Scenic Byway. ArDOT's Beautification Section administers the state's scenic byway program and publishes the designated list at ardot.gov/divisions/right-of-way/row_sections/beautification-section/scenic-byways/ (fetch returned HTTP 403; the page was confirmed from its search-result title and a snippet describing the Highway 88 designation of 1998). AR-9 appears on no byway list and holds no independent scenic designation — near Clinton it merely intersects the genuinely designated Arkansas Scenic 7 Byway. What AR-9 does carry: "Pieces of all three routes are designated as Arkansas Heritage Trails for use during the Civil War and the Trail of Tears." The drive itself is real and pretty — it climbs and winds through classic Ozark foothill terrain northeast from Clinton through Shirley into Stone County — it just is not a byway, and the name on the card implies it is.

Beaver Lake day trip.entity: Beaver Lake, the White River reservoir whose dam the article places 9 miles northwest of Eureka Springs.

Walk the historic downtown.entity: The Eureka Springs Historic District, which as listed in 1970 covers the whole city.

The spring circuit.entity: The town's cold-water springs (Basin Spring and the rest) that the resort was built on; documented at length in the city article.

Lake Leatherwood City Park.entity: Lake Leatherwood Park, listed by name under Points of interest in the Eureka Springs article. No article of its own.

Beaver Bridge.entity: The 1949 one-lane suspension bridge at Beaver, Arkansas carrying AR 187 over the White River — the 'Little Golden Gate', the only suspension bridge open to traffic in Arkansas, about 8 miles from Eureka Springs.

Berryville and the Carroll County square.entity: Berryville, the larger of Carroll County's two county seats, and Carroll County itself.

trails.name: Passion Play Trails / Magnetic Mountain
trails.official_length: over 18 miles of trail on a 667-acre property

other_links.label: The Great Passion Play — Trails
other_links.note: The landowner and trail manager: 'We have over 18 miles of world-class mountain biking trails on our 667-acre property for all skill levels.'

other_links.label: The Great Passion Play — Trail descriptions
other_links.note: Splits the network into 'Shared-Use and Mountain-Bike Optimized Trails' — this is the authority statement that hiking is permitted, not just tolerated. Individual trails carry Biblically-inspired names.

other_links.label: Trailforks — Passion Play hiking view
other_links.note: 37 trails mapped. Trailforks warns plainly: 'These trails are built specifically with mountain biking in mind and are therefore graded on mountain biking difficulty' — a blue here is not a hiker's blue.

other_links.label: OZ Trails NWA
other_links.note: Regional trail authority listing; describes over 18 miles of professionally built mountain biking and hiking trails, part of the Marble Flats system.

trails.stats_note: Kept in the trails box rather than reclassified because the landowner explicitly designates shared-use trails, so hiking is legal — but it is a network, not a single trail, and every published difficulty grade on it is a mountain-bike grade. No AllTrails listing exists for it under any wording tried. Blind-corner descents shared with bikes: not a place to walk a dog on a long lead.

trails.name: Historic District Walking Trail

other_links.label: Visit Eureka Springs — Downtown Historic District
other_links.note: The city tourism authority's page for the Downtown Historic District — the district this walk is through. It is a streetscape stroll, not a built path.

other_links.label: Visit Eureka Springs — 8 walking trails
other_links.note: The city's own list of walking loops, e.g. the 1.3 mi Starlite North loop through wooded terrain — the closest thing to a published in-town trail inventory.

other_links.label: EurekaSprings.com — Parks and Trails
other_links.note: Overview of the city's connected park and trail system.

trails.stats_note: No AllTrails listing and no published length from the city for a route by this name. Confirmed only as the Eureka Springs Downtown Historic District walk by the city tourism authority. Third-party sources describe a 3.5-mile 'Historic Loop' past 300+ pre-1910 Victorian homes, but nothing official carries that figure, so it is not recorded as the length.

dogs_unpublished.authority: Eureka Springs Parks and Recreation Commission (City of Eureka Springs), which manages Lake Leatherwood City Park and the city trail network; the Passion Play trails sit on land of the privately owned Great Passion Play
checked: https://www.eurekaparks.com/parks/lake-leatherwood — official Lake Leatherwood park page. Describes the lake, campground and trail mileage. No pet, dog or leash rule anywhere on the page.
https://www.eurekaparks.com — Eureka Springs Parks and Recreation home page. The only dog reference is the Bark Park at Harmon Park, a separate fenced facility; nothing about dogs on trails.

https://lite.duckduckgo.com/lite/?q=Lake+Leatherwood+City+Park+Eureka+Springs+dogs+leash+rules+official+city+park — search returned no eurekaparks.com or City of Eureka Springs page carrying a trail dog rule; every 'dog friendly' claim came from BringFido, DogPack or Zoomies Zone, which are not authorities.
https://lite.duckduckgo.com/lite/?q=eurekaparks.com+Lake+Leatherwood+park+rules+regulations+dogs+leash+trails — same result: no official park-rules page indexed.

Aug 2026 pass — tried the municipal code rather than the park page: https://lite.duckduckgo.com/lite/?q=Eureka+Springs+Arkansas+municipal+code+ordinance+parks+%22dogs%22+leash+Lake+Leatherwood returned a Facebook hiking post, the STATE enabling statute (Ark. Code 14-54-1102, which only grants municipalities the POWER to prevent dogs running at large — it is not itself a Eureka Springs rule), and a dog-beach aggregator. No City of Eureka Springs ordinance text is indexed.
dogs_unpublished.action: Phone Eureka Springs Parks and Recreation / Lake Leatherwood at 479-253-7921 (or leatherwood@eurekaparks.com) and ask two things: are leashed dogs allowed on the Lake Leatherwood trail network, and is there a leash-length rule. Then ask the Great Passion Play separately about the Magnetic Mountain trails, since that is private land under a different owner.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Beaver Lake Scenic Loop (AR-187)
scenicDrives_patch.distance: 16.57 miles, running from AR-23 north of Eureka Springs to US-62 near Eureka Springs, all within Carroll County
scenicDrives_patch.note: The whole point of this loop is the Beaver Bridge — a one-lane 1949 suspension bridge over the White River, the last of its kind still open to vehicles in Arkansas, 554 ft long and 11 ft wide, on the National Register. The published limit is what to check before driving it: the standing restriction is one-lane traffic with a 20,000 lb (10 ton) weight limit, but recent coverage of the bridge's reopening reports "the structure's weight limit was also reduced from 10 tons to five" and further closures planned. Five tons is 10,000 lb — still above a 4x4 pickup, but it is now a number worth confirming with ArDOT rather than assuming, and the bridge has been closed outright for repairs more than once. Cars take turns; only one direction crosses at a time.

scenicDrives_patch.name: US-62 Historic Corridor
scenicDrives_patch.distance: 26 miles Pea Ridge National Military Park to Eureka Springs on US-62
scenicDrives_patch.note: The Eureka Springs CVB's own scenic-drives article, titled "Four Scenic Drives Near Eureka Springs That'll Take Your Breath Away" and describing "a curvaceous road with rolling hills and plenty of dense foliage" with mountain vistas. The page answered HTTP 403 when fetched, so the listing is confirmed from its title and snippet only and the four drives are not enumerated here. The westbound stretch is the historically loaded one: US-62 runs 26 miles from Pea Ridge National Military Park east to Eureka Springs through rolling northwest-Arkansas terrain, past historic White River bridges. No seasonal restriction found for US-62 itself.

Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art.entity: Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art

Crystal Bridges trails and the Razorback.entity: Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art

Coler Mountain Bike Preserve and Slaught.entity: Bentonville's two city mountain-bike systems. Neither has a Wikipedia article, and the Bentonville article names neither — it refers only to 'long mountain bike trails' in general. NOTE: the bare title 'Slaughter Pen' resolves to the Gettysburg Battlefield article — rejected. Left bare.

Downtown Rogers.entity: The Rogers Commercial Historic District, whose article opens 'known informally as Historic Downtown Rogers'.

not_a_trail.problem: A 300-acre mountain-bike preserve, not a trail: 20+ miles across 56 mapped trails, run by the Peel Compton Foundation. Trailforks maps the network at https://www.trailforks.com/region/coler-mountain-bike-preserve/map/ ; the operator's page is https://peelcompton.org/coler-mountain-bike-preserve/ and the city tourism page is https://www.visitbentonville.com/things-to-do/parks-trails-lakes/coler/ . Hiking IS permitted and the operator lists it alongside biking and camping — but AllTrails' own preserve page (https://www.alltrails.com/parks/us/arkansas/coler-mountain-bike-preserve) indexes exactly ONE trail for hiking out of the 56, which is the honest measure of how much of this is a walking destination. Belongs in the biking box or as an activity, not as a hiking trail.

A trail SYSTEM, not a trail — the City of Bentonville calls it 'This 23+ mile mountain bike system' and an IMBA Silver Level Ride Center (https://www.bentonville.ar.gov/1071/Slaughter-Pen-Trails); OZ Trails puts it at 30+ miles (https://www.oztrails.com/trail/slaughter-pen/) and Trailforks maps 150 individual trails (https://www.trailforks.com/region/slaughter-pen-trails/). Multi-use — TripAdvisor lists it as 'Slaughter Pen Hollow Multi-Use Trail System' and Trailforks tags hiking and trail running alongside mountain and e-bike — so walkers are legal, but every trail is built and graded for bikes. The one AllTrails route that covers it, https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/arkansas/slaughter-pen-hollow-trail (All American, Seed Tick, Medusa, Tatamagouche), is described by AllTrails itself as 'This mountain bike-focused route'. Reclassify to biking.

dogs_unpublished.authority: Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art, which owns and manages the 134-acre trail network including the Art Trail. The City of Bentonville does not manage this trail.
checked: https://crystalbridges.org/policies — the museum's own policies page. Covers photography, bags and drones ('drones are not permitted on the museum's trails and grounds') but says nothing about pets, dogs or service animals.
https://crystalbridges.org/visit/nature-trails — the official trails page, which names the Art Trail and seven other trails. No pet, dog or leash rule.
https://crystalbridges.org/visit/ — the main visit page. No mention of dogs, pets, animals or service animals.

https://lite.duckduckgo.com/lite/?q=Crystal+Bridges+Museum+trails+dogs+leashed+pets+policy+crystalbridges.org — the 'leashed pets are welcome on the museum trails' claim traces only to BringFido and similar aggregators, not to the museum.

Aug 2026 pass — no new sources attempted. The three museum pages above are the museum's complete published policy surface and a private landowner has no code, statute or administrative rule to fall back on, which is the route that settled Bismarck. This one only a phone call can close.
dogs_unpublished.action: Phone Crystal Bridges Guest Services on 479-657-2335 and ask whether leashed dogs are allowed on the Art Trail and the wider museum trail network, and whether the rule differs on the paved North Forest / Orchard sections. One call settles the whole stop, since the Art Trail is the only trail on the card.

Yellow Rock Trail.entity: The 3-mile Yellow Rock Trail to the Yellow Rock Bluff overlook, both named in the state-park article.

Devil's Den's CCC landscape.entity: The Civilian Conservation Corps work that built the park from 1933 — cabins, the dam and lake, the overlooks — documented throughout the park article.

Butterfield Hiking Trail.entity: The Butterfield Hiking Trail, named in the park article (it passes the remnants of the drowned town of Anna near Junction Camp) and taking its name from the Butterfield stage route through the Boston Mountains.

Artist Point.entity: The Artist Point roadside overlook on US 71 north of the park. IMPORTANT: the Wikipedia article 'Artist Point' is an overlook in Yellowstone National Park, Wyoming — rejected on identity. The Arkansas viewpoint has no article and the Devil's Den article never names it. Left bare.

offroad.name: Shores Lake / Salt Fork forest roads
offroad.distance: about 10 mi of FSR 1501 under reconstruction
offroad.season: Work began autumn 2025, expected to finish summer 2027; the Forest Service expects the road to stay open to traffic through most of it
offroad.note: FSR 1501 runs from AR 23 on the east to AR 215 on the west near Shores Lake — culverts, reshaping, fresh gravel and overlook parking. Hurricane Road (FSR 1003) work is already complete. This lands squarely in the trip's window, so expect active construction rather than a closure. No Forest Service page names a 'Salt Fork' road, so that half of the entry is unsourced.

offroad.name: White Rock Mountain Road
offroad.distance: FSR 1505 for 8 mi (first 0.5 mi paved, then gravel), then FSR 1003 west for 2.5 mi of gravel, from AR 215 north of Mulberry
offroad.season: Recreation area open all year
offroad.note: Part of FSR 1003 is still out. Per the Forest Service alert last updated 22 May 2026 (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/ozark-stfrancis/alerts/fsr-1003-white-rock-road-closure-partially-lifted), the stretch between Bliss Ridge Road (FSR 1505-1) and Wood's Gap is repaired and open, but the eastern slide near Spirits Creek Bridge remains closed with no estimate of when or if it will be repaired. Approach from the west via Hurricane Road or from the north via Boles Gap Road (FSR 1505-2). Summit is 2,289 ft with CCC stone cabins and lodge.

offroad.name: White Rock Mountain Road (Ozark National Forest)
offroad.distance: FSR 1505 for 8 mi (first 0.5 mi paved, then gravel), then FSR 1003 west for 2.5 mi of gravel, from AR 215 north of Mulberry
offroad.season: Recreation area open all year
offroad.note: Duplicate — this is the same road as the 'White Rock Mountain Road' entry on this stop, listed twice under two names. Worth folding into one with `same_as` rather than shipping both. Same caveat applies: FSR 1003's eastern slide near Spirits Creek Bridge is still closed with no repair estimate, so come in from the west or the north.

trails.name: Butterfield Hiking Trail (Ozark Highlands Trail segment)

other_links.label: Arkansas State Parks — Butterfield Hiking Trail
other_links.note: Managing authority's trail page. Named for the Butterfield Stagecoach, which ran the area 1858–1861.

other_links.label: HikingProject
other_links.note: 'One of the few looped backpacking trails in the state.'

other_links.label: Arklahoma Hiker
other_links.note: 15-mile loop from Devil's Den State Park near West Fork; ten of those miles run through the Ozark National Forest.

other_links.label: Komoot
other_links.note: 'A challenging 15-mile loop that can be completed as an all-day trek or backpacking trip with one or two nights on the trail.'

trails.stats_note: Correction worth carrying: this is NOT an Ozark Highlands Trail segment. It is its own 15-mile loop that begins and ends in Devil's Den State Park, with about 10 miles running through the Ozark National Forest. Length and difficulty are the state park / Arklahoma Hiker figures — AllTrails surfaced no distance or gain in any indexed snippet. It is the most popular trail in Devil's Den State Park at 4.4 from 1,165 reviews, but at 15 miles and 9 hours it is an overnight or a very long day, not an afternoon.

devils-den-ar.dogs: Arkansas State Parks permit leashed pets on park trails, and the Butterfield's national-forest miles are dog-legal too, so all three work with the dog.
devils-den-ar.dogs_source_quote: Pets or other animals brought into state parks will be appropriately leashed, caged, or otherwise restrained so as to be under the direct physical (not verbal) control of the owner.

Talimena Scenic Byway.entity: The Talimena Scenic Drive, the 54-mile National Scenic Byway from Talihina, Oklahoma to Mena, Arkansas.

Talimena National Scenic Byway.entity: The same Talimena Scenic Drive — the article confirms the National Scenic Byway designation.

Queen Wilhelmina Lodge.entity: The 'Castle in the Sky' lodge on Rich Mountain; the state-park article documents the lodge, its 40 guest rooms and its 1898 origin. The lodge has no separate article.

Lovers' Leap Trail.entity: The Lovers' Leap Trail at Queen Wilhelmina State Park. No article, and the park article never mentions it. NOTE: 'Lovers Leap' resolves to a general article on the folklore place-name — rejected. Left bare.

Spring Trail.entity: The Spring Trail at Queen Wilhelmina State Park. No article, and the park article does not name it. Left bare.

offroad.name: Caney Creek Wilderness access roads (Shady Lake / Forest Service network)
offroad.note: Unlisted. The Mena-Oden Ranger District is the managing authority and its office page confirms it, but the Forest Service publishes no page for Shady Lake, for Caney Creek Wilderness access, or for the surrounding road network, and no off-road database lists a named route. The Ouachita MVUM is the only authority on which of these roads are open and to what vehicle class.
offroad.distance: Forest Road 38 runs 6 miles north off AR-246 to the east trailhead

offroad.name: Cossatot Falls access road
offroad.note: Arkansas State Parks is the managing authority and its park page is the right link, but it publishes nothing about the access road — no surface, no mileage, no clearance requirement and no flood closure policy, despite the falls area being the part of the park most likely to be cut off by high water. Everything about the road's condition is currently unsourced; the park visitor centre is the place to settle it.

offroad.name: Ouachita National Forest roads (FR 106, FR 25 and others)
offroad.note: Unlisted. Neither FR 106 nor FR 25 has a Forest Service page on the Mena-Oden district, and no off-road database lists them. Be careful with the numbers: FR 106 is also a road number on the Grandfather district in North Carolina (Dobson Knob), so a search on the bare number returns the wrong state. The Ouachita MVUM is the authority.

offroad.name: Rich Mountain fire-tower spur
offroad.distance: the byway itself is 54 mi
offroad.season: Byway open year round
offroad.note: The Forest Service page covers the byway that runs the spine of Rich Mountain and Winding Stair Mountain, but says nothing about a fire tower or about any spur road off it — so the spur itself is effectively unlisted and only the parent byway is sourced. The byway is paved; whatever spur the card means is not described anywhere the Forest Service publishes.

offroad.name: Wolf Pen Gap OHV Trail System
offroad.note: A permitted OHV trail system on the Mena-Oden district, not a forest-road drive. The Forest Service lists Mena-Oden among its OHV districts but publishes no mileage, fee, permitted vehicle class or season for Wolf Pen Gap specifically. The same page carries a notice dated 1 June 2026 that USDA and the Forest Service are reviewing OHV policy, so the permit rules may not be what they are now by the time of the stop — confirm with the district before buying anything.

trails.name: Ouachita National Recreation Trail (Rich Mountain segment)

other_links.label: USFS — Ouachita National Forest, Rich Mountain
other_links.note: Managing authority. Rich Mountain is the highest point in the Ouachita National Forest at 2,681 ft.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Rich Mountain point of interest
other_links.note: Confirms the mapping: 'This route follows Section 3 of the Ouachita National Recreation Trail, a long-distance route through the rugged mountains of western Arkansas.'

other_links.label: HikingProject — Rich Mountain Trail
other_links.note: The separate Rich Mountain Trail joins the Ouachita Trail at mile 8.5. Trailforks grades this one black-diamond singletrack, 8 miles — a different and harder line than the OT section.

other_links.label: AllTrails — full Ouachita Trail
other_links.note: The whole east-to-west through-route, for context on where Section 3 sits.

trails.stats_note: AllTrails surfaced no distance, gain, difficulty or rating for Section 3 in any indexed snippet — recorded absent. What it does say: no permits are required for the segment, and overnight use is supported by three-sided shelters and established dispersed campsites. Section 3 is the segment that covers Rich Mountain, confirmed by AllTrails' own Rich Mountain point-of-interest page.

trails.name: Janssen Park Trails (Mena)

other_links.label: City of Mena — Janssen Park
other_links.note: The City of Mena owns and manages the park and confirms it exists, but publishes no trail name or length.

other_links.label: Visit Mena — city parks
other_links.note: City tourism listing for the Mena parks, including a walking/biking trail in the city park system.

other_links.label: Wikipedia — Janssen Park
other_links.note: 'A large grassy expanse with occasional mature trees, and features walkways radiating from a central drive, which circles around Mena's oldest building, the c. 1850s Shelton log cabin.'

trails.stats_note: Confirmed to exist by the City of Mena; no trail database lists it and no authority publishes a length. Realistically a municipal park with radiating walkways and a log cabin, not a hiking trail — a twenty-minute leg-stretch with the dog rather than a walk to plan a morning around. AllTrails has only an empty 'explore/parks' stub for Janssen Park, which is not a listing and has not been linked.

mena-ar.dogs: The Ouachita National Forest allows dogs under restraint on its trails and Queen Wilhelmina is an Arkansas state park, so Rich Mountain works both ways; the City of Mena publishes no rule for Janssen Park, so that one is unknown.
mena-ar.dogs_source_quote: On trails, dogs must be under verbal or physical restraint at all times.

offroad.name: Movie Road (Alabama Hills)
offroad.distance: about 6 miles of graded gravel looping off US-395 through the rock formations and back
offroad.difficulty: not published as a grade. Graded dirt, no low range needed in dry conditions; the spurs off it get rougher
offroad.season: NO CONFLICT. Open year-round at about 4,500 ft. The stop arrives 27 Dec 2027 — snow is uncommon this low, but a winter storm turns the graded dirt greasy and the spurs soft, so pick the day.
offroad.note: Renamed from a vague plural to the one named route. BLM restricts vehicle and mountain-bike use to existing roads and trails — no cross-country driving in the Scenic Area, and the boulder fields are exactly where people are tempted. A free permit is needed to camp, not to drive; get it online, at the Eastern Sierra Interagency Visitor Center on US-395, or at the kiosks on Movie Road itself. BLM publishes a downloadable Movie Road brochure identifying the film locations, which is the point of the drive.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Movie Road, Alabama Hills
scenicDrives_patch.note: From the centre of Lone Pine, 2.7 mi west on Whitney Portal Road, then right onto Movie Road where the pavement ends. Graded gravel, about 6 mi through the rock maze past the western film locations before rejoining US-395; sources also describe a fuller 12 mi loop. BLM publishes a downloadable Movie Road brochure identifying the film sites. Congress designated the Alabama Hills a National Scenic Area in March 2019. Camping at designated sites needs the free Alabama Hills permit.
scenicDrives_patch.season: No gate; usable year-round. Arrive 27 Dec 2027 — cold, low sun, which is the good light here. Graded gravel can wash after storms.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: BLM Alabama Hills pages; BLM Alabama Hills National Scenic Area program page

other_links.label: BLM — Alabama Hills National Scenic Area

scenicDrives_patch.name: US-395 north through the Owens Valley
scenicDrives_patch.was_name: US-395 north toward the Owens Valley
scenicDrives_patch.note: The run up the middle of the Owens Valley with the Sierra crest on the left and the Inyo and White Mountains on the right. Caltrans has officially designated US-395 a state scenic highway from Fort Independence to Fort Springs Road in Inyo County, and again from the Inyo–Mono county line to south of Walker — the whole 200 mi is not uniformly designated. No single official byway page exists, so the Bishop visitor bureau's scenic-drives itinerary is the best available link.
scenicDrives_patch.season: Open year-round as a primary route. Arrive 27 Dec 2027 — winter storms bring chain controls and closures on 395; check Caltrans before a long day north.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: Caltrans scenic-highway designation as reported on Wikipedia's US Route 395 in California; bishopvisitor.com

not_a_trail.problem: A graded gravel ROAD, not a trail — and a duplicate of the scenicDrives entry 'Movie Road, Alabama Hills' on this same stop. AllTrails does index it as 'Movie Road Trail' (251 reviews), but LINKS_STRATEGY §3 rejects roads from the trails box and §6 says to deduplicate across boxes before adding. Drop it here; the drive already carries the BLM link.

lone-pine.dogs: BLM Bishop Field Office publishes no pet rule for the Alabama Hills at all — not on the scenic-area page, not on the Mobius Arch trail page, not in the 2022 brochure or the map and guide — so this is unknown, not permitted.

not_a_route.entry: The coach is appropriate for the main Alaska Highway.
not_a_route.problem: A statement about the coach on a paved highway. Not an offroad route by any reading — it belongs in the leg notes, if anywhere.

dawson-creek.dogs: On leash in every City of Dawson Creek park (Animal Responsibility Bylaw 4420 — Barbaree Park is the only off-leash area), which covers Chamberlain Nature Park and Leoppky Park; Radar Lake, the Rim Rocks wind-park paths and McQueen Slough are all outside the city and none of their managers publishes a dog rule.
dawson-creek.dogs_source_quote: No owner will permit the owner's animal to be at large in the City.

4x4 explore O'Brien Creek Road.entity: The 4x4 spur out of Chitina toward the Copper River. No article; the Chitina, Alaska article's full text never mentions O'Brien Creek Road, so there is no parent that documents it.

offroad.name: McCarthy Road
offroad.was_name: Drive the McCarthy Road to McCarthy & Kennecott (in the towed 4x4, not the motorhome)
offroad.distance: 59.4 miles one way, Chitina State Wayside to the McCarthy footbridge over the Kennicott River
offroad.difficulty: not graded by NPS. Usually driveable in 2WD, but soft shoulders, limited visibility and poor surface mean it is a slow, attentive drive rather than an easy one
offroad.season: Best late June through early September, when the road is clear of ice and snow. The stop arrives 15 Aug 2027 — squarely inside the good window, no conflict.
offroad.note: Pack-dirt and gravel on an old railbed. The state has spent heavily on it in recent years and it is well maintained in summer, but potholes and washboard hold you to 35 mph or below. NPS suggests two hours; allow three each way, and remember there is no vehicle bridge at the far end — you park at the Kennicott River and walk the footbridge into McCarthy. This is the entry the box was really about; the rig advice in the old name is now settled policy and has moved to the note.

offroad.name: O'Brien Creek Road
offroad.distance: about 3 miles from Chitina to the O'Brien Creek parking area — and that is where driveable road ends
offroad.difficulty: not a technical route. The short spur is ordinary rough gravel
offroad.season: The road is there year-round, but its whole character depends on the Copper River personal-use dipnet fishery, which runs periodically between about 7 June and 30 September. The stop arrives 15 Aug 2027, inside that window — expect the parking area busy with dipnetters and charter operators.
offroad.note: Worth correcting an expectation: this is not a 4x4 route, it is a three-mile spur. Beyond O'Brien Creek the old roadbed through Wood Canyon is extremely rough and undriveable — the bridge over the creek takes ATVs only, and the trail past it is an ATV route and a dangerous one. The DOT road project beyond O'Brien Creek has stalled. Also worth knowing before going: the local tribe has petitioned to close the road, which overlies a burial ground, so treat the area as sensitive.

offroad.name: O'Brien Creek Road (4x4)
offroad.distance: About 2.8 miles from Chitina to the parking area on the gravel fan at the Copper River
offroad.difficulty: AWD or high-clearance recommended for the full length; "The final descent to the creek is harrowing and very steep"
offroad.season: Accessible year-round but busiest during dipnetting season, June through early August. The stop arrives 15 Aug 2027, just after the crowd.
offroad.note: One-lane road hugging a cliff down to where O'Brien Creek meets the Copper River. The line that matters: it "is no longer maintained by the state" and may have landslides and stray boulders. Drivers in ordinary cars are told to park in a turnaround after Mile 2 and walk the rest — in the truck that is not the constraint, but the unmaintained status and the rockfall are. The Chitina Dipnetters Association pages (chitinadipnetters.com/access-issues.html, dipnetter.com) carry the most current road reports but both refused connection from this sandbox, so nothing from them is recorded.

not_a_route.problem: Duplicate — the same road is listed twice in this box, once as a verb phrase and once as 'O'Brien Creek Road (4x4)'. Folded into a single entry.

not_a_route.entry: Stop at the Wrangell-St. Elias NPS ranger station in Chitina
not_a_route.problem: A building, and a good idea, but not a route. Belongs in activities or points of interest. It is also where you would ask about McCarthy Road conditions, so it is worth keeping somewhere on the card.

Paton Center for Hummingbirds.entity: Tucson Audubon's hummingbird site in Patagonia. No article, and Tucson Audubon Society has no article to serve as a parent.

offroad.name: Sage Creek Rim Road
offroad.difficulty: NPS: "a dirt/gravel road" that "can be rough during or after storms"
offroad.season: NPS: "may be temporarily closed during or after heavy rain or snow" and "may be closed in the winter due to weather conditions"
offroad.note: NPS allows 1–2 hours to drive it and publishes no mileage. It connects SD 44 near Scenic with the Badlands Loop Road (SD 240) north of Pinnacles Overlook, so it can be run as a leg rather than an out-and-back. Along it: Hay Butte and Badlands Wilderness overlooks, Roberts Prairie Dog Town, Sage Creek Basin and Sage Creek Campground. Road status by phone: 605-433-5361.

offroad.difficulty: NPS: "a dirt/gravel road" that "can be rough during or after storms"
offroad.season: NPS: "may be temporarily closed during or after heavy rain or snow" and "may be closed in the winter due to weather conditions"
offroad.note: Same road as the entry above — one route, listed twice in this box. NPS confirms the SD 590 designation and gives no mileage. Phone 605-433-5361 for status.

other_links.note: Five miles one way, relatively level.

badlands-sd.dogs: No dog walks any trail here — Badlands NP bars pets from every hiking trail, the nature trails and all backcountry; they are confined to roads, parking areas, campgrounds and picnic areas.
badlands-sd.dogs_source_quote: Pets are prohibited from hiking trails, public buildings (i.e. visitor centers), and backcountry areas, including the Badlands Wilderness Area, and areas with prairie dog colonies.

Badlands Loop Road.entity: The park's main scenic road, which is South Dakota Highway 240 — its article opens by noting it is 'also signed as the Badlands Loop'.

Notch Trail / Door Trail.entity: Two short trails off the Door/Window parking area. Neither has an article; the Badlands National Park article lists both by name among its established hiking trails.

Badlands Loop Road (SD-240) end to end i.entity: Same road, named with its route number.

Notch Trail.entity: The ladder-and-ledge trail to the Notch. No article of its own; named in the Badlands National Park article's trail list.

Door and Window trails.entity: Two short boardwalk trails at the Door/Window area. Neither has an article; the Badlands National Park article names Door Trail and Window Trail.

Castle Trail and Medicine Root Loop.entity: The park's two longest maintained trails. Neither has an article and neither is named anywhere in the Badlands National Park article's text. No link.

Sage Creek Rim Road wildlife run.entity: The gravel rim road along the Badlands Wilderness on the park's west side. It has no article, and the Badlands National Park article mentions only Sage Creek Campground, not the road. No link.

Fossil Exhibit Trail and Wall Drug.entity: Two things. Wall Drug, the roadside store in Wall, has its own article. The Fossil Exhibit Trail does not, and the Badlands National Park article does not name it, so only Wall Drug is linked.

_dogs_verdict: Per stop: 'allowed' | 'prohibited' | 'partial' | absent. Absent means NOT RESEARCHED and renders no icon at all — a missing dog rule must never look like a green light. 'partial' means the authority names some trails and not others, so the verdict lives on the trail, not the stop.
_activities: Per-stop overrides for the highlights list. Each entry maps an activity's name to a verified entity: its real Wikipedia article, its direct AllTrails listing where it IS a trail, and the official page. Activities with an entry render real links and pills; activities without one keep the generic name-derived search links, which is the honest fallback until they are researched. `drop: true` removes a duplicate restatement of another activity.
_url_provenance: EVERY url here must be COPIED from a search result that returned it. Never construct a slug from a trail's name — alltrails slugs are unpredictable (--2, --3 suffixes, reworded titles) and a fabricated one looks exactly like a real one until it 404s in front of you at a trailhead. This rule exists because four urls were built from names in this file; three happened to be right and one was not, which is luck, not verification.
_auto: Entries marked auto:true were resolved by resolve_highlights.py — the headline reduced to candidate entity names and checked against Wikipedia's real article index. Exact hits only; a fuzzy match is treated as no match. Hand-written entries are richer and are never overwritten.
_search_note: Searching with allowed_domains=alltrails.com returns FEWER alltrails results than an open web search does. Warner Point, Horse Gulch and Piedra River were all recorded as 'no listing found' from a restricted search and all three have listings — found by searching the open web instead. Search open, then take the alltrails url from the results.
_verification_incident: 32 Wikipedia links were written from a batch verifier that reported non-existent articles as valid. MediaWiki numbers every missing title -1, -2, -3...; the script tested only for '-1', so all but the first missing title in each 40-title chunk passed. The identical bug had already been found and fixed in resolve_highlights.py and was never ported to wiki_batch.py — one fix, two copies. Both now test the `missing` key, and wiki_batch.py also rejects disambiguation pages. Controls proved it: 'Qqxzptl Museum of Nonexistence' passed as valid before the fix. | Third residue, found by sweeping the BUILT page rather than the db: six wikipedia links were live on the page. Four titles did not exist (Alberta Falls, Canyon Road (Santa Fe), Fremont Lake (Wyoming), Green River Lakes) and two were DISAMBIGUATION pages (Salmon River, Sprague Lake) — a class the earlier sweeps did not test for at all. Three had a correct target confirmed by coordinates; three had none and were dropped. Sweep the built page, not the db: the db still holds stripped urls by design.
_dead_links: URLs proven NOT to exist. build_links.py strips any of these from a highlight's links on every run, so a bad link cannot survive in the built page just because it was written there once. Removing an entry from this db is not enough — the page is merged into, not rebuilt.
_offroad: Offroad routes researched per stop. Every url was copied from a search result and re-verified to resolve before merging. rig is truck everywhere by standing decision. `not_a_route` records entries that were never routes: rig constraints filed as list items, road-status links, non-motorised areas, and duplicates of the scenic-drives box.
_dogs_unpublished: Stops carrying `dogs_unpublished` were researched and the managing authority publishes NO dog rule at all. They deliberately have no dogs_verdict: a 'partial' badge with every trail null renders as a green light on the card, which is the one thing this field exists to prevent. The record names every page already checked so a later pass does not re-spend on them, and names the phone call that would actually settle it.
